body:
### Bug type

Client crash (OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe hard crash, intermittent)

### Summary

The Windows tray/Hub client (2026.11.1) hard-crashes intermittently during normal use. On the same machine the session also exhibits the tray menu rendering completely empty after extended uptime (#1567) and occasional full UI freezes that require killing the process via Task Manager.

Three crash dumps were captured within 5 days. All three carry the same stowed-exception code **0xC000027B** (stowed C++/WinRT exception), with the faulting module varying between `CoreMessagingXP.dll` and `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll`:

| # | local time (UTC+8) | exception | faulting module | module version | offset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-11-05 15:42:39 | 0xC000027B | Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll | 3.3.0.0 | +0x3A9DBD |
| 2 | 2026-11-05 17:01:10 | 0xC000027B | CoreMessagingXP.dll | 12.6.4.0 | +0x97976 |
| 3 | 2026-11-10 10:36:23 | 0xC000027B | CoreMessagingXP.dll | 12.6.4.0 | +0xADF5E |

### Steps to reproduce

No deterministic sequence is known - the crashes happen at seemingly random points during normal tray/native-chat usage (two crashes within ~2 hours on one day, then one five days later). Common conditions across all three dumps:

1. Launch OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe (portable install) and connect to the local Gateway.
2. Use the app normally over an extended session (tray menu open/close, native chat).
3. The app hard-crashes; the process terminates and a dump is written to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe.<pid>.dmp`.

Not reproducible on demand. Related observation on the same session: #1567 (tray menu renders empty after ~90+ min uptime) and intermittent hard freezes (window unresponsive, kill via Task Manager) precede some of the crashes.

### Root cause

Not established in this report. Measured facts from parsing the minidumps (module list + exception stream):

- All three crashes surface as stowed WinRT exception `0xC000027B` propagated through the XAML/composition stack (`Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll` 3.3.0.0, `CoreMessagingXP.dll` 12.6.4.0, self-contained WindowsAppRuntime 2.6.0.0 in the app-local install dir).
- Faulting sites vary (2 in CoreMessagingXP.dll, 1 in Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll) while the exception signature is identical, which is consistent with the stowed-exception family already tracked here (#2069 on chat send, #1947 LayoutCycleException, #1270 crash-loops under event throughput) and with the popup/GDI resource accumulation documented in #1567.

### Expected behavior

The client should not hard-crash during idle/normal use. Stowed exceptions in the XAML/composition stack should be caught and logged (at least once, with context) instead of terminating the process.

### Environment

- Windows client: OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe 2026.11.1.0 (portable install, self-contained deployment)
- UI stack: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll 3.3.0.0, Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime.dll 2.6.0.0, CoreMessagingXP.dll 12.6.4.0, Reactor.dll
- OS: Windows 11 build 10.0.26300 (x64), 16 CPUs
- Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), local loopback
- Crash dumps: 3 full dumps (~22 MB each) preserved locally; happy to share or run follow-up extraction (stack walk, stowed exception payload) on request

body:
## Problem

Native Gateway onboarding in OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI can fail at "Finishing setup" when the health RPC exceeds its default 10-second deadline. The app then stops the Gateway and reports that setup could not finish.

Original public report by @Steklorez, with reproduction and logs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196251

## Reported environment and behavior

- Windows 11 x64, MSIX / WinGet, Gateway 2026.11.1.
- Install a local native Gateway, choose Ollama, then "Use this model".
- `openclaw.exe gateway health --json` returns `gateway_transport_error`, `kind: timeout`, `timeoutMs: 10000`; the command takes 14130 ms including CLI startup.
- The app next invokes `clawctl gateway-service stop` and fails setup.

The command duration does **not** establish that the Gateway becomes ready at 14 seconds. Neither a native reproduction nor a successful longer-deadline run has been verified by this routing investigation.

## Current source evidence

`src/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.UI/NativeGatewaySetupHost.cs`, `VerifyHealthAsync`, invokes `gateway health --json` without an explicit RPC timeout. Its outer `CliCommandTimeout` is a separate process budget. Core already exposes `--timeout`; increasing the global CLI RPC default would affect unrelated callers.

Please diagnose the startup readiness deadline at this setup owner, preserving cancellation and visible failure/retry recovery. Acceptance should exercise native setup with the packaged Gateway through actual readiness and the final setup result, not only assert the command arguments.

This is an owner-routing issue, not a claimed fix. The original reporter does not need to resubmit their logs.

body:
## Summary

When auto-repair restarts a setup-managed local WSL gateway, it force-terminates the distro first. That also kills the keepalive (`wsl.exe -d <distro> -- sleep infinity`). The keepalive is re-armed only when the restart succeeds. If the restart fails or is aborted after the terminate, the distro is left with no keepalive until something else calls `TryEnsureAsync`. In my case that took about 6 hours.

## Version

- OpenClaw Windows companion 2026.11.1 (`04f413d26531`)
- Setup-managed local gateway in the WSL distro `OpenClawGateway`, running OpenClaw 2026.10.6

## Code path (v2026.11.1)

1. [`WslGatewayController.cs:130`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.11.1/src/OpenClaw.Connection/WslGatewayController.cs#L130): `TerminateDistroAsync`, i.e. `wsl.exe --terminate <distro>`. This kills every `wsl.exe` session of the distro, the keepalive included.
2. [`ManagedLocalGatewayRepairCoordinator.cs:403-417`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.11.1/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/ManagedLocalGatewayRepairCoordinator.cs#L403-L417): when the restart throws, returns `!restart.Success`, or hits `GetRestartAbortResult`, the method returns `RestartFailed` or an abort result.
3. [`ManagedLocalGatewayRepairCoordinator.cs:419-421`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.11.1/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/ManagedLocalGatewayRepairCoordinator.cs#L419-L421): `_reArmKeepAliveAsync` is reached only on success, so the early returns above skip it.

## Evidence (tray log, local time UTC-3)

```
[2026-11-08 20:53:08.412] [INFO] Running OpenClaw gateway restart in WSL distro 'OpenClawGateway'.
[2026-11-08 20:53:09.945] [INFO] Force-terminating WSL distro 'OpenClawGateway' before restart (in-place restart failed).
[2026-11-08 20:53:09.946] [INFO] [WSL] wsl.exe --terminate OpenClawGateway
[2026-11-08 20:53:10.035] [INFO] Running OpenClaw gateway restart in WSL distro 'OpenClawGateway'.
...
[2026-11-08 21:06:53.411] [INFO] Running OpenClaw gateway restart in WSL distro 'OpenClawGateway'.
[2026-11-08 21:06:55.202] [INFO] Force-terminating WSL distro 'OpenClawGateway' before restart (in-place restart failed).
[2026-11-08 21:06:55.202] [INFO] [WSL] wsl.exe --terminate OpenClawGateway
```

- The previous `[WslKeepAlive] Started keepalive` line is from 2026-11-07 17:25.
- After these terminates, the next `[WslKeepAlive]` line is at 2026-11-09 03:18:20.
- The log does not record the outcome of either repair, so I can't tell whether it was `RestartFailed` or an abort. Because no re-arm happened, it was not a success.
- The gateway was slow and failing at startup at the time, which makes a failed restart likely.

## Impact

- With no keepalive, the distro idles out and gets started again by later `wsl.exe` calls.
- Each of those unclean stops counts toward the gateway's restart-loop breaker, which suppresses channel auto-start.
- Each stop also leaves behind a plugin capture, and those captures filled the host drive (see openclaw/openclaw#161839).
- The gateway also had startup failures of its own, so this was not the only source of unclean restarts. It did keep the distro from recovering on its own.

## Expected

After any repair attempt that has already issued `--terminate`, the keepalive should be re-armed, for example from a `finally` once the terminate has run, whether the restart succeeds or not. A more robust alternative would be for the keepalive service to watch its own process and respawn it whenever it exits.

## Workaround

A per-user scheduled task at logon that runs `wsl.exe -d OpenClawGateway -- sleep infinity` in a loop and relaunches it when it exits.

body:
### Summary

Since Gateway 2026.11.1, session lifecycle patches (archived, snoozedUntil, sidebarRoot) require `expectedSessionId` for optimistic concurrency. The Companion never sends it - `SessionPatch` has no such field - so **every Archive/Unarchive action from the Workspace sidebar context menu is rejected**:

```
expectedSessionId required for session lifecycle patch: agent:default:dashboard:<uuid>
```

### Repro

1. Connect Windows Hub to a Gateway running OpenClaw 2026.11.1.
2. In the Workspace chat sidebar, right-click any conversation -> Archive (reproduces even on brand-new, never-archived conversations).
3. The action fails with the error toast above; the row stays in the active list (correctly - the archive never applied).

### Root cause (source, main branch)

- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Windows/WorkspaceSessionMenuController.cs` - `ToggleArchiveAsync`:
  ```csharp
  await operation.PatchAsync(session.Key, new SessionPatch { Archived = !session.IsArchived });
  ```
- `src/OpenClaw.Shared/GatewayProtocolModels.cs` - `SessionPatch` / `ToPayload`: the class already has `ExpectedMarkedUnreadAt`, but there is **no `expectedSessionId` field**; `ToPayload` emits only `key` + the patched fields. Grepping `expectedSessionId` across `src/` returns zero hits.
- Gateway side (2026.11.1) rejects any patch carrying `archived` / `snoozedUntil` / `sidebarRoot` without `expectedSessionId` in lifecycle admission:
  `expectedSessionId required for session lifecycle patch: <storeKey>`

The web Control UI bundled with the same gateway sends `expectedSessionId` with every lifecycle patch (per-target for `sessions.patchMany`) and archives fine, so this is a Companion protocol gap.

### Expected behavior

Include `expectedSessionId` (the session SessionInfo.SessionId) in `sessions.patch` payloads whenever `archived`, `snoozedUntil`, or `sidebarRoot` is set - matching the web client.

The same omission exists in `DeleteSessionConfirmedAsync` (only `key` + `deleteTranscript`); worth aligning `sessions.delete` / `sessions.reset` flows with the web client expectedSessionId usage as well.

### Environment

- Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)
- Client: Windows Hub - reproduces on current releases; `main` still lacks the field

Switching conversations should land on the newest messages without freezing, while still not interrupting someone who is reading.

The freeze is a WinUI bug, not our timing. `ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView` runs a synchronous layout; if that layout recycles the target row, `ItemsView::GetElementIndex` keeps asking for the same container and never exits. Upstream fixed this in [microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml#12320](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/pull/12320) (commit `54d01b8`), but no supported Windows App SDK release contains it: the supported 2.6.5 ships identical code to our 2.6.4, so a package bump does not help.

Chat tail navigation therefore no longer calls that API. It realizes the newest row through the timeline's `ItemsRepeater` outside layout, waits for native layout to settle, reacquires the live container once with full revalidation, and calls `StartBringIntoView` on that container. Preparation gets one bounded recovery. If preparation or reacquisition still fails during the initial landing, the existing bounded landing check retries the newest row instead of leaving the conversation at the top. A landing is confirmed only when the native list is showing the current rows, because an empty or stale list also reads as "at the bottom". User input, conversation replacement, unload and disposal cancel pending work. The earlier far-edge anchoring and in-flight deferral remain, along with the reviewed input-cancellation correction. The architecture ledger records the workaround and when to retire it (once a supported WinUI release contains the upstream fix).

The current head adds three mounted native regressions. The transient-source recovery test fails with recovery disabled and passes with it restored. The held-missing-source test (`TailNavigation_InitialLandingRetriesWhenSourceStaysMissingThroughPreparation`) timed out with the view stranded at the top (offset 0 of 25208) when the failure path was temporarily reverted to the old give-up behavior, and passes with the retry. body:
Lane 4 of 5 for #2071. _Filed by a Copilot agent._

**Problem:**
- `GatewayConnectionManager.ScheduleOperatorReconnectAsync` (~3351) checks `IsCurrentLifecycle(request.Attempt)` without holding `_transitionSemaphore`. It then calls `ReconnectIfCurrentAsync`, which checks only the user-disconnect intent and the active gateway id.
- A plain `DisconnectAsync` does not change either of those. Plain disconnects are used for:
  - the setup connector timeout cleanup (ConnectionManagerOperatorConnector ~111/162)
  - direct-connect rollback (GatewayDirectConnectService ~203)
  - removing the active gateway (ConnectionPage ~2667)
- So a reconnect queued behind one of those disconnects can reconnect the gateway the caller just tore down.

**Fix:**
- Make the scheduled reconnect take the semaphore via `AcquireCurrentAttemptAsync(request.Attempt)`, and reconnect under that lease.
- Use `DisconnectByUserAsync` when removing the active gateway.

**Done when:**
- a deterministic `GatewayConnectionManagerTests` case (hold the semaphore, queue the disconnect, release) shows no reconnect
- the required validation passes

body:
Lane 1 of 5 for #2071. _Filed by a Copilot agent._

**Problem:**
- `WebSocketClientBase.ListenForMessagesAsync` calls `OnDisconnected` only on a Close frame, a premature close, or a keepalive OCE. It skips it in two cases:
  - a client-initiated abort (`AbortCurrentWebSocket`, for example from a bad chat stream), which is filtered by `_clientAbortedGeneration`
  - the oversized-message `CloseAsync(MessageTooBig)` + `break` path
- In both cases it goes straight to `ReconnectWithBackoffAsync`, so `OpenClawGatewayClient.OnDisconnected` never runs. In-flight requests (chat send, etc.) wait for their full timeout instead of failing fast with `GatewayConnectionLostException`, and the handshake snapshot, `MainSessionKey` and advertised methods stay stale until the next connect.
- `OnError` (OpenClawGatewayClient.cs ~415) only drains pending requests.
- `CheckHealthAsync` (~636-664) calls `ReconnectWithBackoffAsync()` with no owner. A `(null, 0)` owner always passes `IsReconnectOwnerLocked`, so after the delay the loop can dispose a socket the manager has just connected.

**Fix:**
- Report the connection loss exactly once per current connection on every listen-loop exit, using one invalidate path shared by `OnError`.
- Pass the current socket and generation as the owner from `CheckHealthAsync`.

**Coordinate with:** #1574, which concerns the same reconnect loop.

**Done when:** a `WebSocketClientBaseTests` regression test shows `OnDisconnected` runs after `AbortCurrentWebSocket` and after an oversized message, and the required validation passes.

Lane 3 of 5 for #2071. _Filed by a Copilot agent._

**Problem:**
- The single-instance mutex is taken early (App.xaml.cs ~600), but the forwarded-activation listener starts only at ~1107. That is after onboarding and after `CheckOrdinaryStartupUpdateAsync`, which awaits `UpdateDialog` with no timeout.

- **Result** in unpackaged release builds with an update available:
  - relaunching does nothing
  - deep links are dropped
  - the global hotkey is dead until the dialog is answered

**Related:** `_globalHotkey` has two writers. Startup (`_globalHotkey = new GlobalHotkeyService()` at ~1112) overwrites a hotkey that a settings save already registered during that wait. That leaves an orphaned registration that disabling the hotkey cannot remove.

**Fix:**
- Start the listener before the update check. Forwarded plans already marshal to the UI thread.
- Register the hotkey through `ApplyGlobalHotkey`, so it has a single writer.

**Done when:**

body:
Lane 2 of 5 for #2071. _Filed by a Copilot agent._

**Problem:**
- `NodeService.StartMcpServer` (~773-839) checks and then sets `_enableMcpServer`/`_mcpServer` with no lock, and its catch sets `_mcpServer = null` unconditionally.
- `StopMcpServerAsync` swaps the fields with no lock.
- `SetMcpEnabled` holds `_clientLock`, and its comment wrongly says the stop is lock-protected.
- `AttachClient` calls `RegisterCapabilities()` (which ends in `StartMcpServer`) after releasing `_clientLock`, on a threadpool thread from the NodeConnector `ClientCreated` event.

**Failure:** saving settings with node mode and MCP both on reconnects the node and calls `SetMcpEnabled` at the same time. That can start two servers, where the losing attempt nulls the winner, or it can lose a disable. Either way an untracked MCP listener, including `system.run`, keeps running and turning MCP off cannot stop it until restart.

**Fix:**
- Add a dedicated MCP lifecycle lock around start and stop.
- Re-check the enabled flag inside the lock.
- In the catch, clear the field only if it still holds this attempt.
- Correct the comment.

**Done when:**
- a regression test covers concurrent start/stop
- the required validation passes
- there is `winnode` MCP proof that enable/disable still works
- a rubber-duck review is done

Closes #1944

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with a screen reader, the chat transcript is announced as one unnamed list, Up and Down do not move between messages, each message is announced as raw markdown with no send time, and repeated tool calls in one activity all announce the same text.

## User Impact

User impact: screen reader users can Tab into the chat history, hear one message at a time with its sender, literal text and the time shown in the window, press Up or Down to walk the transcript, and hear each nested tool call's position and input summary instead of an identical label.

### Bug type

Client crash (Windows Hub native chat)

### Summary

Windows Hub **2026.10.5-alpha.4** crashes (process terminates) almost every time a chat message is sent from the native chat, against a **2026.11.1** gateway. Three crashes plus one hang within ~10 minutes. Same fault signature each time.

Possibly related to #1779 (native chat freezing after send against a newer gateway), but this is a hard crash with a stowed exception in `CoreMessagingXP.dll`, not just a freeze, and on the alpha build.

### Environment

- Windows Hub: `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw_2026.10.502.0_x64` (product version `2026.10.5-alpha.4+Sha.f81edef9a06222e4eea5a93dd21ecfb7e3002c10`), MSIX install
- Windows 11 23H2, build 10.0.22631.6199, x64
- Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20) on macOS, `gateway.bind: lan`, token auth, plain `ws://` over LAN (no SSH tunnel)
- Hub connected as operator only. Node mode is off; the PC's node is a separate `openclaw node` 2026.11.1 Scheduled Task and is unaffected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Hub to a 2026.11.1 gateway over LAN with token auth.
2. Open a session in native chat and send a message.
3. Hub crashes shortly after send (or hangs, then WER reports `MoAppHang`).

### Crash details (Application event log)

Event 1000:
```
Faulting application name: OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe, version: 2026.10.5.0, time stamp: 0x6ac20000
Faulting module name: CoreMessagingXP.dll, version: 10.0.27200.1054, time stamp: 0x1cff1018

Event 1001 (WER), twice with the same bucket:
```

`0xc000027b` is a stowed (WinRT) exception, so the real exception is likely an unhandled error on the UI thread during the send/reply render path. A WER minidump exists locally and I can attach it if that helps.

Depends on #2063 (feat: decide approvals from the Inbox and background toasts), which depends on #2060 (feat: show live Gateway approvals, automation failures and account alerts in the Inbox) and #2057 (feat: web-aligned Inbox for the footer bell and notifications page). This is layer 4 of 4. The branch remains cumulative; the dependency must land first and the stack must be reconciled before the next landing.

## What Problem This Solves

There was no way to silence OpenClaw alerts without also missing approvals, and nothing told you when Windows privacy settings blocked a device that an enabled node capability (camera, microphone, location) needs.

## User Impact

User impact: the Inbox (bell flyout and full Inbox page) has a **Do not disturb** toggle. While it is on, Windows toasts, their sounds and in-app banners stay silent for everything except approvals and device pairing or scope-upgrade requests; the Inbox still collects items and the bell still counts them, and the bell switches to a slashed bell with help text "Do not disturb is on. N waiting". The **System** tab now shows **This PC** alerts (for example "This PC: camera access is off") with **Open Windows privacy settings**, which disappear when the block clears or the capability is turned off. This PC alerts work in the packaged (MSIX/Store) app; unpackaged development builds never show them (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One Do not disturb rule.** `DoNotDisturbPolicy` decides; `ToastService.ShowToast` applies it using the alert kind `AppNotificationPublisher` derives from the existing Inbox classification (so exec-approval Gateway notifications still toast), and `AppNotificationInfoBarPresenter` applies it to banner eligibility without forgetting banners the user closed. Background approval toasts from `ApprovalToastPresenter` are never silenced. The Settings **Send test notification** button stays an explicit user test.
- **Persisted through the settings owner.** `SettingsData.DoNotDisturb` is a field-scoped `ISettingsStore` save; hosts read and toggle it only through `InboxFeed`, which ignores stale change events.
- **No consent prompts.** This PC alerts read `AppCapability.CheckAccess` (no prompt) only for devices an enabled capability needs while node or MCP mode is on: camera for `camera.*`, microphone for speech-to-text and camera clips (they record sound by default), location for `location.get`. ## What Problem This Solves

Pending approvals showed in the Inbox after #2060, but they could only be decided from the chat conversation, and nothing told you about an approval while OpenClaw was in the background.

## User Impact

User impact: Inbox approval rows (bell flyout and full Inbox page) now offer **Allow once**, **Always allow** and **Deny**, limited to the decisions the request offers, matching the web Control UI. When an approval arrives while OpenClaw is in the background, an actionable Windows toast offers **Deny**, **Review**, and **Allow once** only when the toast shows the whole command. Deciding in chat, the Inbox, a toast or another client clears the approval everywhere. Without `operator.approvals`, rows show "You need approval access to approve." and no buttons.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One decision path.** A new App-owned `OperatorApprovalDecisions` is the only owner of operator approval decisions. Inbox rows, toasts and the existing chat banner all go through it. It sends through one kind-aware client RPC (`exec.approval.resolve`, `plugin.approval.resolve`, or `approval.resolve` with kind `system-agent`). The chat banner keeps using the RPC, not the `/approve` slash command, for the same reason as before.
- **Revalidated right before sending.** Every Inbox and toast decision is checked against the live pending approval: same id, not expired, decision offered, an explicit `operator.approvals`/`operator.admin` grant, and observed on the authenticated connection epoch that is still current. The RPC itself refuses a different epoch before transmitting. `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND`/`APPROVAL_ALREADY_RESOLVED` remove the row like a success; a failure after final transport admission keeps an uncertain-outcome row and blocks another decision. One connection-bound complete-list read may retire a missing request, but pending presence does not prove the earlier resolve finished and does not authorize a retry.
- **Same safety rule as the chat banner.** A command that is missing, truncated, oversized or concealing text offers only Deny, and commands are shown through the existing approval display sanitizer. A request that states `allowedDecisions` this client doesn't recognize offers nothing rather than the defaults.
- **Toast activation arguments carry no command text.** Buttons carry only the approval id, the decision and a random one-shot token bound to the client and connection epoch that showed the toast. Stale, forged, replayed or earlier-connection activations decide nothing and open the Inbox. A toast never offers Always allow. Toasts honor **Show notifications**, only appear while no OpenClaw window is in the foreground, skip approvals hydrated on connect, and are withdrawn once the approval is decided, expires or the connection changes.
- **Local exec approvals unchanged.** Node exec approvals for commands this PC runs (`ExecApprovalV2DialogPromptHandler` / `ExecApprovalDialog`) remain their separate in-process flow and do not pass through the Inbox.
- New strings are localized in all six locales; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` gains the decision-owner and toast rows and closes the chat-only resolve path.

<details>
<summary>Notes and follow-ups</summary>

- A blank exec command is now kept as a deny-only Inbox row (the web UI drops it; the native chat banner already shows it deny-only), so the Inbox and chat agree.
- Legacy chat slugs must correlate to a tracked canonical approval. Untracked or stale requests do not bypass the shared decision owner.

body:
Related: #1887

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a console window keeps flashing and taking focus every minute after a full `clean-uninstall.ps1` when Companion's Gateway cleanup task and folder are left behind.

## User Impact

User impact: a clean uninstall now removes the Gateway cleanup task and its files, so nothing keeps running afterwards, and a WSL distro the plan says it will preserve can no longer be unregistered by that task.

This does not fix the Store-build flashing reported in #1887, which needs #1782 to reach the Store. It also does not repair machines that already have an orphaned task until cleanup is run again.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clean-uninstall.ps1` only selected tasks named exactly `OpenClaw Companion`, so `OpenClaw Gateway cleanup - <SID> - <family>` survived, and so did `~\.openclaw-companion`. Removing that folder by hand left a task that could neither run nor unregister itself.

The task is now selected by exact identity (SID, family, root path, principal and action, for both the windowless host and the older PowerShell action) and fails closed on anything else. It deliberately does not depend on the task's files, because orphaned tasks have none. It is removed after native teardown and before package removal: the task reacts to package removal, and leaving it armed through teardown failures would be the worse outcome. Dev families still require `-IncludeDev`.

<details>
<summary>Tradeoffs</summary>

- A worker already running at the moment of removal is not stopped. The window is seconds, and today the task stays armed for the whole run.
- If `Remove-AppxPackage` fails after the task is removed, it stays disarmed until Companion next starts, which re-registers it from `owned.json`. The script already reports partial cleanup.
- I considered having `cleanup.ps1` unregister itself when `owned.json` is missing and dropped it. `DeployAsync` is skipped without a record, so existing installs would never receive it, and it added a race with concurrent registration.
- A sweep for existing orphans at Companion startup is left for maintainers to decide on. It is the only thing that would repair affected machines automatically.

</details>

## Evidence

On an ARM64 machine with this orphaned task, a read-only dry run of this branch selected the real legacy task. Before the task was removed, a window hook recorded 6 of 6 task runs opening a Windows Terminal window that took focus for about 0.35s, with matching PIDs. No console window appeared in the 3 minutes after removal.

body:
## What happens

On Diagnostics, Copy Device ID and Copy Public key read `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\device-key-ed25519.json` and look for `deviceId` and `publicKey`. The paired identity is `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\gateways\<gateway-id>\device-key-ed25519.json`, written with `DeviceId` and `PublicKeyBase64`. A paired user gets the missing-file text instead of that identity.

That gateway file also contains `PrivateKeyBase64`. The copy must not include the private key.

## Where

Checked on [fc777f2f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/fc777f2f855289bb862c14166d9956181eccaebe).

- Wrong file: [DebugPage.xaml.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/fc777f2f855289bb862c14166d9956181eccaebe/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/DebugPage.xaml.cs). `DeviceKeyPath` is under the local data directory. `LoadDeviceIdentity` reads `deviceId` and `publicKey`.
- Right file: [ConnectionStatusWindow.xaml.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/fc777f2f855289bb862c14166d9956181eccaebe/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Windows/ConnectionStatusWindow.xaml.cs) already reads `device-key-ed25519.json` from `GetIdentityDirectory` and uses `DeviceId`.
- Names: [DeviceIdentity.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/fc777f2f855289bb862c14166d9956181eccaebe/src/OpenClaw.Shared/DeviceIdentity.cs) stores `DeviceId`, `PublicKeyBase64`, and `PrivateKeyBase64`.

## Suggested fix

Read the active gateway identity file. Copy `DeviceId` and `PublicKeyBase64` only.

## Environment

Windows 11. .NET 10. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `fc777f2f`.

## Fix

I have a fix on my fork, branch `fix/f060-diagnostics-device-id`, commit `8065eec19130ad8604dcdc50de28e14882322f8f`.

body:
## What happens

A second click cancels only the wait. Whisper and Piper share one download, and that download is started with `CancellationToken.None`, so the body copy keeps reading. Neither loop stops when the bytes pass the pinned model or archive size. The file is hashed only after the stream ends, so a sender that keeps writing fills the disk until the request timeout or the socket closes.

Canceling one waiter while another is still attached must leave the shared download running.

## Where

Checked on [122bda71](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e).

- Shared start: [SingleFlightDownload.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Audio/SingleFlightDownload.cs) calls `startDownload(CancellationToken.None)`.
- Whisper body: [WhisperModelManager.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Audio/WhisperModelManager.cs) reads until the stream ends. The pinned sizes are `ApproximateSizeBytes` (`77_691_713`, `147_951_465`, `487_601_967`).
- Piper body: [PiperVoiceManager.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Audio/PiperVoiceManager.cs) does the same. The catalog had a hash and no archive size.

## Suggested fix

Give the shared download its own token. Cancel that token when the last waiter cancels, and also on the existing 30 minute Whisper and 10 minute Piper limits. Stop the copy when the body grows past the pinned size. Keep a download that still has another waiter.

## Environment

Windows 11. .NET 10. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `122bda71`.

Piper archive sizes were read from the `k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx` release `tts-models` on 2026-11-06. Amy low is 67095344 bytes. LibriTTS high is 131033598 bytes.

## Fix

I have a fix on my fork, branch `fix/f091-download-cap`, commit `0cf973d5c77f6e42a681038bb0bc08189712a0c9`.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f091-download-cap?expand=1

body:
## What happens

The MSIX storage validator reads `success` and `postconditions` from the setup engine JSON. The engine writes `outcome` and `exitCode` instead. `success` is therefore empty, and `postconditions` stays empty. The final exit still returns pass when the evidence files exist and the verdict is Path A or Path B. Nothing has shown that the device token was cleared or that the WSL distro is gone.

## Where

Checked on [122bda71](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e).

- Read: [validate-msix-storage-paths.ps1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/scripts/validate-msix-storage-paths.ps1). `Invoke-CliEngineUninstall` uses `$engineJson.success` and `$engineJson.postconditions`. `Get-FinalExitCode` returns pass when the evidence files exist and the verdict is not blank or Inconclusive.
- Write: [Program.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.SetupEngine/Program.cs) `SerializeJsonOutput` writes `outcome` and `exitCode`.

## Suggested fix

Treat `outcome` `Success` and `exitCode` `0` as the engine success. Do not invent postconditions. Fail the final result for Path A or Path B unless `cross_check_consistent` is true and both `device_token_cleared` and `wsl_distro_absent` were reported.

## Environment

Windows 11. PowerShell 7. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `122bda71`.

body:
## What happens

Turning auto-start off on an unpackaged install deletes the Run value, calls unregister on the logon task, and ignores the result. The method then logs "Auto-start disabled" even when the task is still registered. The settings apply treats that as success, so the saved preference becomes off while Windows still starts Companion at logon.

This is not the installer shortcut in #1956. That issue is the `{userstartup}` link the installer creates. This one is the scheduled task `AutoStartManager` already tries to remove.

Turning auto-start off when the Run value and the task are already absent must still succeed. `schtasks /Delete` fails when the task is not there, so a missing task is not a failure.

## Where

Checked on [122bda71](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e).

- Apply: [AutoStartManager.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/AutoStartManager.cs) `SetUnpackagedAutoStart`. The disable branch calls `WindowsStartupTaskRegistration.Unregister` and does not read the bool.
- Result: [WindowsStartupTaskRegistration.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Shared/WindowsStartupTaskRegistration.cs) `Unregister` returns the `schtasks` exit result.

## Suggested fix

After the disable attempt, read the Run value and query the task again. If either is still present, throw `AutoStartRefusedException` so `ApplyAutoStart` rolls the saved preference back. Do not call delete when the task is already absent.

## Environment

Windows 11. .NET 10. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `122bda71`.

## Fix

I have a fix on my fork, branch `fix/f096-autostart-unregister`, commit `6e610a2f0ec9a2a7f0e3c80b2844744610240cf2`.

## Suggested fix

Remember the agent id, request path, and load token when the get starts. Apply the body only when those still match, and compare the returned path to that request path.

body:
## What happens

Restoring a checkpoint replaces the visible transcript with an empty timeline, then asks for `chat.history`. Every row disappears while that request is in flight. If the request fails, nothing puts the previous rows back.

A message that arrives during the restore must stay. Rows that belonged to the old transcript must not stay once the restored history commits and does not contain them.

## Where

Checked on [122bda71](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e).

- Clear: [ChatConversationState.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ChatConversationState.cs) `BeginHistoryReplacement` assigned `ChatTimelineState.Initial()` and removed the thread metadata, then built the snapshot.
- Publish: [OpenClawChatDataProvider.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/OpenClawChatDataProvider.cs) `ReplaceHistoryAfterCheckpointRestoreAsync` publishes that snapshot before `LoadReplacementAsync`.

## Suggested fix

Keep the current transcript until the replacement history commits. Publish that transcript while the load is in flight. When the load commits, drop ids that were already visible and are absent from the new history, and keep a message that arrived after the restore started. If the load fails, leave the previous transcript.

## Environment

Windows 11. .NET 10. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `122bda71`.

## Fix

I have a fix on my fork, branch `fix/f050-checkpoint-timeline`, commit `79558a2f617245cb2618ccbcafd79883b147bd0c`.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f050-checkpoint-timeline?expand=1

Fork pull request, where I provide the fix: https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw-windows-node/pull/5

body:
## What happens

A Hugging Face model download can resume from a partial file. When the server answers the range request with HTTP 200 instead of 206, the installer treats that as a full restart. It truncates the partial and resets the hash before it checks `Content-Length`. A 200 whose length is not the pinned size already erased the bytes on disk, and then the length check fails.

On this machine a partial whose first bytes were `veri` (118, 101, 114, 105) was an empty file after a 200 that declared 2 bytes.

## Where

Checked on [122bda71](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e).

- Resume: [HuggingFaceModelInstaller.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.SetupEngine/HuggingFaceModelInstaller.cs) `DownloadAndVerifyAttemptAsync`. The non-append branch calls `partial.SetLength(0)` and `hash.GetHashAndReset()` before the `Content-Length` check.

## Suggested fix

Compare `Content-Length` with the pinned size first. Truncate the partial only after a 200 is accepted as a full restart. A declared length that does not match leaves the partial untouched.

## Environment

Windows 11. .NET 10. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `122bda71`.

## Fix

I have a fix on my fork, branch `fix/f114-hf-resume`, commit `37a748e18795d4f9966bbf52280a385da212f538`.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f114-hf-resume?expand=1

Fork pull request, where I provide the fix: https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw-windows-node/pull/4

body:
## What happens

The chat box stays editable while voice is recording. `AppendVoiceTranscript` reads the draft and builds the next string before the write is queued. Keystrokes are applied later, in order, on the UI thread. A keystroke queued after that read and before the voice write is replaced by the stale string. Enter can send the voice text without those keystrokes.

On this machine, with the UI queue held, a draft of `typed` followed by a transcript `heard` became `heard`.

## Where

Checked on [122bda71](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e).

- Append: [ChatComposerViewModel.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ChatComposerViewModel.cs) `AppendVoiceTranscript` reads `_draft` and then calls `SetDraft`.
- Queue: `SetDraft` applies the value inside `Mutate`, which drains in FIFO order.

## Suggested fix

Read the draft and append the transcript inside the queued mutation, so the write sees the draft at the moment it is applied.

## Environment

Windows 11. .NET 10. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `122bda71`.

## Fix

I have a fix on my fork, branch `fix/f047-voice-draft`, commit `4ac31a11557e80bfc93359c516287c2242c857ec`.

body:
## What happens

On the Cron page, Remove sends `cron.remove` on the first click. The job id is stored in `_removedJobIds` before the gateway accepts the remove. If the remove is rejected, that id stays stored, so a later one-shot completion notice for the same id is suppressed.

Run Now calls `cron.run` with `force: true`, which is the client default, including when the job is turned off. The Sessions page asks before a destructive action. These two do not.

## Where

Checked on [122bda71](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e).

- Remove and Run Now: [CronPage.xaml.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/CronPage.xaml.cs). `OnRemoveClick` adds the id, then calls `RemoveCronJobAsync`. `OnRunNowClick` calls `RunCronJobDetailedAsync(jobId)` with no confirm.
- Force default: [OpenClawGatewayClient.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Shared/OpenClawGatewayClient.cs) `RunCronJobDetailedAsync` parameter `force = true`.

## Suggested fix

Ask before remove, and ask before Run Now when the job is disabled. Remember the id only for the gateway call, and forget it when remove is not accepted.

## Environment

Windows 11. .NET 10. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `122bda71`.

## Fix

I have a fix on my fork, branch `fix/f058-cron-confirm`, commit `12c236d6eec5ba3d31b0e126ada1ebb6bd33e6a4`.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f058-cron-confirm?expand=1

body:
## What happens

`system.which` is supposed to search `PATH` for a single executable name. A name such as `C:tool` has no slash, so it is accepted. `Path.Combine` of a PATH directory and `C:tool` drops the directory. `File.Exists` then probes the current directory of drive C. On this machine that returned `C:openclaw-which-probe-3db8754daa314c33a58d38366da....exe`, which is not a PATH hit.

`NUL`, `CON`, `COM1`, and `LPT1` are reserved device names. They are rejected too, including a `PATHEXT` suffix.

## Where

Checked on [122bda71](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e).

- Lookup: [SystemCapability.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/122bda71b2211a8fdb40bb7c8589efd19beb5b2e/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/SystemCapability.cs) `ResolveExecutable` rejected only `/` and `\`, then called `Path.Combine` and `File.Exists`.

## Suggested fix

Accept only a single file name. Reject `:`, reserved device names, and any candidate whose full path is not under that PATH directory.

## Environment

Windows 11. .NET 10. OpenClaw Companion source on main at `122bda71`.

## Fix

I have a fix on my fork, branch `fix/f010-which-reserved-names`, commit `4fcec8e48bb6f381b9c9d9bc4227911a768c80b6`.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f010-which-reserved-names?expand=1

Before the change, the lookup returned the drive-relative file. After the change, that name is not resolved. `cmd` on PATH still resolves.

# Companion reports every native Gateway decode failure as a missing integration contract

Companion's native Gateway client reuses this error for several different contract-validation failures:

> The installed Gateway MSIX does not expose Companion's isolated-session contract. Update the Gateway MSIX, then retry setup. Credentials were not sent.

That recommendation is misleading when initial contract detection succeeded but a later lifecycle response is missing a required field, has an unexpected type, or has a different command/schema.

## Evidence and scope

- Reported Store versions: Companion **2026.10.502.0**, Gateway **2026.10.900.0**.
- The package-qualified `clawctl status --json` response exited **0** with `ok: true`, `schemaVersion: 1`, `command: "status"`, and `integration: { "kind": "isolated-session", "version": 1 }`. It reported a running session and Gateway.
- Companion subsequently logged the quoted error while blocking a strong credential pending managed-local endpoint ownership verification.
- Companion's public package reservation `msix-package/2026.10.5/502` identifies source `f81edef9a06222e4eea5a93dd21ecfb7e3002c10`, also tagged `v2026.10.5-alpha.4`. Its [native package client](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/f81edef9a06222e4eea5a93dd21ecfb7e3002c10/src/OpenClaw.Connection/NativeGateway/NativeGatewayPackageClient.cs) routes multiple validation failures through the generic unsupported-contract message.
- Top-level `status` does not exercise the detailed `gateway-service status` or `companion prepare --check` decoders. The incident's exact rejected operation/field remains unknown; valid initial detection does not prove that later responses are valid or that Companion selected the same package.
- The declared listener types in Gateway `v2026.10.9-msix.0` and the matching Companion decoder agree. No numeric/date encoding defect or verified repair is established.

Related connection-failure report: #1691. This bug specifically tracks error classification and actionable, credential-safe reporting, not a claim that the underlying connection failure has been diagnosed or fixed.

## Expected behavior

Distinguish a genuinely unsupported integration contract from a later malformed/incompatible response, an unsuccessful command, and process/timeout failures. Identify the operation, rejected field path, and safe expected/observed shape where available. Do not prescribe a Gateway update solely because an unrelated required field was absent.

Preserve the credential preflight boundary: no fallback to sending credentials, relaxed ownership checks, retries that change state, or extra probe invocation just to explain an error.

## Acceptance criteria

Related: #2000, #1981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Build and Test fails on unrelated PRs and `main` pushes when hosted runners are loaded. Separately, a pathological A2UI SVG can freeze the chat UI thread for longer than the 8 s render cap.

## User Impact

User impact: CI stops failing intermittently on four tests that were timing-sensitive. An A2UI SVG with more than 64 KiB of path data now shows the broken-image fallback immediately instead of freezing the UI. Ordinary SVGs are unaffected: the largest SVG still allowed decodes in about 0.2–0.3 s locally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each failure was traced to a cause before any test was changed, and none of the assertions were loosened:

- **`ChatComposerControllerTests.Dispose_VoiceCancellationCallbackCanWaitForReentrantControllerWork`**: the test blocked shared thread-pool threads that its own cleanup work needed. It now uses dedicated threads, the same fix the sibling lifetime test already had.
- **`ActivationRouterTests.StopAsync_CancelsAndDrainsInFlightDirectConfirmation`**: hard-coded 2 s waits now use a named constant (default 10 s, `OPENCLAW_TRAY_TEST_ACTIVATION_WAIT_SECONDS`).
- **`GatewayProtocolLiveRoundTripTests.HandshakeGate_Reconnect_SuppressesEarlyMutationThenSendsAfterHelloOk`**: polling could miss the roughly 1 s window before the client reconnects. The test now waits for the `Disconnected` event, and the mock server holds the reconnect by not sending the challenge on the second socket until the test sends it.
- **`GatewayFixtureUiTests.HomeSidebar_CustomizeDoesNotNavigate_AndHomeRestoresCanonicalConversation`**: the sidebar geometry was read before layout settled after unpinning. The test now waits for the settled layout and keeps the same pixel ranges.
- **SVG (product)**: `SvgImageSource.SetSourceAsync` can block the UI thread past `SvgRenderTimeout`, because the timeout stops only the wait, not the parse. The new `SvgGeometryBudget` rejects oversized `d`/`points` path data before decode.
- **Tray UI testhost crash** (`ReactorChatLayoutProofTests` flyout tests): diagnostics only. When Tray UI tests fail, a new CI step saves the crash entries from the Windows event log (crashing module, exception code, offset; no memory dumps) to `TrayUI/wer-testhost-events.txt` in the `test-results-ui` artifact. The test was not reordered: closing the flyout first would remove the live-update behavior that `SandboxFlyout_*` tests.
- **`HistoricalFractionalVoiceConversationRendersWithoutLoadingPlaceholder`**: not changed here; #1996 fixed it on `main` after these failing runs.

`docs/CI_FAILURES.md` now covers the crash investigation (adds `SandboxFlyout_*`, the run links, and the new crash-records file), notes the SVG fix, and adds an entry for the cluster of UI Automation "Operation timed out" errors in run 41786895448.

## Evidence

- **Composer dispose test.** Throwaway repro with the thread pool saturated: the old pattern still hadn't finished after 10 s; the dedicated-thread pattern finished at once. After the fix, 30/30 passes (together with the ActivationRouter tests).
- **Handshake reconnect test.** 30/30 passes of the `GatewayProtocolLiveRoundTripTests` class with all 32 CPUs busy (24 tests per run). The trace shows `socket #2 accepted; challenge delivered`.
- **SVG.** `PathologicalGeometry_RejectedBeforeDecode` finishes in 30–42 ms (5/5 runs of `A2UISvgTests`). The largest SVG still allowed (3,560 path segments, 65,608 bytes) decodes in 204–319 ms.
- **Sidebar test.** The first 10 local runs went 6/10. The four failures were at other assertions (a "customize flyout" timeout and an `Assert.Equal`), not the new geometry wait. The next 16 runs all passed.
- **Fractional voice test.** 10/10 locally on current `main` (unchanged by this PR).

- [x] Chore or infrastructure

## Required proof pools

- `./build.ps1`: all builds succeeded.
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj`: 5070/5070 passed.
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj` (with `OPENCLAW_REPO_ROOT` set): 4927 passed, 1 failed, 24 skipped.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro for Workstations
- `openclaw/openclaw-windows-node` `origin/main` `b6c849e8ed44a6193710a73432e385c9f1608d2f`
- Fix branch `fix/f079-exec-approvals-ui-thread` at `eab9b6b914f93aac217f12381d3751bbf7fc9d9e` on `SebTardif/openclaw-windows-node`
- Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f079-exec-approvals-ui-thread

`CreatePullRequest` is forbidden for this account, so this issue carries the branch.

## What happens

Saving an exec policy awaits the store, then a failed replace raises the failed status on the continuation thread. The success path already posts its update through the UI dispatcher. The failure path did not, so the save-failed hint can throw before it appears.

## Steps

1. Check out `b6c849e8ed44a6193710a73432e385c9f1608d2f`.
2. In `SaveExecApprovalsAsync`, after `ReplaceAsync` throws `IOException` or returns no snapshot, `SetExecApprovalsFailure` runs on the caller continuation.
3. `CompleteExecApprovalsMutation` for a successful replace is inside `HandleOnUiThread`.

## Repair

On `eab9b6b914f93aac217f12381d3751bbf7fc9d9e`, the failure call uses `HandleOnUiThread` as well.

`DefaultActionSaveFailure_ReportsStatusOnTheUiThread` holds the test dispatcher. The status stays unchanged until the queued update runs, then it is `SaveFailed`, and the displayed action stays `prompt`.

Related: #1976

## What Problem This Solves

Qualified Qwen Local AI models keep thinking when Effort is Off, and unsupported effort levels can fail when the Gateway sends them to llama-server. This PR addresses those Qwen templates; #1976 still needs model-specific proof and effort metadata for Bonsai, Nemotron Bolt, and custom profiles.

## User Impact

Qualified Qwen models can receive `reasoning_effort: "none"`, and canvas actions leave the user's Effort setting alone. Existing companion-owned provider entries migrate their model settings without replacing credentials. These reasoning controls require Gateway 2026.9.8 or newer; older Gateways show an upgrade error before the model starts. Bonsai, Bolt, and custom model effort metadata remains unchanged pending template proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

The router no longer forces reasoning on. The model catalog records the verified effort vocabulary for each qualified Qwen template, and provider registration maps Off to `none` while hiding unsupported levels. The provider coordinator recognizes the previous exact provider shape and replaces only its owned model array, with a Gateway version check and a guarded write.

## Evidence

- On an isolated WSL llama.cpp b11320 router using the real Qwen3.5 9B GGUF and a preset without the forced reasoning line, `reasoning_effort: "none"` returned answer `4` with **0 reasoning characters**. The router process was stopped after the check.
- Against an isolated **real OpenClaw 2026.9.8 CLI**, the model-array dry run and guarded write both succeeded; the test credential and primary model were preserved; a retry with the stale expected value was rejected (exit 1).
- Earlier isolated Gateway request checks found that 2026.6.5 accepted the config fields but still sent `medium` for Off; 2026.9.8 sent `none`. This is why the floor is 2026.9.8 rather than the issue's proposed 2026.6.5.
- Focused WSL tests: 110 Tray provider tests at `cefc096` and 113 SetupEngine recovery/onboarding tests at this head passed. Two new native credential integration tests are skipped outside Windows. The preceding implementation also passed 2 Connection tests and 79 Shared catalog tests.
- Still needed before merge: Windows app build and UI proof, a real native Gateway migration run, full-weight Qwen3.8 inference, and product end-to-end testing. Medium generation with the 9B model exceeded the laptop's 120-second request window.

ClawSweeper reviewed the older `d8f5e32` head and reported three code findings. This revision admits only the exact current or pre-effort Qwen provider shape in setup recovery and cleanup, checks native Gateway compatibility before starting the model, and localizes the new upgrade and migration guidance in all six supported resource files. An independent follow-up review also found that native recovery could stop before migrating the verified legacy provider, and that WSL recovery rollback could restore the wrong model shape. Both paths now continue through guarded publication or restore the exact prior shape using the known credential. Tests cover legacy recovery, rollback and uninstall, rejection of an edited legacy provider, native preflight before runtime or configuration writes, and localized upgrade guidance. An independent final-diff review found no further actionable code issue. The ClawSweeper comment has not yet been rerun on this head; maintainer decisions and product proof requested by the bot remain open.

body:
## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro for Workstations
- `openclaw/openclaw-windows-node` commit `b6c849e8ed44a6193710a73432e385c9f1608d2f` (`origin/main` on 2026-11-04)
- Python 3.13.15, the interpreter installed on this machine
- Python 3.11.9, a second interpreter used for the same command
- Dry run only. `--yes` was not passed. No process was stopped and no file was deleted.

## What happens

The wipe script compiles its dev-patch pattern while the module is loading, before it reads a profile path and before it prints an inventory:

```python
DEV_PATCH = re.compile(r"\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,13}[a-z0-9])?\z")
```

That line is `scripts/wipe_openclaw_state.py:104`. It has been there since `598918ff8d7f5a151c3682cc33307ca80e7f7188` (`chore: add scripts/wipe_openclaw_state.py`, #1734).

`\z` is the end-of-string anchor in .NET, which is what a PowerShell `ValidatePattern` uses. [Python 3.14 adds `\z` as a synonym for `\Z`](https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.14.html#re). On 3.11 and 3.13 the same spelling is a bad escape. The script's top-level handler catches `InventoryError`, `OSError`, and `subprocess.SubprocessError`. `re.error` is not one of those, so the process prints a traceback and stops.

The current-head proof on #1734 used Python 3.14 ([comment 6587094781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1734#issuecomment-6587094781)). `\z` compiles on that version. This report is the same command on 3.11 and 3.13.

## Steps

1. Check out `b6c849e8ed44a6193710a73432e385c9f1608d2f`.
2. Run `python scripts/wipe_openclaw_state.py` with Python 3.13.15. Do not pass `--yes`.
3. Run the same command with Python 3.11.9.

## Result

Both runs exit 1 at line 104, before any `== DRY RUN:` heading.

Python 3.13.15:

```text
re.PatternError: bad escape \z at position 38
```

Python 3.11.9:

```text
re.error: bad escape \z at position 38
```

`scripts/test-wipe-openclaw-state.ps1` exits 1 while it imports the module, so the patch checks in that driver do not run.

## Repair

In `DEV_PATCH`, spell the end of the string as `\Z`.

On Python 3.13.15, `\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,13}[a-z0-9])?\Z` matches `beta1`, `a`, `ab`, and 15 `a` characters. It rejects `a-`, `bad!name`, 16 `a` characters, and the empty string. `gateway_dev_patch` lowercases the suffix before `fullmatch`, so `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClawGateway-Beta1` still returns `beta1`. These patch tokens have no newline, so the 3.14 synonym does not change their match.

## Python 3.11 after that compile

Those two runs never reach the file inventory. After the pattern compiles, Python 3.11 still stops on a later call. [`Path.is_junction()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path.is_junction) was added in Python 3.12. On 3.11.9, `hasattr(Path, "is_junction")` is false. On 3.13.15 it is true.

`models_in` calls it for every directory:

```python
if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.is_junction():
```

`inventory_paths` calls `models_in` from `take_inventory`. `main` does that inventory before the dry-run return and before `stop_processes`. `AttributeError` is not caught. A matching directory, such as a direct child of `%APPDATA%` whose name contains `openclaw`, is enough. The dry run and `--yes` both take that path.

`remove_path` calls the same method at line 800. A dry run that finds only files does not call the directory branch in `models_in`. `--yes` then reaches `remove_path` after `stop_processes`.

A missing `is_junction` has to stay a refusal. Treating it as an ordinary directory makes `remove_path` walk the junction target. The link-only delete is `os.rmdir` on that branch.

Python 3.12 has `Path.is_junction` and still does not have `re`'s `\z`, so a version check that only asks for 3.12 leaves the import crash in place. Change the pattern first. The 3.11 follow-through is a Windows junction test that does not need `Path.is_junction`, or a clear exit that names Python 3.12 before inventory starts.

## Separate from the URL issues

#2001 through #2010 are display and copy leaks. This report is the wipe script exiting before it prints a report.

body:
## What happens

The exec-approval dialog shows the sanitized command, then Allow runs the original command. The sanitizer escapes control, format, and non-ASCII spaces. It does not treat U+2800 BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK as invisible. That character is category Other Symbol, so `IsInvisible` leaves it in the text.

In the dialog font it looks blank. The operator can approve a command whose visible spacing is not the command that runs. Mixed-script confusables already raise a warning. A braille blank does not.

## Where

Checked on [7967d509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c) by reading the code. An approval dialog was not opened.

- Invisible set: [ExecApprovalCommandDisplaySanitizer.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Shared/ExecApprovals/ExecApprovalCommandDisplaySanitizer.cs#L266)
- Dialog binds the sanitized text: [ExecApprovalV2UiPromptHandler.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Shared/ExecApprovals/ExecApprovalV2UiPromptHandler.cs#L49) and [ExecApprovalDialog.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Dialogs/ExecApprovalDialog.cs#L136)

## Suggested fix

Escape U+2800 the same way the sanitizer already escapes other invisible code points, so the operator sees the escape instead of a blank.

## Environment

Windows 11. OpenClaw Companion source on main at commit 7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c (2026-11-04). No packaged installer build was used.

## Steps

1. Send an exec-approval request whose command contains U+2800 BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK between two tokens.
2. Read the approval dialog.
3. Allow. The original command, including U+2800, is what runs.

`ExecApprovalCommandDisplaySanitizer.IsInvisible` escapes control, format, and non-ASCII spaces. U+2800 is category Other Symbol, so it stays in `commandStatus.Text`. The dialog binds that text. Mixed-script confusables already show a warning. A braille blank does not.

## Repair

Escape U+2800 with the same invisible-code-point path. Add a regression that a command containing U+2800 is shown with the escape, not as a blank gap. Stop there.

body:
## What happens

`scripts/validate-msix-storage-paths.ps1 -CertPath` imports that certificate into `Cert:\LocalMachine\TrustedPeople` so the sideload package can install. Teardown removes the AppX package with `Remove-AppxPackage` and does not remove the certificate. The publisher stays trusted on the machine after the validation run exits.

Import requires an elevated store write. The leftover is the trust entry the script added and then did not undo.

## Where

Checked on [7967d509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c) by reading the script. The script was not run.

- Import: [validate-msix-storage-paths.ps1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/scripts/validate-msix-storage-paths.ps1#L588)
- Teardown: [validate-msix-storage-paths.ps1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/scripts/validate-msix-storage-paths.ps1#L1041)

## Suggested fix

Record the imported thumbprint and remove that certificate from TrustedPeople during teardown. Do not remove a different certificate that was already in the store.

## Environment

Windows 11. OpenClaw Companion source on main at commit 7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c (2026-11-04). No packaged installer build was used.

## Steps

1. On Windows, as an administrator, run `scripts/validate-msix-storage-paths.ps1 -CertPath` with a test `.cer`.
2. Let the script import the certificate and finish teardown.
3. Open `Cert:\LocalMachine\TrustedPeople` and find that thumbprint.

Line 591 calls `Import-Certificate` into `Cert:\LocalMachine\TrustedPeople`. `Invoke-Teardown` removes the AppX package and does not remove the certificate.

## Repair

Remember the thumbprint this run imported and remove only that certificate during teardown. Add a regression, or a script assertion, that a thumbprint which was already in the store is left in place. Stop there.

body:
## What happens

A tool event stores `command` or `url` in the activity label. `GatewayService` copies that label into the activity title. Command Center support text includes the title, then says command arguments are excluded.

The tray log line for the same event does go through `TokenSanitizer.SanitizeLogMessage`, which drops a URL query. The copied support text does not. A command, a path, or a `?token=` in the title is therefore copied with the support bundle.

## Where

Checked on [7967d509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c) by reading the code. Support text was not copied from a running app.

- Title: [GatewayService.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/GatewayService.cs#L267)
- Log line, which is sanitized: [ActivityStreamService.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/ActivityStreamService.cs#L50)
- Support copy: [CommandCenterTextHelper.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Helpers/CommandCenterTextHelper.cs#L64)

## Suggested fix

Record only the tool name and phase in the activity title. Keep the "command arguments are excluded" line true.

## Environment

Windows 11. OpenClaw Companion source on main at commit 7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c (2026-11-04). No packaged installer build was used.

## Steps

1. Receive a gateway tool event with a `command` or `url` argument.
2. Open Command Center and copy the support text.
3. Read the recent-activity line, then the line that says command arguments are excluded.

`GatewayService.OnActivityChanged` sets the activity title to `sessionKey: activity.Label`. `CommandCenterTextHelper.BuildSupportContext` copies `item.Title`. The tray log line is sanitized by `TokenSanitizer.SanitizeLogMessage` before it is written. The copied support text is not.

## Repair

Put only the tool name and phase in the activity title used for support text. Add a regression that a command argument is absent from `BuildSupportContext` while the exclusion sentence remains. Stop there. The tray tooltip is #2007.

## What happens

A tool event copies `command` or `url` into the activity label, cut at 60 characters, with no redaction. The tray icon tooltip prints that label on each refresh through `AgentActivity.DisplayText`. The gateway client log deliberately omits the label because it can carry a command, path, or URL. A `?token=` in the first 60 characters is still shown on the tooltip.

## Where

Checked on [7967d509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c) by reading the code. A tool event was not sent from a live gateway.

- Label: [OpenClawGatewayClient.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Shared/OpenClawGatewayClient.cs#L4082)
- Display text: [Models.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Models.cs#L92)
- Tooltip: [TrayTooltipBuilder.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/TrayTooltipBuilder.cs#L50)

## Suggested fix

Redact URL userinfo, query, and fragment before the label is stored. Keep the tool name and phase, which the client log already records.

## Environment

Windows 11. OpenClaw Companion source on main at commit 7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c (2026-11-04). No packaged installer build was used.

## Steps

1. Receive a gateway tool event whose `args.command` or `args.url` is longer than a short label and contains a query.
2. Hover the tray icon while that activity is current.
3. Read the tooltip.

`OpenClawGatewayClient.HandleToolEvent` copies the first 60 characters of `command` or `url` into `AgentActivity.Label`. `DisplayText` includes that label. `TrayTooltipBuilder` prints `CurrentActivity.DisplayText`. The client log already omits the label.

## Repair

Store a redacted label: drop URL userinfo, query, and fragment before truncation. Add a regression that a `?token=` query is not in `DisplayText`. Stop there. The copied support bundle is #2008.

body:
## What happens

A config object that has no `properties` map, and an array whose items are not plain scalars, is serialized into a plain text box. Nested token, secret, and password fields inside that JSON are visible. Password fields elsewhere on the page leave an existing secret blank and do not preload it.

Any edit parses that box and stages the whole JSON value. Save then writes the whole object or array, not the one field the user changed. A redaction marker that arrived inside the JSON is staged with the rest.

Objects that do declare `properties` are still rendered field by field. This path is only the schemaless object and the complex array.

## Where

Checked on [7967d509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c) by reading the code. The Config page was not opened.

- Schemaless object: [SchemaConfigEditor.xaml.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Controls/SchemaConfigEditor.xaml.cs#L231) calls `RenderJsonObjectField`.
- Complex array: [SchemaConfigEditor.xaml.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Controls/SchemaConfigEditor.xaml.cs#L379) calls `RenderJsonArrayField`.
- Objects that have `properties` stay on the field walker: [SchemaConfigEditor.xaml.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Controls/SchemaConfigEditor.xaml.cs#L105).

## Suggested fix

Edit map entries and object-array items as individual fields. Do not stage a redaction marker as a new value. Mask nested credential names the same way the password field already does.

## Environment

Windows 11. OpenClaw Companion source on main at commit 7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c (2026-11-04). No packaged installer build was used.

## Steps

1. Open Config for a schema property whose type is `object` and which has no `properties` map.
2. Read the editor. It is one JSON text box containing the stored object.
3. Change one nested field and save.

`RenderField` sends that object to `RenderJsonObjectField`. A non-scalar array goes to `RenderJsonArrayField`. Either edit stages the whole JSON value. Objects that declare `properties` stay on the field walker.

## Repair

Do not preload a nested credential into that box, and do not stage a redaction marker as the saved value. Add a regression that editing one key in a schemaless object does not write a placeholder over an untouched secret. Stop there.

The Local AI page shows the same saved URL when the gateway has no friendly name. Direct connect stores the URL after `NormalizeForWebSocket`, which removes userinfo and leaves the query and fragment. `GatewayUrlHelper.SanitizeForDisplay` is not used on either surface.

Display `GatewayUrlHelper.SanitizeForDisplay` of the saved URL in both places. Prefer the friendly name on Local AI when one exists, and use the sanitized URL only as the fallback.

body:
## What happens

The copied browser-proxy SSH line builds `user@host` from the saved SSH user and host with no charset check. Open Terminal and the tunnel launcher reject a user or host that is outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` or that starts with `-`, through `SshTunnelCommandLine.ValidateUserAndHost`. The copy path does not. Command Center diagnostics and the browser setup copy both build that target.

Pasting the copied line into cmd or PowerShell treats `&`, `|`, and similar characters as shell syntax. The app itself would have refused to start `ssh` with that user or host.

## Where

Checked on [7967d509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c) by reading the code. The line was not copied into a shell.

- Command Center builder: [CommandCenterStateBuilder.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/CommandCenterStateBuilder.cs#L399)
- Diagnostics copy: [CommandCenterTextHelper.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Helpers/CommandCenterTextHelper.cs#L322)
- The check the launcher already uses: [SshTunnelCommandLine.cs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c/src/OpenClaw.Shared/SshTunnelCommandLine.cs#L24)

## Suggested fix

Keep the `<user>@<host>` placeholder unless the saved user and host pass `ValidateUserAndHost`.

## Environment

Windows 11. OpenClaw Companion source on main at commit 7967d509886fc9efecbb19c8236350a82867f69c (2026-11-04). No packaged installer build was used.

## Steps

1. Save an SSH tunnel whose host contains a character outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, or a host that starts with `-`.
2. Open Command Center and copy the browser-proxy SSH line.
3. Compare that line with Open Terminal for the same host.

`SshTunnelCommandLine.ValidateUserAndHost` rejects that host before `ssh` starts. `CommandCenterStateBuilder.BuildSshTarget` and `CommandCenterTextHelper.BuildBrowserProxySshForwardHint` still concatenate `user@host`.

## Repair

If the saved user or host fails `ValidateUserAndHost`, copy the `<user>@<host>` placeholder instead. Add a regression for a host containing `&` and for a host that starts with `-`. Stop there.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a portable update download that receives the response headers and then stalls never finishes. Closing the progress window does not cancel it, and startup stays behind that wait.

## User Impact

User impact: closing the download window stops the download. A download that stalls after the headers also stops at a deadline, 10 minutes unless `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` sets another positive number of seconds. A canceled download does not install, and the app continues to start.

## Why This Change Was Made

`DownloadUpdateAsync()` was called with no cancellation token. Updatum reads the asset after the headers arrive, so the 100-second HTTP timeout does not cover a stalled body. The progress window had no close signal. The download now receives a token that cancels when that window closes and when the overall deadline ends. If that token is already canceled when the download call returns, the app does not install. The success path closes the window after that check, and that close is what cancels the token.

## Evidence

`UpdateDownloadDeadlineTests` passed: blank and invalid values stay at 10 minutes, and `1` and `30` become that many seconds. The tray source passes that token to `DownloadUpdateAsync`, cancels it from the progress window `Closed` event, and records a canceled download instead of installing.

The release app from this head showed the update window, and closing the download window wrote `Update download canceled.` The installer did not start.
