body:
Related: openclaw/openclaw#192217, openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging#241

## What Problem This Solves

Developers had no repeatable way to measure whether Microsoft Defender scanning of the native Gateway payload's many files slows Gateway startup and Companion native setup.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible change. Developers can record a private Defender, file I/O and CPU trace of a synthetic Gateway startup or a real Companion native setup, and get a sanitized summary of which payload packages were scanned during each setup step.

## Why This Change Was Made

These scripts produced the evidence behind the Gateway startup file-count fixes (openclaw/openclaw#192217) and the install-time payload prewarm (openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging#241). Keeping them in the repository lets those changes, and later bundling or lazy-loading work, be measured the same way.

- `scripts\Invoke-GatewayStartupTrace.ps1` runs a bounded pre-listener startup probe, on the host and optionally in an MXC session, while a single named WPR instance records Defender `Scans.Light` with FileIO, DiskIO and CPU.
- `scripts\Invoke-GatewaySetupTrace.ps1` records a person running the real Companion native setup, and splits the trace at setup-log milestones and the observed AI-setup page.
- Only the recorder is elevated, through a UAC prompt. It owns one `OpenClawStartup-<guid>` WPR instance and stops or cancels only that instance. Every WPR call is time-bounded.
- Summaries contain only counts, durations, anonymous process indexes and payload-relative package names. ETL files, copied setup logs and raw errors stay in a private run directory.
- `Build-NativeGatewayFromSource.ps1` gains `-SkipSetup`, passed to the deploy step, so a candidate can be registered without running setup before tracing.

No Defender, power or system setting is changed, and no exclusion is added. See `scripts\gateway-startup-trace\README.md`.

## Evidence

Two traced Companion native setup runs on the same ARM64 host, using Gateway 2026.10.9 with the startup file-count fixes (both reached the AI-setup page):

| Milestone (s from attempt start) | Without prewarm | With prewarm |
|---|---|---|
| Config validation | 57.5 to 68.7 | 51.8 to 60.7 |
| Gateway start requested | 71.5 | 63.9 |
| Start acknowledged | 111.3 | 89.3 |
| Listener verified | 112.2 | 90.2 |
| Model discovery | 150.1 | 128.3 |

| Defender payload scans | Without prewarm | With prewarm |
|---|---|---|
| All processes | 8,734 (union 82.7 s) | 10,346 (union 77.2 s) |
| Gateway runtime process | 4,599 | 2,272 |
| Prewarm worker | none | 5,842, all on listed startup files |

These are single warm runs. They show the tooling attributes scans to processes, packages and setup steps; they do not prove the cause of the timing difference. Confounds include:

- setup in the prewarm run began about 20 s before recording;
- no reboot between runs;
- the payload was freshly extracted;
- heavy unrelated concurrent scanning on the host;
- different packaging versions;
- prewarm overlaps setup, so scan unions are not exclusive.

<details>
<summary>Review follow-ups applied before publication</summary>

An independent review of the scripts found these issues, now fixed and covered where possible offline:

- `wpr.exe -stop` could hang with no cancel. Stop, status and cancel are now bounded child processes; a timed-out stop is killed and the same instance is cancelled.
- An attempt started during the UAC prompt was ignored, leaving `milestones` null. The controller now follows attempts started after it launched, keeps `milestones` an array, and the summary reports `attempt_started_before_recording` and each window's `unrecorded_prefix_ms`.
- Raw exception text could reach the shareable summary. It now uses fixed `stop_reason` codes; raw text stays in the private result.
- A comma-joined root from `pwsh -File` silently produced zero scans. Roots must now contain `openclaw.mjs`, comma-joined roots are rejected, and `report_files_matching_payload` distinguishes zero scans from a wrong root.
- Startup-mode counts and package groups now use only scans inside the measured arm, matching its scan union.

</details>

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs or instructions
- [x] Tests or validation
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore or infrastructure

## Scope

- [ ] Tray or WinUI UX
- [ ] Windows node capability
- [ ] Local MCP or `winnode`
- [ ] Gateway, connection, or pairing
- [ ] Setup or onboarding
- [ ] Permissions, privacy, or security
- [x] Tests, CI, or docs

## Required proof pools

- `none`: developer-only measurement scripts. No product code, installer, node capability or Gateway path changes.

## Validation

Run on the PR head with `OPENCLAW_*` variables cleared and `OPENCLAW_REPO_ROOT` set to the worktree:

- `.\scripts\test-gateway-startup-trace.ps1`: passed (offline helper, guard, refusal and summary root-validation checks; never starts WPR, MXC or a Gateway).
- `.\scripts\validate-docs.ps1`: passed.

- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore`: first run 1 failed, 4809 passed, 24 skipped, in a Gateway fixture exec-approval test this PR does not touch. Rerun: 4810 passed, 0 failed, 24 skipped, 4834 total.
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore`: 4788 passed, 0 failed.

- Evidence after fix: the milestone and scan tables in Evidence, from the sanitized summaries.
- Observed result: both runs saved the named WPR instance and left WPR not recording. Milestones, per-process scan counts and package groups were produced. For the prewarm run, milestones were derived from the copied setup log because setup began before recording (the issue fixed above).
- Screenshot or artifact links verified? `N/A`. ETL files and logs are private and not published.

Related: #1117. Depends on the personal-identity Control UI contract in openclaw/openclaw#163765. Related to, but separate from, the managed Gateway upgrade in #1128.

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.

Companion users cannot select their own verified Tailscale identity when connecting to a supported Gateway, so human activity is associated with shared Gateway credentials.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

Users can explicitly select personal Tailscale identity for an eligible secure Tailscale Gateway. Existing shared-credential connections remain available. The Gateway continues to decide pairing and permissions; a failed personal sign-in does not silently become Shared owner.

The follow-up hardening rejects the shared `gateway-owner` profile in personal mode. Profile changes retire the old lease until the same person is verified again; a different person cannot silently replace that identity on the existing socket. Personal legacy media reads use the verified Serve origin and current granted scopes without a bearer fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The native connection verifies the personal operator before exposing the session to Chat and Dashboard. Dashboard authentication stays bound to the current Gateway, verified person, device and connection generation. Reconnection or a change of selection retires the previous authority. Node identity and shared-credential paths remain distinct.

This is a draft pending the common Control UI contract and real Tailscale validation. It does not change a Gateway's configuration or migrate existing profiles automatically.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

- The hardening delta over `1cc74a49` passed 30 focused Shared tests and 55 focused Connection tests. They cover shared-owner rejection, same-person reverification, changed-person refusal, personal media headers and refusal, and in-flight media lease retirement.
- A pure policy negative control used the original PR policy source and the same `gateway-owner` response: the original admitted it; the corrected policy rejects it. This is API-level red/green evidence, not a live Gateway claim.
- Independent P0-P3 source review found no actionable defects in the nine-file hardening delta. The named comment audit found no added comments or suppressions. These are source/proof-plan assessments, not live Gateway execution.

body:
## What Problem

A portable update download that receives the response headers and then stalls never finishes. Closing the progress window does not cancel it, and startup stays behind that wait.

Pull request creation is refused for this account (`CreatePullRequest` FORBIDDEN, REST create 404). Permissions are `pull: true` and `push: false`. The branch is on the fork.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f118-update-download-deadline?expand=1

Head: `a8e2518215ba93131da1cb6d70ca67e77b704240` on `SebTardif:fix/f118-update-download-deadline`

## User Impact

Closing the download window stops the download. A download that stalls after the headers also stops at a deadline, 10 minutes unless `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` sets another positive number of seconds. A canceled download does not install, and the app continues to start.

## Why

`DownloadUpdateAsync()` was called with no cancellation token. Updatum reads the asset after the headers arrive, so the 100-second HTTP timeout does not cover a stalled body. The progress window had no close signal. The download now receives a token that cancels when that window closes and when the overall deadline ends.

## Evidence

`UpdateDownloadDeadlineTests` passed: blank and invalid values stay at 10 minutes, and `1` and `30` become that many seconds. The tray source passes that token to `DownloadUpdateAsync`, cancels it from the progress window `Closed` event, and records a canceled download instead of installing.

`./build.ps1` succeeded. Shared tests: 4810 passed, 24 skipped. Tray tests: 4796 passed.

## Not verified

The progress window was not opened. A live GitHub download that stalls after the headers was not captured.

body:
## Summary

Reasoning control is broken for Local AI (the llama-server the app launches and registers as the `llamacpp` provider):

1. **Effort Off / `/think off` does not stop thinking.** The model keeps reasoning; the gateway only hides the output, so Off still costs the full thinking time.
2. **Newer gateways can fail outright.** Gateway 2026.10.5 beta sends `reasoning_effort` to local OpenAI-compatible providers by default. With the app's current provider entry, `/think minimal` on Qwen3.8 returns HTTP 500 from llama-server.

## Root cause

- `LlamaServerRouterConfiguration.cs:295` writes `reasoning = on` into the llama-server preset. With `--reasoning on`, llama.cpp ignores `reasoning_effort: "none"`, so the per-request off switch has no effect. This is an upstream llama.cpp bug (still on master); under the default `--reasoning auto`, `"none"` turns thinking off for every template in the Local AI catalog.
- `LocalAiGatewayProviderDefinition.BuildProviderJson` declares `reasoning = true` but no `compat.supportsReasoningEffort` / `supportedReasoningEfforts`. The gateway therefore either sends nothing the server honors (older gateways) or sends levels the model template does not support, such as `minimal` (2026.10.5 beta).
- `GatewayActionTransport.cs:122` sends `thinking: "low"` with every canvas (A2UI) action. The gateway persists that level on the chat session, so one canvas action silently switches the user's Effort to Low and turns Off back into thinking.

## Proposed fix (standard `reasoning_effort`, not model-specific)

Use OpenAI's `reasoning_effort` field, which llama-server implements and the gateway already supports per model, with Off sent as `"none"`:

1. Drop `reasoning = on` from the llama-server preset (fall back to the default `auto`).
2. Declare per-model effort support in the provider entry, sourced from the model catalog for every entry:
   - Qwen3.8: `supportedReasoningEfforts: [none, low, medium, high]`, hide Minimal (its template has low / medium / xhigh, and accepts high as xhigh).
   - Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5: `[none, medium]`, hide Minimal and High (on/off only).
   - `"none"` must be listed, or the gateway drops Off.
   - Do not hide Low: the gateway rejects an explicitly requested hidden level rather than clamping it, and paired phones request Low.
3. Stop canvas actions from sending `thinking: "low"`.

Resulting pickers: Off / Low / Medium / High / Ultra for Qwen3.8, Off / Low / Medium / Ultra for Qwen3.6 (Ultra is a gateway mode and cannot be hidden).

Both app config write paths (`config set --batch-file` and `config.patch`) preserve the hidden-level settings and pass the exact readback check. Existing installs need a provider-entry migration so an upgrade does not hit the "changed outside the companion" repair state.

## Trade-offs to decide

- **Default effort drops** for Qwen3.8 from xhigh to medium (the gateway default). In return, switching between Medium and Off reuses the prompt cache instead of re-prefilling the agent prompt (about 21 s on an RTX Spark), because the Qwen3.8 template writes the effort level at the top of the system prompt.
- **Gateway floor rises to v2026.6.5**, since older gateways reject the level-hiding setting. Only native-gateway installs are affected; WSL setup installs the latest gateway.
- Phones can still switch Effort to Low through voice transcripts and the iOS share extension. That needs an upstream gateway change.

## Validation so far

Proven end to end through real gateways 2026.9.8, 2026.10.2 and 2026.10.5 beta on Linux with an RTX 4090, using a small stand-in model loaded with the real Qwen chat templates.

Not yet tested: the real catalog models, Windows, the app's own Effort UI and canvas path, and llama-server router mode under `auto`.

body:
Windows Companion 2026.9.8-1; Gateway MSIX 2026.10.900.0; CLI 2026.10.9. Native isolated-session-v1 setup, without SSH or a managed WSL Gateway.

Agent chat works and browser.proxy is approved. However, requesting tabs with the user browser profile fails: “Browser control authentication was blocked because the local listener owner could not be verified.”

Restarting the Gateway restored basic connectivity. Changing the security preset from Locked Down to Recommended did not resolve the browser error.

Source review suggests that the non-SSH browser authorization callback requires ResolveManagedDistroName, while that method returns null for native-package Gateways. Could this reject a valid native Gateway? This is our analysis, not a maintainer-confirmed diagnosis.

Please confirm a supported fix or compatible version combination that preserves existing conversations and settings without disabling ownership verification. Related reports: #1333 and #1691.

body:
Closes #1956

Original fix by @MertBasar0. Current evidence: Mert's checksummed Windows report at **e4affd6a3d996af83e6d4bb7957aae8898cd674d**. Metadata-only update; no new commit.

**Not merge-ready. S06 passed; S05 and S18 are still open; Finding 4 is explicitly out of scope.**

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Companion keeps starting at logon after **Start with Windows** is turned off, when the installer's startup task was selected.

## User Impact

User impact: the installer's startup choice uses the registration Settings manages. The tested migrated path can be turned Off and stays Off through same-version repair. Existing unquoted Run entries remain a limitation (Finding 4 below).

Behavior to review:
- The "Start when Windows starts" task is offered on a fresh install only.
- An upgrade moves an enabled Startup folder shortcut to the Run value when the destination approval and command are compatible. Windows-disabled, unreadable, or unrecognized entries are retained without enabling a new startup identity. A user whose toggle was off while the shortcut kept launching sees the toggle **On** after the upgrade, which is what was really happening, and can now turn it off.
- At startup an unpackaged build raises the stored preference to `true` only for this executable's enabled installer Run command. Scheduled-task presence alone never enables an Off preference. It never lowers an enabled preference.

## Why This Change Was Made

Old owner: `installer.iss` created a `{userstartup}` shortcut that no other code reads or removes. New owner: the `HKCU\...\Run` value that `AutoStartManager` already reads and deletes. Legacy migration still requires an existing owned, argument-free entry. Only its Run output quoting changed; task migration, ordering, approval guards and uninstall remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Windows 11 Home build 26200, x64, tr-TR, unsigned Dev build at e4affd6. Candidate installer SHA-256: AAC2ED073D911329AEEAB86768E5FE777CABF4767547D5F58B5C83BA08197599. Baseline: a4dd026cc5f85a444a0fcd05eef5b86282dbda8c.

| Case | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| S00, baseline | Mert clicked Off; stored False, legacy shortcut retained. Visible On was read before the click; visible Off was not read after the window closed. |
| S03 | Shortcut migrated to quoted Run. After launch: visible On via UI Automation, stored True. |
| S04 | Real Off click: visible Off, stored False, Run removed; task/shortcut absent. Same-version repair and relaunch preserved the state. |
| OBS-494 | Argument-free migration now produced quoted Run and raised stored AutoStart, resolving Finding 3. |

The agent reports full installed/publish hash matches for the executable and managed DLLs; displayed hashes are shortened. Dev identity verified. S04 is not logon or future-release upgrade proof.

### Shortcut-ownership P2 follow-up

At 0700f09f, StartupShortcutIsInstallerOwned reads the .lnk through WScript.Shell before any Run write or shortcut deletion. Only this installation's executable with no arguments or exactly --background is migrated; retargeted, customized-argument and unreadable links are preserved and logged. The published tree is identical to Mert's 1cbd43b8/7cc96f55 candidate. Mert reports Windows 11 validation: the new regression fails on ff341166 and InstallerIssAssertionTests passes 26/26; build.ps1 succeeds; Tray 5082/5082; Shared 4924 passed with two reported host-only failures (tr-TR casing and symbolic-link privilege); Test-InstallerScriptCompiles.ps1 -RequireCompiler compiles x64, arm64 and DevBuild. A real .lnk WScript.Shell probe accepted original no-argument/--background links and rejected retargeted, extra-argument, corrupt and missing links, including corrupt links returning empty TargetPath. **Live installer runs of the customized-shortcut cases were not performed.** These native results are supplied by Mert, not newly executed in this publication turn.

## Change Type

## Required proof pools

- `windows-clean-installer-upgrade`: the install and upgrade path changed. Not run here; it needs exact signed artifacts.
- `windows-winui-interactive`: the value the Settings toggle shows can change at startup. Not run here.

## Validation

Local merge of e4affd6 with main 4aee38a1 (Windows 11 build 26200): build.ps1 exit 0; Tray tests 5081 passed, 0 failed; Test-InstallerScriptCompiles -RequireCompiler compiles x64, arm64 and x64 DevBuild; Shared tests 4924 passed, 2 failed (the same two host-only failures as before: no symlink privilege, and ExecReusableCommandBinderTests.PinnedCarrier_IgnoresShadowInsertedAfterApproval). The handshake test that failed in CI passes.

### User-provided native Windows results at e4affd6

- ./build.ps1 and validate-docs.ps1: exit 0.
- Tray: **4818 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Focused startup/installer tests: **64 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Shared: **4806 passed, 2 failed, 26 skipped**. Reported host failures: ExecReusableCommandBinderTests.PinnedCarrier_IgnoresShadowInsertedAfterApproval (long computer name) and MxcFolderAdmissionTests.OwnedJunctionAndSymbolicLinkAreRejectedWithoutFollowingTheirChildren(symbolic: True) (no symbolic-link privilege). No Shared product code changed.
- Test-InstallerScriptCompiles.ps1 -RequireCompiler: **native Windows exit 0** for x64, arm64 and x64 DevBuild. Candidate Dev installer built successfully.
- setup-dev -CheckOnly passed on an earlier SHA, not repeated here.

Earlier agent-side checks: 49 focused Linux passes, pre-fix regression failure, clean diff and P0-P3 review; real Inno under Wine compiled three variants. Full Linux suites did not pass. These are separate runs, not an all-green claim.

## Real Behavior Proof

| Scenario result |
| --- |
| S06 PASS (negative logon after Off). After Mert's reboots, Shell-Core event 9707 recorded no Run start for OpenClawTray-Dev on three boots: 2026-11-02 (observed about 2 h 53 min, 7 other Run starts), 2026-11-03 (second reboot, same state), 2026-11-05 (4 other Run starts). No Run value, shortcut or task, stored AutoStart=False, Dev log unchanged, no Dev process. |

### Current-head scope

Current cases were reset and rerun at e4affd6; older SHA results remain historical. Mert performed the clicks; UI Automation read toggle states, without screenshots. The S00 log's FAIL line was a closed-window read, not a demonstrated product failure; visible Off was not captured in that baseline case.

With Mert's approval, click cases used EnableMcpServer=true in Dev settings to bypass first-run setup in local-only mode. No Gateway, pairing or credentials were used; this differs from a default profile. Isolation/fixture variables were checked in the launching process tree, not independently in the child. No -Isolated autostart proof is claimed.

S01/S02/S09/S10/S13/S19 and S12-A passed. S14/S15 and S12-D/E/F are labeled fixture proof. S07/S08/S12-B/C fixtures do not fulfill Windows-UI state creation. Uninstall removed a retained shortcut but left Windows-owned approval metadata; this is an observation, not a new failure.

### Not verified or blocked

- S05: NOT_RUN. The positive logon control needs the toggle On and another reboot; scheduled with Mert.
- S18: wizard not run. S07/S08/S12-B/C still need Windows-UI state creation.
- S11: disabled-task creation denied (0x80070005). S16/S17: no approved disposable environment for permission tests.
- Same-version repair is not future-release upgrade proof. Signed-artifact/latest-stable upgrade proof and formal pools remain incomplete.
- Stored AutoStart=true without registration still stays true; On alone is not registration proof.

The Dev install is retained for S05. Release state and distros were reported preserved. Evidence is supplied report/log excerpts; public screenshot/artifact links verified: N/A.

### Finding 4: known limitation, explicitly out of scope

An **already unquoted owned Run command with --background** is not normalized. With a no-space path and stored AutoStart=false, upgrade/launch leaves it active and the stored toggle value False. If an enabled legacy shortcut exists too, both remain because the destination fails exact-command comparison. The original symptom can therefore remain for these users.

This PR stops the corrected argument-free migration from creating that form; it does not repair existing argument-bearing entries. Frequency is unknown. Finding 4 is excluded by agreed scope, not claimed fixed. Suggested On-then-Off recovery was not tested and may leave the shortcut. No new commit was made for it.

body:
Closes #1957

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: autostart turned on during setup opens the Companion window at logon when the session is not elevated, and setup can report that it could not confirm a task it did create.

## User Impact

User impact: every autostart registration now starts quietly in the tray. Setup no longer rejects the app's own scheduled task.

Behavior to review: `MatchesExpectedTask` now requires `--background`. A legacy task with no arguments counts as `Different`, the same answer it gives for any other command line.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserved invariant: `docs/CONNECTION_ARCHITECTURE.md` says new autostart registrations pass `--background`. The Run key fallback in `ApplySetupPreferenceAsync` was the one writer that did not, and that fallback is the normal path without elevation, because `schtasks /Create /SC ONLOGON` is refused. `MatchesExpectedTask` required empty arguments while `CreateRegisterProcessStartInfo` always registers `--background`, and its test fixture used empty arguments, so nothing caught the mismatch. `CreateBackgroundLaunchCommand` is now the single owner of that command.

## Evidence

Windows 11 x64 build 26200, standard session without elevation:

```text
schtasks /Create /SC ONLOGON /HRESULT exit: 0x80070005
```

The updated tests against the baseline matcher, with the arguments the app really registers:

```text
Failed OnlyExactEnabledStartupTaskCountsAsCompletedRegistration(changed: "expected", matches: True)
Failed OnlyExactEnabledStartupTaskCountsAsCompletedRegistration(changed: "no-arguments", matches: False)
```

They pass with this change. `ActivationRouterTests` already pins that an unpackaged launch with no arguments opens a window and that `--background` does not.

- Shared tests: 4809 passed, 2 failed, 26 skipped. Both failures come from this host and are in code this PR does not touch: `ExecReusableCommandBinderTests.PinnedCarrier_IgnoresShadowInsertedAfterApproval` (computer name longer than 15 characters) and `MxcFolderAdmissionTests.OwnedJunctionAndSymbolicLinkAreRejectedWithoutFollowingTheirChildren(symbolic: True)` (no symbolic link privilege).

## Upgrade compatibility

This change touches no stored settings. `settings.json`, `AutoStart` and the gateway registry are read and written exactly as before. It changes only two things: the command a new autostart registration writes, and which existing scheduled task setup accepts as its own. Every registration an earlier release can leave behind:

| Existing registration (who wrote it) | After upgrade, before any toggle or setup | Next setup or Settings apply |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run value `"<exe>" --background` (Settings toggle) | Unchanged. Still starts in the background. Toggle reads On. | Rewritten to the same value. |
| Run value `"<exe>"` (setup fallback before this fix) | Unchanged. Still starts at logon, still with a window. Toggle reads On (`IsAutoStartEnabled` checks only that the value exists). | Setup: registration is rejected on a standard account and no task exists, so the value is rewritten with `--background`. Settings Off then On also rewrites it. #1964's installer migration also rewrites this exact value with `--background` (proven live at e4affd6). |
| Task `"<exe>" --background` (created since #1541) | Unchanged. Starts in the background. | Previously `InspectStrict` reported `Different` for setup's own task, so setup could reject its own correct registration. Now `ExpectedEnabled`. This is the fix. |
| Task `"<exe>"` with no arguments (created before #1541, needs elevation) | Unchanged. Still starts at logon. `Exists` still reports it, so the toggle reads On. | `/Create /F` replaces it with the `--background` task whenever registration succeeds. If registration is rejected, `InspectStrict` now reports `Different` and setup shows its existing "could not be confirmed" warning instead of accepting a task that opens a window. No fallback Run value is created. Turning autostart off still unregisters it (`Different` != `Absent`). |

Nothing stops loading or working. The only behavior difference for old data is that setup no longer silently accepts the pre-#1541 argument-free task.

Tests covering these rows:
- `StartupTaskInspectionTests.OnlyExactEnabledStartupTaskCountsAsCompletedRegistration` covers `--background` matches, plus the `no-arguments` and `arguments` cases.
- `SetupStartupPolicyTests.ConfirmedRejectionStillRequiresExactTaskInspection` and `AmbiguousRegistrationNeverCreatesRunKey` cover `Different`: a throw with no Run key.
- `DisableRequiresBothRunKeyRemovalAndSuccessfulTaskRemoval` covers unregistering any present task.

Fixes: the Tray test command that `AGENTS.md` requires writes into the developer's real Companion profile unless the `OPENCLAW_TRAY_*` variables are set first.

## User Impact

User impact: no end-user change. A developer or agent who runs `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj` beside a real installation no longer gets fixture files in it.

Behavior to review: the tests now always run with `AppIdentity.IsIsolated` true, as they already do in CI, which sets `OPENCLAW_TRAY_DATA_DIR`. Values the caller already set are kept.

## Why This Change Was Made

Production code falls back to `%APPDATA%` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%` when these overrides are unset, so isolation depended on remembering them. `AGENTS.md` asks for it, but its own required command does not set them. A module initializer runs before any test and cannot be forgotten.

Before, on `a4dd026` beside an installed Companion, one plain run created `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\device-key-ed25519.json` and added fixture chat-state files and about 2660 log lines under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray`.

| Alpha build, `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_CHANNEL=alpha` (#1642) | Prereleases skipped, no update offered | The newest alpha or stable release with a compatible asset is selected and activated for download and install |

body:
## Summary

When setup turns on **Start with Windows** in a session without elevation, the registration it falls back to has no `--background`. Companion then opens its window at every logon instead of starting quietly. A second defect in the same path makes setup report that startup registration could not be confirmed, even when the app's own task is in place.

## Cause

**Run key without the argument.** A logon scheduled task needs elevation here, so `schtasks /Create` is refused and setup falls back to the Run key. The two writers in `AutoStartManager` disagree:

```csharp
// ApplySetupPreferenceAsync, the setup path
key.SetValue(AppName, $"\"{exe}\"");
// SetUnpackagedAutoStart, the Settings path
key.SetValue(AppName, $"\"{exePath}\" --background");
```

`docs/CONNECTION_ARCHITECTURE.md` says new autostart registrations pass `--background` to remain quiet, and `ActivationRouterTests` pins that an unpackaged launch with no arguments opens a window. `installer.iss` already migrates this exact argument-free value to `--background`, but only during an upgrade, and setup can write it again afterwards.

**Strict check that rejects the app's own task.** `WindowsStartupTaskRegistration.MatchesExpectedTask` requires empty arguments, while `CreateRegisterProcessStartInfo` always registers `--background`. `InspectStrict` therefore returns `Different` for a task the app created. It matters when `schtasks` times out or returns an unclassified error after creating the task: `SetupStartupPolicy.ApplyUnpackaged` throws "Windows startup registration could not be confirmed". The existing test fixture uses empty arguments, so it did not catch this.

## Evidence

Windows 11 x64 build 26200, main `a4dd026`, standard session without elevation:

```text
schtasks /Create /SC ONLOGON /HRESULT exit: 0x80070005
```

Tests against the baseline matcher, using a task description with the arguments the app really registers:

```text
Failed OnlyExactEnabledStartupTaskCountsAsCompletedRegistration(changed: "expected", matches: True)
Failed OnlyExactEnabledStartupTaskCountsAsCompletedRegistration(changed: "no-arguments", matches: False)
```

## Fix I have ready

One shared `CreateBackgroundLaunchCommand` for the scheduled task and both Run key writers, and `MatchesExpectedTask` now requires `--background`.

## Not verified

- I did not complete the setup wizard and log on again, so the window at logon comes from the code and the router test, not from watching it happen.
- The strict check's failure path was tested through the matcher, because a logon task cannot be created on this machine without elevation. The new round-trip test exits early when Windows refuses the task, as it does here, so it only proves something on an elevated host.

I found no existing issue or PR for this. I will open a PR.

body:
## Summary

If "Start OpenClaw Companion when Windows starts" was selected in the installer, Companion keeps starting at logon after the user turns **Start with Windows** off. An upgrade can also bring the startup entry back.

## Cause

There are two separate autostart registrations, and only one of them is managed.

| Owner | Registration | Settings can see it | Settings can remove it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `installer.iss`, `startupicon` task | `{userstartup}\OpenClaw Companion.lnk` | No | No |
| `AutoStartManager` | `HKCU\...\Run` value and logon scheduled task | Yes | Yes |

`AutoStartManager.SetUnpackagedAutoStart(false)` and `SetupStartupPolicy.ApplyUnpackaged(false, ...)` delete only the Run value and the scheduled task. The setup wizard's startup choice goes through the second one, so it cannot remove the shortcut either.

Inno also inherits earlier task selections on an upgrade, so a shortcut the user deleted by hand comes back.

## Reproduce

Unsigned Dev installers built from main `a4dd026`, Windows 11 x64 build 26200, on the Dev identity. The Settings toggle binds to `SettingsData.AutoStart`, so I set the state the toggle stores, launched the installed tray with `--background`, and read the state back.

```text
installed with /TASKS=startupicon, AutoStart set to false
settings.json AutoStart (the Settings toggle): False
startup shortcut: True; Run value: absent

shortcut deleted by hand, then a silent upgrade
startup shortcut: True; Run value: absent
```

## Fix I have ready

- The installer task writes the same Run value that Settings manages, with `--background`, instead of a shortcut.
- The task is offered on a fresh install only, so an upgrade cannot turn autostart back on.
- An upgrade moves an existing shortcut to the Run value and removes the shortcut.
- At startup an unpackaged build reports an existing registration in the toggle, so a user who turned the toggle off before the upgrade sees **On** and can really turn it off. It never lowers an enabled preference.

Results with the fix, on the same setup:

```text
fresh install with the task
startup shortcut: False; Run value: "<app>\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe" --background

fresh install without the task
startup shortcut: False; Run value: absent

baseline with the shortcut and AutoStart false, then upgrade
startup shortcut: False; Run value: <app>\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe --background
log: Auto-start setting corrected from False to True to match Windows.
settings.json AutoStart (the Settings toggle): True

Run value removed, then a silent upgrade
startup shortcut: False; Run value: absent
```

## Not verified

- I did not click the toggle in the UI or reboot. That the toggle removes the Run value comes from reading `SetUnpackagedAutoStart`.
- Signed artifacts.

I found no existing issue or PR for this. I will open a PR.

body:
## Summary

`winget uninstall` removes the local WSL gateway without asking. The distro and everything inside it are gone, with no prompt and no way to keep them. The README tells users they will be asked.

This needs a product decision, because `DEVELOPMENT.md` documents the silent behavior on purpose: "A silent uninstall (`/SILENT`, `/VERYSILENT`) always removes the gateway."

## Why I think the default should change

- `installer.iss` already says why the dialog defaults to **No**: removing the WSL gateway "is destructive and unrecoverable", and someone uninstalling in order to reinstall "must not lose their gateway by pressing Enter". A silent uninstall skips that protection and picks the destructive answer.
- A silent uninstall is what package managers do by default. Companion is on winget as `OpenClaw.OpenClawCompanion`, and winget uses the entry's `QuietUninstallString` (`unins000.exe /SILENT`) unless the user passes `--interactive`.
- Someone running `winget uninstall` to reinstall, or a fleet script removing the app, did not ask to delete a gateway and its workspace.
- #1461 (`feat(migration): gate Inno-to-Store migration preview and preserve the gateway on uninstall`) already moved one silent case toward preserving, but only where a Store app is registered.

## Reproduce

Unsigned Dev installers built from main `a4dd026`, Windows 11 x64 build 26200. I registered a throwaway `OpenClawGateway-Dev` distro with `wsl --import`, read `QuietUninstallString` from the entry, and ran exactly that command.

```text
QuietUninstallString: "<app>\unins000.exe" /SILENT
distro registered before: True
still in Installed apps: False; distro registered after: False
```

## Options

1. **Keep the gateway on a silent uninstall, and let an unattended caller ask for removal** with `/RemoveLocalGateway=yes`. This is my recommendation. Nothing is lost by default, and the removal stays available to scripts. Scripts that rely on today's behavior would need the new switch.
2. **Keep today's behavior and correct the docs.** Add the warning to the README and the winget description. This changes no code, but the data loss stays.

I built option 1 and ran it on the same setup:

```text
QuietUninstallString: "<app>\unins000.exe" /SILENT
still in Installed apps: False; distro registered after: True
log: Silent uninstall: preserving the OpenClawGateway-Dev WSL distro and generated state. Pass /RemoveLocalGateway=yes to remove them.

unins000.exe /VERYSILENT /RemoveLocalGateway=yes
distro registered after: False; install folder left: False
log: Silent uninstall: /RemoveLocalGateway=yes requested local gateway cleanup.
log: Local gateway cleanup completed successfully.
```

## Not verified

- I did not run the `winget` command itself. The Dev entry does not appear in `winget list` on my machine, and running it on the real package would remove my installed Companion. The steps above run the same registered command winget reads. `winget uninstall` on a throwaway machine would confirm the last link.
- Signed artifacts, and a distro with a real Gateway inside it.

Which option do you want? Option 1 is ready as a PR once it is agreed.

body:
## Summary
The native Windows client (`OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`) repeatedly crashes with an unhandled `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.LayoutCycleException` ("Element is already the child of another element"). After the crash the process stays alive and keeps receiving Gateway WebSocket events, but its main window is destroyed (`MainWindowHandle = 0x0`), so the app appears open (tray icon / taskbar) while **no window can be focused or typed into**. The web Control UI keeps working fine.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 Famille 10.0.26300 (x64)
- Gateway / CLI: OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (build fe06181)
- Windows package (Tray): `OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw_rfcbke2p71se2` (MSIX, C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\...)
- Gateway: ws://127.0.0.1:18789 (loopback local mode), healthz = {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
- Process at crash aftermath: PID 36848, SessionId=1, ~590 MB WS, 82 threads, Responding=True, MainWindowHandle=0x0

## Steps to reproduce
1. Launch OpenClaw Companion on Windows 11, connected to a local Gateway.
2. Open a chat session with a large history / large agent response (session `agent:main:dashboard:47e8905e-5015-4518-aff3-6a64a8acd832`, "Réflexion Objectifs", model mistral-large-4).
3. Immediately before each crash the log shows:
`[GatewayClient] Sending frame: sessions.patch [GatewayClient] Sending frame: chat.history Wizard response payload kind=Object len=438296 [ERROR] CRASH UnhandledException: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.LayoutCycleException`
4. After the crash: click the app in taskbar/tray → window frame may appear but input fields are dead / window cannot take focus. `Get-Process` shows MainWindowHandle=0x0.

## Expected
The WinUI window survives rendering large chat payloads; a layout cycle should be caught/logged without killing the main window, or the UI should be recreated automatically.

## Actual
Unhandled LayoutCycleException destroys the main window. The process remains alive in tray-only mode (still connected to the Gateway), so Windows still shows the app as running — but there is no usable window.

## Crash log (5 occurrences, 2026-10-18 → 2026-10-31)
`[2026-10-18 22:52:16.431] UnhandledException [2026-10-19 11:45:14.131] UnhandledException [2026-10-19 22:41:51.130] UnhandledException [2026-10-25 12:01:18.824] UnhandledException [2026-10-31 11:26:27.601] UnhandledException Microsoft.UI.Xaml.LayoutCycleException Element is already the child of another element.`

## Log files (paths on the reporter machine)
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenClawFoundation.OpenClaw_rfcbke2p71se2\LocalCache\Local\OpenClawTray\crash.log` (5 entries)
- same dir: `openclaw-tray.log` (~4.5 MB, rotated `.old` 5 MB) — crash at line ~26676
- same dir: `last-chat-state.json`

## Workaround (confirmed)
1. Quit the zombie tray process (tray icon → Quit, or `taskkill /PID <pid> /F`).
2. Relaunch OpenClaw Companion from the Start menu.
3. Avoid reopening the very large session in the Hub until fixed (web Control UI unaffected).

## Additional context
- Not correlated with Gateway restarts (Gateway healthy throughout).
- Each crash is immediately preceded by a large `Wizard response payload` (438 KB) + `chat.history` → suspected XAML layout cycle when rendering a large markdown/tool-result tree in the chat view.
- Suggested fix: guard `LayoutCycleException` in the chat view and recreate the main window on failure; or virtualize/limit the rendered message tree.

body:
## Environment

- Windows 11 (x64), OpenClaw Companion **2026.9.8-1** installed build, native WinUI tray app, gateway connected.
- NVDA, laptop keyboard layout, Caps Lock as the NVDA key.
- Code re-checked against `main` at `a4dd026c`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Settings page: change any option and save. A confirmation bar appears at the top; NVDA stays silent.
2. Permissions page with MCP enabled: copy the MCP token or URL. A short status line changes; NVDA stays silent.
3. Connection page: run a connection action ("Test", "Repair") and watch the status text change; NVDA stays silent.
4. Cron page: expand or collapse a job card; NVDA is not told whether the card opened or closed.

## Actual behavior

Results of user initiated actions are visible but not announced. A screen reader user has to move focus back and hunt for a changed sentence after every save, copy or connection attempt.

## Root cause

`main` raises live region events in only two places:

- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ChatCopyButton.cs:134`
- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Windows/StoreMigrationWindow.xaml.cs:109`

There are no `RaiseNotificationEvent` calls in the repository. Most result surfaces are InfoBars whose `IsOpen` is set to `true` while the control is still collapsed, or plain `TextBlock`s. In both cases NVDA drops the event: a collapsed element has no automation peer yet, and a `LiveRegionChanged` on a text block is often ignored.

## Expected behavior

When a user action finishes, the result is announced once, with the right urgency (polite for success, assertive for errors), without moving focus.

## Proposed solution

Add a small helper, for example `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Helpers/AutomationAnnounce.cs`, with two entry points:

```csharp
internal static void OpenInfoBar(InfoBar bar)
{
    bar.IsOpen = false;
    bar.Visibility = Visibility.Visible;
    FrameworkElementAutomationPeer.CreatePeerForElement(bar);
    bar.IsOpen = true;
}

internal static void Notify(FrameworkElement element, string? message = null)
{
    var peer = FrameworkElementAutomationPeer.FromElement(element)
        ?? FrameworkElementAutomationPeer.CreatePeerForElement(element);
    if (peer is null) return;
    message ??= AutomationProperties.GetName(element);
    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(message) && element is TextBlock text) message = text.Text;
    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(message)) return;
    peer.RaiseNotificationEvent(
        AutomationNotificationKind.ActionCompleted,
        AutomationNotificationProcessing.MostRecent,
        message,
        "OpenClawStatus");
}
```

`OpenInfoBar` follows the InfoBar guidance: a property change while the bar is open does not raise a notification, so close and reopen it.

Wire it into the places that currently set `IsOpen = true` or replace a status string:

- `Pages/SettingsPage.xaml.cs` (saved settings bar),
- `Pages/ConfigPage.xaml.cs`, `Pages/ChannelsPage.xaml.cs` (existing InfoBars),
- `Pages/SandboxPage.xaml.cs` (unavailable action bar),
- `Pages/CronPage.xaml.cs` (job completed bar, form error, and expand/collapse announcement using the job name),
- `Pages/DebugPage.xaml.cs` (copy feedback bar),
- `Pages/PermissionsPage.xaml.cs` (MCP copy status),
- `Pages/ConnectionPage.xaml.cs` (gateway action status, after the panel is made visible),
- `Windows/WorkspaceWindow.xaml.cs` (operation info bar).

Keep `AutomationProperties.LiveSetting="Assertive"` on error surfaces and `Polite` on success surfaces, matching the existing markup.

## Validation plan

- Source contract tests in `tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests` that assert the announcement helper is used instead of bare `IsOpen = true` for the listed surfaces.
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj -c Debug -p:Platform=x64`
- Manual NVDA pass over Settings save, MCP copy, connection actions and Cron expand/collapse.

## Scope

Screen reader access only. No localization content is requested in this issue.

body:
## Environment

- Windows 11 (x64), OpenClaw Companion **2026.9.8-1** installed build, native WinUI tray app.
- NVDA, laptop keyboard layout, Caps Lock as the NVDA key.
- Code re-checked against `main` at `a4dd026c`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Bindings page: focus the refresh button (top right). NVDA announces nothing useful, only "button".
2. Config page: focus the save / discard row and the per-row remove buttons. Save is unnamed, remove says only "Remove item" in English from its tooltip.
3. Usage page: scroll the provider and daily tables. NVDA reads `OpenClawTray.Pages.UsagePage+ProviderRow` and `OpenClawTray.Pages.UsagePage+DailyRow`.
4. Sessions page: focus the session list. NVDA reads `PART_ItemsView` instead of a list name.
5. Settings page: focus the eight notification checkboxes one by one. Each has a good label, but nothing says they are one group of notification preferences. The same happens with the four clipboard options in Sandbox.

## Actual behavior

- The bindings refresh button and the config save button are built from a `StackPanel` with an icon and a text block, so they have no accessible name.
- Usage list rows fall back to the data type name, because `ProviderRow` and `DailyRow` do not override `ToString()`.
- The sessions list has no name.
- Groups of related options are not announced as groups.

## Expected behavior

Every focusable control has a name that matches its visible label, list rows read their data, and related option groups say what they are.

## Root cause

- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/BindingsPage.xaml`: `RefreshButton` content is `StackPanel { FontIcon, TextBlock }`, no `AutomationProperties.LabeledBy` or `Name`.
- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/ConfigPage.xaml`: `SaveButton` has the same shape.
- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Controls/SchemaConfigEditor.xaml.cs`: the remove button is icon-only and only gets a tooltip.
- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/UsagePage.xaml.cs`: `ProviderRow` and `DailyRow` (around lines 340 and 348) have no `ToString()`, so the list item name falls back to the type name.
- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/SessionsPage.xaml`: `SessionListView` (line 110) has no `AutomationProperties.Name`.
- Settings notification checkboxes and Sandbox clipboard options live in plain panels. Panels have no automation peer, so setting a name on the panel would not be announced.

## Proposed solution

1. Bindings and config buttons: point `AutomationProperties.LabeledBy` at the visible label, the pattern already used in `ConfigPage.xaml` for the search box:
   ```xml
   AutomationProperties.LabeledBy="{Binding ElementName=RefreshButtonLabel}"
   ```
   and give the inner `TextBlock` `x:Name="RefreshButtonLabel"`. Do the same for `SaveButtonLabel`.
2. Schema editor remove button: set `AutomationProperties.Name` from the localized string and reuse it for the tooltip.
3. Usage rows: add `public override string ToString()` on both row types, joining the visible columns (date, plan, usage, status). This is the cheapest fix and needs no new resource keys.
4. Sessions list: `AutomationProperties.SetName(SessionListView, ...)` in the constructor, using the existing sessions heading key.
5. Option groups: add a small `AutomationGroup : StackPanel` control whose automation peer reports `AutomationControlType.Group` and forwards its children's peers (otherwise the children disappear from the tree). Wrap the notification checkboxes and the clipboard radio buttons, and set the group name from the existing heading text, trimming the trailing colon. This gives one "group" announcement, not one per item.
6. Tests:
   - source assertions in `tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests` for the new `LabeledBy`, `ToString()` overrides and group control usage;
   - a UI Automation proof that dumps the affected pages and asserts every focusable control has a non-empty name and no name matches `\+.*Row$`.

## Validation plan

- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj -c Debug -p:Platform=x64`
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Tray.UITests --no-build -c Debug -r win-x64 --filter Category=Accessibility`
- Manual NVDA pass over Settings, Bindings, Config, Sessions and Usage.

## Scope

Screen reader access only. The names should come from the existing visible labels; no translation work is requested in this issue.

body:
## Environment

- Windows 11 (x64), OpenClaw Companion **2026.9.8-1** installed build, native WinUI tray app, gateway connected.
- NVDA, laptop keyboard layout, Caps Lock as the NVDA key. NVDA does not offer browse mode outside web content, so all reading must come from UI Automation items.
- Code paths below re-checked against `main` at `a4dd026c`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Companion window with a conversation that contains at least two messages.
2. Press `Tab` until focus reaches the chat history. NVDA announces "Chat messages" and nothing else.
3. Press `Up` / `Down`. Focus does not move between messages and nothing is read.
4. Send a request that runs several tools, expand the activity card, and `Tab` through its rows. Every row is announced with the same name, for example "Tool call exec. Done.".

## Actual behavior

- The whole transcript is one unnamed group. Individual messages are not automation items, so a screen reader cannot read who said what, in order, and cannot reach the copy and read-aloud buttons that live inside each message.
- An expanded activity card lists tool calls that share one automation name, so a list of several calls cannot be followed.

## Expected behavior

- Each message is an automation item: `Tab` enters the list, `Up` / `Down` move between messages, each message announces its sender and text, and `Tab` continues to the per-message actions.
- Each tool call inside an activity announces its position and enough input detail to tell it apart from the others.

## Evidence

UI Automation dump of the main window, gateway connected:

```
[List] name='Chat messages'
  [ListItem] name='ItemContainer' focusable=False
```

Before any fix the only item the reader can reach is the list itself. Expanded activity rows (with several calls) already render this way on `main`:

```
[Button] name='Tool call exec. Done.'
[Button] name='Tool call exec. Done.'
...
```

## Root cause

`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ReactorChatTimeline.cs`:

- line 156: `.IsTabStop(false)` on every `ItemContainer(...)`;
- the container is never given an automation name;
- line 181: only the `ItemsView` is named (`"Chat messages"`);
- `SelectionMode = None` and `IsItemInvokedEnabled = false`, so there is no focus model either.

The text elements inside a row do carry names, but they are plain elements without automation peers, so they never surface as items.

`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ToolCallCardRenderer.cs`:

- line 73: `BuildStandalone(...)` names every expander `"{Chat_Tool_CallLabel} {toolName}. {statusLabel}."`;
- `BuildActivityCore(...)` maps `activity.Tools.Select(tool => BuildStandalone(..., isNested: true))` without any index or input detail, so rows that share one status are identical.

## Proposed solution

1. In the `ItemsView` item factory, build the row content once and derive the container name from it:
   ```csharp
   var content = BuildRow(...);
   var name = content!.Modifiers!.AutomationName;
   ```
   Prefix user messages with a sender label. For activity rows, whose name lives on the inner expander, fall back to a summary built from `row.Activity?.Summary`.
2. Name the container and make it a Tab stop only when it has a name:
   ```csharp
   ItemContainer(Border(content!))
       ...
       .IsTabStop(!string.IsNullOrEmpty(name))
   ```
   then `.AutomationName(name)` for non-empty names.
3. Keep the `ItemsView` name so the user still hears the list itself.
4. Add two resource keys in all six resource files: a user sender label (`Chat_Timeline_UserSenderLabel`) and an activity summary format (`Chat_Activity_AutomationSummaryFormat`, with the activity summary and the tool count).
5. For tool calls: add `int position = 0, int total = 0` to `BuildStandalone`, keep `"Tool call <name>. <status>."` as the stable prefix, then append an ordinal (new key `Chat_Tool_CallPositionFormat`, value like `{0} of {1}`) and the first line of the input (trimmed to about 120 characters with an ellipsis). Pass `index + 1` and `activity.Tools.Count` from `BuildActivityCore`.
6. Tests:
   - extend the source assertions in `tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/ChatTimelinePresentationTests.cs` for the new calls and keys;
   - in `tests/OpenClaw.Tray.UITests/ReactorToolActivityProofTests.cs`, assert that the nested rows have distinct automation names;
   - in the same project, add a proof that dumps `ControlType.ListItem` names from the chat window and checks focusability.
7. Existing proof tests that match `"Tool call Bash. Done."` exactly (`NativeToolIdentityScreenshotProofTests.cs`) need prefix matching because of the suffix.

## Validation plan

- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj -c Debug -p:Platform=x64`
- `dotnet build tests/OpenClaw.Tray.UITests/OpenClaw.Tray.UITests.csproj -c Debug -r win-x64` and the focused UI proof tests with `OPENCLAW_REPO_ROOT` set.
- Manual NVDA pass: Tab into the list, Up/Down through messages, Tab to copy/read-aloud, expand an activity and arrow through the tool rows.

## Scope

Screen reader access only. No localization content is requested here; the two new resource keys are keys the automation names need, with English values provided by the implementer, and translations can follow the repository localization process.

body:
## Summary

With a WSL Gateway and the Windows Companion, there is no supported way to run a Windows-only stdio MCP server. Photoshop MCP is one example. The same MCP server works when launched directly on Windows. The Gateway can only start stdio MCP commands inside the WSL distro, where Windows COM and other Windows-only backends are unavailable. The Windows node does not advertise any MCP execution capability.

This is a host/topology gap. It is not a Photoshop or MCP server crash.

## Environment

- RTX Spark N1X, Windows ARM64
- Gateway 2026.9.7 (c074824) in the `OpenClawGateway` WSL distro
- Windows Companion 2026.9.5 (diagnostic build)
- Photoshop 2026, running on Windows
- [alisaitteke/photoshop-mcp](https://github.com/alisaitteke/photoshop-mcp) 1.7.25 (commit `fc7c9d6c`), stdio transport, Node.js 22 on Windows ARM64

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set up a local WSL Gateway with the Windows Companion paired as a node.
2. Build photoshop-mcp on Windows and confirm it works directly. `initialize` and `tools/list` succeed (125 tools), `photoshop_ping` returns "Successfully connected to Photoshop", and `photoshop_get_state` returns the open document.
3. Try to register it with OpenClaw using `openclaw mcp add`.

## Expected

A supported registration path launches the Windows stdio MCP on the Windows host and routes tool calls to it, with approval controls and a tool allowlist. At minimum, OpenClaw should state which topology is supported and give an actionable message when a Windows-only MCP cannot be hosted.

## Actual

- `openclaw mcp add` accepts only a Gateway-local stdio command or an HTTP URL. There is no option to run the command on a Windows node.
- The Gateway distro's `/etc/wsl.conf` disables automount and interop (`enabled=false`, `appendWindowsPath=false`), so the Gateway cannot launch Windows executables.
- `openclaw nodes status --json` shows the Windows node connected with `canvas`, `device`, `screen`, `stt`, `system` and `tts` capabilities. It has no MCP capability, no `mcp.tools.call.v1` command, `sessionHost=false` and `nodePluginTools=[]`.
- The MCP's executor supports only Windows and macOS. A Linux process cannot use Windows COM, and the MCP's loopback UXP bridge is not an HTTP MCP endpoint.

## Notes

The native Windows Gateway may remove this limitation because stdio MCP commands would run on the Windows host. That has not been validated for this scenario. Related but separate: #1717 covers Gateway cleanup and restarts after removing an unavailable MCP server.

Note: tracked internally as NVBug 6850792.

body:
## Summary

On an RTX Spark N1X system with 64 GB of memory, the Local AI model picker does not offer Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B. Only Qwen models are listed. The device reportedly falls short of Bolt's roughly 31 GB requirement, but the picker gives no indication that Bolt exists or why it is unavailable.

## Environment

- NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X, 64 GB installed memory, Windows ARM64
- Windows 11 Pro 26H1, build 28000.3231
- NVIDIA driver 621.01
- OpenClaw from the Microsoft Store, WSL Gateway (app-managed `OpenClawGateway` distro)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw from the Microsoft Store and start first-run setup.
2. Select **Install a local Gateway (WSL)** and wait for Gateway setup to finish.
3. Select **Local AI on this PC**.

## Expected

Nemotron 3.5 Bolt appears in the model list on 64 GB RTX Spark devices. If it cannot run on this configuration, the picker should say so and explain why, instead of hiding it.

## Actual

Only Qwen models are listed. Bolt does not appear and no reason is shown.

## Notes

`LocalInferenceEligibility.CanOffer` only offers Bolt for fresh selection when the device is `Eligible` with a currently fitting profile of 128K context or more. `Assess` also rejects Bolt when free GPU memory is unknown or the GPU is not on the qualified Bolt list. On a 64 GB unified-memory device, any of these checks may hide Bolt. The exact rejection reason on this device has not been captured yet.

Questions to settle:
- Should Bolt be supported on 64 GB RTX Spark SKUs, perhaps with a reduced context profile?
- If not, should the picker show Bolt as unavailable with a reason?

body:
Closes #1937

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the first Local AI message after the app starts or restarts its llama-server takes 5-16 s, because the whole OpenClaw system prompt and tool definitions (about 14k tokens with the real Gateway) are processed again before the model answers. Later messages in the same server run take 0.25-0.4 s.

## User Impact

User impact: after a restart, the first message reuses the system prompt the model already processed instead of computing it again, so the first-message wait drops by roughly half on the measured setup (see Evidence). Later messages are unchanged.

Things to know:
- The managed llama.cpp runtime moves from b11320 to b11700. Existing installs recorded against b11320 keep working (retired entry) until setup upgrades them, and the upgrade downloads the new runtime archive.
- The Tray now serves Local AI through a loopback proxy inside the app. `OPENCLAW_LOCAL_AI_PREFIX_CACHE=0` turns that off and goes straight to the router as before.
- Up to 4 saved prefix files (about 0.4-1.2 GB each, depending on the model) are kept under `LocalAI\prefix-cache`.

## Why This Change Was Made

llama-server can save and restore a slot's KV state, but it does not choose what to save. The app owns the llama-server process, so it keeps the prefix state on disk keyed by a hash of the launch profile, model, system/developer messages and tools, and restores it when the server starts. Four commits:

1. `build(local-ai)`: runtime b11320 to b11700. Needed because b11700 writes context checkpoints into saved slot files; on hybrid models (Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8, Nemotron Bolt) a state restored from b11320 cannot be reused (the server logs "forcing full prompt re-processing"). b11700 is the build the Nemotron Bolt runtime already pins; archive sizes and SHA-256 were recomputed from the downloaded archives.
2. `feat(local-ai)`: file store (keeps the newest 4) and slot save/restore client.
3. `feat(local-ai)`: the loopback proxy. Everything is forwarded unchanged and streamed, except a chat with a leading system prefix while nothing else is running: it restores the saved prefix, or runs the prefix alone and saves it, then forwards the real request unchanged. Any failure is logged and the request is forwarded anyway.
4. `feat(local-ai)`: runtime wiring. The router runs on an internal port, the proxy owns the published endpoint, and after the router is healthy the proxy restores the newest saved prefix in the background.

**Open decision for review:** step 4 restores at start, which loads the model at app start. Measurements (below) show this helps a user who waits about 20 s (1.7-2.0 s first message) but makes a message typed immediately after launch 2-5 s slower than no cache, and it can restore the wrong prefix when the Gateway has sent a second prefix. The author's recommendation is to leave it off by default (one line) and refresh a file's timestamp whenever its prefix serves a request; the first-message restore alone is already a clear win. This draft keeps it on, as requested, until that is decided.

## Evidence

Real Gateway, real prompt (not a synthetic prefix). RTX Spark (Windows ARM64), the real WSL Gateway (OpenClaw 2026.10.8) sending a plain "hi", the real install (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MTP UD-Q4_K_S, 98,304 context, the app's preset exactly as written). The prefix (system prompt plus 12 tools) is about 14.1k tokens. Time to first token:

| Scenario | b11320 | b11700 |
|---|---|---|
| No cache, first "hi" after a start | 6.5 s | 5.5 s |
| First "hi" after a full restart, restored on that message | 6.8-7.2 s (full re-prefill, no benefit) | 2.6-3.3 s |
| Prefix already loaded, any later "hi" or new session | 0.35-0.40 s | 0.24-0.34 s |
| Saved file | 298-339 MB | 454-493 MB |

With restore at start (this PR as written), b11700:

| Scenario | TTFT |
|---|---|
| Wait for the restore, then "hi" (x3) | 1.7-2.0 s |
| "hi" immediately after launch, with the cache (x3) | 14.5-17.3 s |
| "hi" immediately after launch, no cache (x3) | 12.3-14.6 s |

After a 5-turn session with the default 32 checkpoints, a fresh session's first "hi" took 0.54 s with the prefix checkpoint restored.

<details>
<summary>Details and other measurements</summary>

body:
## Problem

When the app starts (or restarts) its local llama-server, the first chat message has to process OpenClaw's entire system prompt and tool definitions again before the model can answer. llama-server keeps that prefix in memory, so every later message in the same server run is fast, but the cost is paid again on every server start.

With the real OpenClaw Gateway, that prefix (system prompt plus 12 tools) is about 14k tokens. Measured on an RTX Spark (Windows ARM64) with the real WSL Gateway sending a plain "hi":

| | Time to first token |
|---|---|
| First "hi" after a server start | 5.5-6.5 s (full prefill of ~14.1k tokens) |
| Any later "hi", same server run | 0.25-0.4 s |

On a larger model the gap is wider. With Nemotron Bolt and a synthetic 10.7k-token prefix the full prefill took about 16 s.

## Expected

After a restart, the first message should reuse the previously processed system prompt instead of computing it again.

## Notes from investigation

- llama-server can save and restore a slot's KV state to disk (`POST /slots/{id}?action=save|restore`). It does not decide what to save or key the files by prompt, so the client has to.
- On hybrid models (Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8, Nemotron Bolt) a restored state is only reusable if the saved file includes the recurrent-state context checkpoints. The pinned runtime b11320 does not write them (a restored state is thrown away: "forcing full prompt re-processing"). b11700 does.
- The system prompt is byte-identical across fresh sessions for the main agent request, but its size changes with Gateway state (53,165 vs 44,341 characters in two runs), and the Gateway occasionally sends a request with a different prefix (about 43.8k characters, 11 tools). A single slot can only hold one prefix at a time.
- Restoring a saved prefix costs about 2-2.5 s for a ~450-500 MB file, and the first request after a model load has its own warmup cost, so this removes most of the prefill but not all of the first-message latency.

## Proposal

Keep the system-prompt prefix's KV state on disk, keyed by a hash of what makes it valid, and restore it when the server starts. This needs the runtime moved to b11700 or newer. A PR follows.

Native geometry drives the asynchronous scroll. Recycling before an offset is issued retries normal layout; recycling after issuance preserves the valid native correlation instead of endlessly replacing the request. If the settled target was lost, a generation-fenced retry resolves live coordinates after anchor retention.

Owned native completions, including canceled brings and replaced offsets, are distinguished from reader navigation. Reader completion cancels pending retries and supersedes a still-issued tail offset at the observed reader position. Each new explicit history request establishes a native boundary so an older reader completion cannot cancel the newer jump. Correlation ordering and wrap handling follow the SDK's [31-bit counter implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/blob/d8915cf00984489da2541fc2328818ec23baa466/controls/dev/ScrollPresenter/ScrollPresenter.cpp#L3331), with focused boundary/wrap coverage.

+  request native target geometry asynchronously
+  preserve issued offsets when their containers recycle
+  retarget lost settled anchors using live coordinates
+  honor current reader navigation; fence stale completions

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three related problems with the managed-local WSL gateway trust check:

- It failed closed on unsigned modern Store WSL `wslrelay.exe`.
- It accepted a fake `wslrelay.exe` planted in a WSL-named folder nested inside another package's `WindowsApps` directory.
- When relay binary trust stayed unproven but the managed distro confirmed the gateway, the only signal was a log line.

## User Impact

User impact:

- Genuine unsigned Store WSL (2.6.3+) relays connect instead of failing the relay trust check.
- A nested `WindowsApps` spoof can no longer be treated as the expected managed gateway or receive the shared gateway credential.
- When Windows cannot fully verify the relay but the WSL distro confirms the gateway, Settings > Connection shows a Warning banner with the verifier's reason. Before this change the only signal was a log line.

## Why This Change Was Made

Modern Store WSL ships `wslrelay.exe` without a per-file Authenticode signature. To handle that, `WindowsAuthenticodeVerifier` gained a package-level fallback (commit `93a4d246`, dual-reviewed). It grants trust when three conditions hold:

1. The relay is at a canonical path.
2. A matching `Get-AppxPackage` identity exists.
3. The path ACL is admin-protected.

When that evidence is unavailable, the verifier returns a warning instead of failing, and the managed distro ownership probe must corroborate the gateway.

**Nesting spoof (finding R1 of the advisory review).** The original fallback checked only the relay's immediate parent directory name, so `WindowsApps\Other.App_...\MicrosoftCorporationII.WindowsSubsystemForLinux_9__8wekyb3d8bbwe\wslrelay.exe` passed. `IsWslPackageRootRelay` now accepts only `{WindowsApps}\{WSL package directory}\wslrelay.exe`: the WSL-named directory must be the package root, and the relay must sit directly in it. Review findings R2-R8 are intentionally not addressed here.

**Visible warning.** The warned state was previously detected by searching `Detail` for a log phrase. The verifier reason now travels as a typed field:

`GatewayEndpointProvenance.RelayTrustWarning` → `EndpointCredentialAuthorization.RelayTrustWarning` → `GatewayConnectionSnapshot.ManagedRelayTrustWarning` → `ConnectionPagePlan.RelayTrustWarningDetail` → the `RelayTrustWarning` InfoBar.

`GatewayConnectionManager` owns the warning's lifecycle:

- **Sets it:** on connect and on node-only connect.
- **Refreshes it:** on every allowed operator credential handoff. The refresh runs in the background, so the handshake never waits on the transition lock.
- **Clears it:** at the start of each connect attempt, on disconnect, and when a later handoff is denied.

The copy is localized in all six locales.

## Evidence

- **Nesting spoof, red/green:** `VerifyMicrosoftSignedFile_WslNamedDirectoryNestedInsideAnotherWindowsAppsPackage_IsRejected`, with Protected and Unverifiable path evidence. On the unfixed verifier both cases returned `IsTrusted=true`; after the fix both are rejected.
- **Warning lifecycle, red/green:** `ManagedRelayTrustWarning_PublishesOnConnect_RefreshesOnHandoff_ClearsOnDisconnect` runs for the device-token and shared-token credential paths. With the handoff observer removed, both cases time out.
- **Denied handoff, red/green:** `ManagedRelayTrustWarning_ClearsWhenLaterHandoffIsDenied` times out when the clear-on-denied-handoff line is removed.
- **UI:** the fixture app (synthetic Gateway, injected reason) shows the Warning InfoBar while connected and removes it after disconnect. See Real Behavior Proof.
- **Reviews:**
  - An independent rubber-duck review (reviewer agent) of the warning commit `66e0c475` found one P2: the banner went stale after a denied handoff. It also found one P3: ASCII punctuation in the zh-cn/zh-tw copy. Both are fixed in `9521eec1`.
  - A separate rubber-duck review of the R1 commit found no defects.
- **Not exercised:** no malicious installed package, other-user attack or credential disclosure was demonstrated. The verifier proof uses synthetic paths with injected seams.

body:
## Summary

With the native (MSIX / Store) Gateway, a cold boot leaves Companion permanently "not connected" until the app is restarted. The startup connect happens exactly once, and it is rejected while the Gateway package is still in the `starting` state. Nothing reconnects afterwards — not the WebSocket backoff, not the operator reconnect scheduler, and not the managed-local auto-repair monitor.

The fix is not user error and not a timing coincidence: the Gateway needs ~150 s to become reachable after boot, and the one-shot startup attempt lands inside that window every time.

## Environment

- Windows 11, Companion v2026.9.8-1 (latest release), installed from the MSIX/Store package
- Gateway: native MSIX package, `isolated-session-v1` runtime contract, endpoint `ws://127.0.0.1:54610/`
- Companion autostarts on logon; the Gateway package also starts on its own at boot
- Verified the same code exists on `main` (c59652f) and on tag `v2026.9.8-1`, so this is shipped behavior, not an outdated build

## Steps to reproduce

1. Reboot the machine with the native Gateway installed and Companion set to autostart.
2. Let both start on their own (Gateway takes ~150 s to open its HTTP/WS listener).
3. Open Companion.

## Expected

Companion shows "connecting" and connects on its own once the Gateway is ready (the readiness budget already exists: `IsolatedGatewayRuntime.StartupTimeout` = 180 s by default).

## Actual

Companion stays disconnected indefinitely. Restarting the app makes it connect within seconds.

### Evidence from `openclaw-tray.log` (offsets from Gateway start)

| Offset | Event |
| --- | --- |
| T+0 | Gateway package starts (its own `gateway.json` records the start) |
| T+77 s | Companion tray starts |
| T+79 s | `Connecting to last successful gateway during startup: ws://127.0.0.1:54610/ (identity.DeviceToken)` — and then **nothing** |
| T+148 s | Gateway log: `[gateway] ready` |
| T+163 s | User restarts Companion |
| T+169 s | `Connecting to gateway: ws://127.0.0.1:54610/` |
| T+173 s | `Handshake complete (hello-ok)` |

The diagnostic signature matters: the failed attempt logs **no** `Connecting to gateway:` line, **no** `Loaded Ed25519 device identity`, and **no** error line at all. The connect pipeline never reaches the WebSocket layer, so there is nothing to retry.

## Root cause

### 1. The startup connect is one-shot

`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs` — `TryConnectGatewayIfCredentialAvailable(...)` calls `_connectionManager.ConnectAsync(record.Id)` once during startup and only observes the task for faults. There is no scheduler behind it.

### 2. The pipeline refuses a Gateway that is still booting

`GatewayConnectionManager.ConnectCoreAsync` (`src/OpenClaw.Connection/GatewayConnectionManager.cs:434`) calls `AuthorizeCredentialForEndpointAsync` → `NativeGatewayEndpointSecurity.AuthorizeAsync` → `IsolatedGatewayRuntime.EnsureRunningCoreAsync`:

`src/OpenClaw.Connection/NativeGateway/IsolatedGatewayRuntime.cs:105`

```csharp
if (status.State is "not-started" or "stopped")
{
    ...
    status = await StartAndWaitAsync(package, endpoint.Port, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
}

if (status.State != "running" || status.Port != endpoint.Port)
    throw new NativeGatewayContractException(
        "The package-managed Gateway is not running on Companion's selected port. " +
        "Check clawctl gateway-service status before connecting.");
```

The state vocabulary (`src/OpenClaw.Connection/NativeGateway/NativeGatewayPackageClient.cs:150`) is `running`, `not-started`, `stopped`, `starting`, `unhealthy`, `unknown`.

So a Gateway that is **already booting on its own** reports `starting`, which:

- does not enter the `not-started`/`stopped` branch that would wait, and
- fails the `!= "running"` check and throws immediately.

`StartAndWaitAsync` already knows how to poll `starting`/`unhealthy` until ready (`IsolatedGatewayRuntime.cs:212`) with a bounded budget, but that loop is unreachable from a `starting` state.

### 3. The rejection parks the connection in Error and returns

`GatewayConnectionManager.cs:445`

```csharp
if (!endpointAuthorization.Allowed)
{
    _stateMachine.TryTransition(ConnectionTrigger.ConnectRequested);
    ...
    _stateMachine.TryTransition(...ConnectionTrigger.WebSocketError..., endpointAuthorization.Detail);
    _diagnostics.Record("setup", "Blocked strong credential before managed-local endpoint ownership was proven", ...);
    EmitStateChanged();
    return;
}
```

No client is created, so no WebSocket attempt, no `connecting` log line, no error log line — exactly the observed signature.

### 4. No retry path covers this failure

- `WebSocketClientBase.cs:381` schedules `ReconnectWithBackoffAsync` only after a socket was actually attempted.
- `IOperatorReconnectScheduler.ScheduleOperatorReconnect` (`GatewayConnectionManager.cs:3341`) exists only for `OperatorReconnectReason.PostBootstrapHandoff` and operator-token recovery.
- `ManagedLocalGatewayAutoRepairMonitor` deliberately ignores native records: `WslKeepAlivePolicy.IsSetupManagedLocalRecord` → `GatewayRecord.ResolveManagedDistroName` returns `null` when `NativePackageFamilyName is not null` (`GatewayRecord.cs:195-199`, comment: "A native gateway's display name must never confer legacy WSL ownership"). The in-app self-heal therefore never runs for the native Gateway.

## Suggested fix

Minimal, two changes:

1. **`IsolatedGatewayRuntime.EnsureRunningCoreAsync`**: treat `starting` (and `unhealthy`) as a pending start and enter the existing bounded readiness poll instead of throwing. E.g. factor the status loop out of `StartAndWaitAsync` into `WaitForRunningAsync` and call it for both the `not-started`/`stopped` branch and a `starting`/`unhealthy` pre-state. A cold boot within `StartupTimeout` then simply succeeds.
2. **`ConnectCoreAsync`**: for a native record whose authorization failed with `GatewayErrorKind.Network` and a `NoListener`/`UnknownListener` provenance, schedule one bounded retry (new `OperatorReconnectReason`, reusing the existing backoff helper) instead of parking in `Error` forever.

A unit test with a fake package client returning `starting` then `running` (in the style of the existing `IsolatedGatewayRuntime` tests) would lock this in.

## Workaround

A logon wrapper that polls `http://127.0.0.1:54610/health` and only launches Companion once the Gateway answers, plus a bounded watchdog that relaunches Companion if it does not connect, works reliably. That is what I am using now, but it is a shim for a state the client should handle itself.

## Notes / limits

- The evidence is from logs plus the source above; I did not instrument the running app, so the exact provenance kind at the failure instant is inferred from the silent branch and the code path rather than read out of the state snapshot.
- No secrets, tokens, device ids or user names are included in this report.
