body: ## Summary The Windows uninstall registration for the Inno-installed Companion (`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\{M0LTB0T-TRAY-4PP1-D3N7}_is1`) keeps the **version and install date of the first install** after the app is upgraded, both by the built-in updater and by running a newer `OpenClawCompanion-Setup-x64.exe`. Settings → Apps and anything that reads this key (support checks, inventory tools, and possibly the Store migration's previous-installation validation, see #1592) see a version that no longer exists. #1592 notes that "the earlier update sequence that produced the stale registration has not been established"; this report documents one such sequence. ## Environment - Windows 11 Home, build 10.0.26300, x64; per-user Inno install in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray` - Inno Setup version recorded in the key: 6.7.1 ## Sequence observed (one machine, all dates 2026) | Date | Action | Exe version afterwards | Uninstall key afterwards | |---|---|---|---| | Oct 3 | Fresh Setup install, **v2026.9.5-alpha.93** | 2026.9.5-alpha.93 | DisplayVersion `2026.9.5-alpha.93`, InstallDate `20261003` | | Oct 5 ~19:59 | Ran **`OpenClawCompanion-Setup-x64.exe` for v2026.9.5-alpha.97** over the existing install (signature valid, SHA-256 matched the release asset) | 2026.9.5-alpha.97 | **unchanged**: still `2026.9.5-alpha.93` / `20261003`, although `unins000.exe`/`unins000.dat` in the install folder were rewritten at 2026-10-05 19:59 (so Setup did run) | | Oct 7 21:00 | Built-in updater: "Update available: v2026.9.8-1" → Download → "Installing update and restarting..." | **2026.9.8-1** (`2026.9.8-1+2ba89f37…`, signature Valid, OpenClaw Foundation) | **unchanged**: still `2026.9.5-alpha.93` / `20261003` | | Oct 7 21:04 | Windows reboot | 2026.9.8-1 | **unchanged** | Current key (non-sensitive fields): `DisplayName = OpenClaw Companion version 2026.9.5-alpha.93`, `DisplayVersion = 2026.9.5-alpha.93`, `InstallDate = 20261003`, `MajorVersion = 2026`, `MinorVersion = 9`, `Publisher = OpenClaw Foundation`, `InstallLocation = %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\`, `Inno Setup: Setup Version = 6.7.1`. ## Likely causes (two paths) 1. **Built-in updater:** `App.xaml.cs` configures Updatum with `InstallUpdateSingleFileExecutableName = "OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI"`, so the in-app update replaces the program files directly rather than running the Inno installer, and nothing rewrites the Inno uninstall key. Every in-app update widens the gap between the registration and the real version. 2. **Setup reinstall:** a newer Setup run over an existing install rewrote `unins000.*` but did not refresh `DisplayVersion`/`DisplayName`/`InstallDate` in the existing `_is1` key. I haven't determined why (installer script settings vs. Inno behavior with this AppId). ## Expected After any successful upgrade path, the uninstall registration reflects the installed version (at least `DisplayVersion`/`DisplayName`), so Settings → Apps, support diagnostics and the Store migration's previous-installation checks see the truth. ## Suggested direction (maintainers' call) - After an in-app update succeeds, refresh `DisplayVersion`/`DisplayName` (and optionally `MinorVersion`/`InstallDate`) in the Inno `_is1` key, or have the updater run the signed Setup package instead of replacing files. - Check that the Setup script updates the existing uninstall key on reinstall. - For #1592: if migration validation reads this key, validate against the executable's version (or both), since the key can be stale. Screensnip of the previous version showing in Windows' "Settings"->"Apps"

Fixes: a failed welcome suggestion click disables the other chips.

## User Impact

User impact: after a welcome chip send fails, the other chips can be clicked. A chip stays disabled only while its send is in flight, or until the thread that was sent shows a user row.

## Why This Change Was Made

The click set `firstSendInFlight` and did not look at the send result. The flag cleared only when the compose-target timeline already had a user row. On a new empty chat, a send that returned false left the flag set.

## Evidence

Head `304928e0051da0ddf419c9a48499273b8e71b0f1`. A disposed host can still observe a provider acceptance. That result is not a failed submission, so welcome recovery does not run. Recovery runs only when the host is still live and the provider rejected the send. It removes only the failed queue card for that welcome submission id. It clears the timeline only when the turn is idle, nothing is queued, sending, or failed, and the timeline is exactly one user row with that text plus status lines. A queued follow-up, a failed same-text follow-up, an active turn, or a second user row stays in place.

body:
## Summary
On an alpha install, **Check for updates** always reports "No updates available", even when a newer alpha has been published. The updater only asks GitHub for the repository's *latest* release, and GitHub's latest-release endpoint never returns pre-releases. So an alpha user stays on their alpha until a newer *stable* release ships, and "up to date" is misleading in the meantime.

## Environment
- OpenClaw Companion **2026.9.5-alpha.93** (installed with the Setup installer, not the Store/MSIX; the update check runs, see the log below)
- Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200
- Newest published pre-release: **v2026.9.5-alpha.97** (2026-10-03T18:55:21Z, `prerelease: true`, not a draft, includes `OpenClawCompanion-Setup-x64.exe` and `OpenClawTray-2026.9.5-alpha.97-win-x64.zip`)
- Repository "latest" release (`GET /repos/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/releases/latest`): **v2026.9.4** (2026-09-15)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install any alpha, e.g. v2026.9.5-alpha.93.
2. Wait for a newer alpha to be published (e.g. alpha.97).
3. Click **Check for updates**.

**Actual:** "No updates available" / status `Current`.
**Expected:** Either the newer alpha is offered, or the UI states that alpha builds don't self-update and points to the Releases page.

## Log evidence (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\openclaw-tray.log`)
```
[2026-10-05 08:23:52.470] [INFO] Manual update check requested
[2026-10-05 08:23:52.470] [INFO] Checking for updates...
[2026-10-05 08:23:52.770] [INFO] No updates available
```
`settings.json` has no update-channel or pre-release setting (checked all 70 keys), so this isn't configuration drift.

## The alpha channel is set and displayed, but the updater ignores it
- The Windows **user environment variable `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_CHANNEL=alpha`** is set on this machine.
- **Settings → About → App info** shows **Version v2026.9.5-alpha.93** and **Update channel: alpha**, right next to the **Check for updates** button that then reports no update *(screenshot in the comment below)*. The label is read from that variable:
  [`SettingsPage.xaml.cs` L206-L207 @ 7127c16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7127c16d537cf9d2d92012cc0c16ea6d3c7c73a7/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/SettingsPage.xaml.cs#L206-L207)
- The developer launcher documents it as the prerelease switch, in [`run-app-local.ps1` L44-L45](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7127c16d537cf9d2d92012cc0c16ea6d3c7c73a7/run-app-local.ps1#L44-L45): *"Set OPENCLAW_UPDATE_CHANNEL for this launch. Use alpha for prerelease update testing…"*
- But **nothing in the update path reads `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_CHANNEL`**. Across the repo at 7127c16 it's referenced only by the Settings label and `run-app-local.ps1`. So the UI tells the user they're on the alpha channel while the updater stays on stable.

## Root cause
1. **The app pins Updatum to the latest release only**, and leaves `AllowPreReleases` at its default (`false`):
   [`App.xaml.cs` L46-L50 @ 7127c16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7127c16d537cf9d2d92012cc0c16ea6d3c7c73a7/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs#L46-L50)
   ```csharp
   internal static readonly UpdatumManager AppUpdater = new("openclaw", "openclaw-windows-node")
   {
       FetchOnlyLatestRelease = true,
       InstallUpdateSingleFileExecutableName = "OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI",
   };
   ```
2. **In Updatum 1.3.4** (the version referenced in `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.csproj` L119), `FetchOnlyLatestRelease` calls `Release.GetLatest(...)`, and pre-releases are skipped unless `AllowPreReleases` is set:
   [`UpdatumManager.cs` L629](https://github.com/sn4k3/Updatum/blob/1.3.4/Updatum/UpdatumManager.cs#L629) and [L644](https://github.com/sn4k3/Updatum/blob/1.3.4/Updatum/UpdatumManager.cs#L644)
   ```csharp
   var release = await GithubClient.Repository.Release.GetLatest(Owner, Repository)...
   ...
   || (!AllowPreReleases && release.Prerelease)) // Skip pre-releases if not allowed
   ```
   GitHub's latest-release endpoint returns the most recent **non-pre-release, non-draft** release (currently v2026.9.4). Because v2026.9.4 is older than 2026.9.5-alpha.93, Updatum reports no update.
3. **The app's fallback path also excludes pre-releases** by design (stable-correction ordering):
   [`UpdateCheckPipeline.cs` L164-L166 @ 7127c16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/7127c16d537cf9d2d92012cc0c16ea6d3c7c73a7/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/UpdateCheckPipeline.cs#L164-L166)

So there's currently no code path by which an alpha install can be offered a newer alpha.

## Suggested direction (maintainers' call)
- **Option 0, wire up the existing knob:** when `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_CHANNEL` is `alpha`, configure Updatum with `FetchOnlyLatestRelease = false` and `AllowPreReleases = true` (and let the fallback pipeline accept pre-releases on that channel). The Settings label would then match the real behavior.
- **Option A, alpha channel follows the build:** when `AppVersionInfo.Version` has a pre-release label, set `FetchOnlyLatestRelease = false` and `AllowPreReleases = true`, so alpha installs track alphas and stable installs stay on stable.
- **Option B, explicit opt-in:** an "Update channel: Stable / Alpha" setting that switches the same two Updatum properties.
- **Option C, minimum:** if alpha self-update isn't intended, have alpha builds show "Alpha builds don't auto-update; see Releases" instead of "up to date".

Side note: the same panel shows **Install type: Unpackaged (developer)** for a normal Setup-installer install. `SettingsAppInfoProjection.InstallKind` maps every non-MSIX install to that label, even though this install runs the regular release update check. A plain "Unpackaged" or "Installer" label would avoid suggesting it's a dev build.

Related context: `docs/VERSIONING.md` notes that alpha release objects older than 30 days are deleted, which makes it more likely that alpha users end up on stale, unpublished builds without being told.

---
*Reported by @Speculorum9. Investigation done with Claude Code (read-only: local settings and log files, GitHub API, source review).*

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the tray keeps growing when a host system.run command prints output faster than its timeout.

## User Impact

User impact: host command output now stops at 4 MiB by default. The process is killed, the result is marked timed out, and stderr includes `[output truncated]` instead of every line printed so far.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sandbox path already stops at the 4 MiB output setting. Host fallback called the local runner with no cap, and that runner appended every stdout and stderr line until the process exited. The runner now reads bytes with one UTF-8 decoder, keeps a character only when the whole character fits, and stops the process when the cap is crossed. Host fallback copies a caller-supplied cap onto the fallback request. Null and non-positive caps use the 4 MiB default.

Stopping the process is the behavior on this head. ClawSweeper recommends draining the rest of the output and letting the command finish. That choice is still open for a maintainer. This update does not change it.

## Evidence

Current head `b6fbbb473187fcd8c2ac8999de403616210247b3`, worktree `C:\Users\sebta\wt-wn-f029`. The host runner is `LocalCommandRunner`.

Unterminated flood. PowerShell writes 256-byte blocks and never exits. Cap 4096, timeout 15 seconds.

```
timedOut=true exit=-1 durationMs=223 stdoutBytes=4096 stderrBytes=18 newlines=0
stderr=[output truncated]
```

Split UTF-8. PowerShell writes bytes F0 9F, flushes, waits 200 ms, then writes 98 80. Cap 64.

```
timedOut=false exit=0 durationMs=404 stdoutBytes=4 stderrBytes=0
stdout=U+1F600 replacement=false
```

Truncation boundary. The same four-byte character with cap 3 does not fit, so nothing is kept. Cap 4 keeps that character and drops the following byte.

```
cap=3 timedOut=true exit=-1 durationMs=183 stdoutBytes=0 replacement=false stderr=[output truncated]
cap=4 timedOut=true exit=-1 durationMs=179 stdoutBytes=4 stdout=U+1F600 stderr=[output truncated]
```

Small command. `cmd.exe /C echo hi`, cap 4096.

```
timedOut=false exit=0 durationMs=25 stdoutBytes=2 stdout=hi marker=false
```

MCP on this same Debug tray. Isolated data directory, `SystemRunSandboxEnabled` false, exec approvals security full and ask off. `winnode --list-tools` exited 0 and listed `system.run`. `system.run` with `cmd.exe /d /s /c echo hi` returned:

```
{"stdout":"hi","stderr":"","exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"success":true,"durationMs":30}
```

The tray log for that call says `sandbox=disabled; routing system.run through host runner` and `Exit=0 Duration=30ms TimedOut=False Stdout=2chars Stderr=0chars`.

The same MCP `system.run` then started a PowerShell loop that writes forever. The tray log says `Output exceeded 4194304 bytes; stopping process`, then `Exit=-1 Duration=346ms TimedOut=True Stdout=4194304chars Stderr=18chars`. `winnode` did not print that body: the captured NUL bytes expand past its 16777216 byte response buffer. The tray log is the result. Stderr is 18 characters, the truncation marker.

Before this cap, the same style of flood kept 87998 bytes, `timedOut` false, exit 0, and an empty stderr. That transcript is from the earlier head `bf03b06fe82f4c304ce369025d2791c718755320`, not from this byte reader.

body:
## Summary

#1281 stopped offering Qwen3.5 9B. Since then, the smallest model offered by default (Qwen3.8 27B) needs about 21.6 GiB at its smallest profile, so Local AI is unavailable on 12 and 16 GiB GPUs. This PR brings 9B back as an offered, auto-recommended and launchable model with the full set of 8 context/KV profiles, **only** while `OPENCLAW_LOCAL_AI_DEV_LOW_MEMORY_MODELS=1` is set in the process environment. With the variable unset, behavior is unchanged.

It also carries two related pieces of work on the same branch:

- **User recipe overrides** (`feat(local-ai): add user recipe overrides and a sweep benchmark`): `LocalAI\recipe-overrides.ini`, when present, is merged into the generated llama-server preset on every start and restart. `[*]` applies to every model and `[<model-id>]` wins over it; a key replaces the generated value in place or is appended, and an empty value removes it. An invalid file fails startup with `recipe-overrides.ini line N: ...` on the Local AI page. `scripts/bench-local-ai-recipe.ps1` sweeps candidate override sets against the installed llama-server and writes `results.csv` plus a `best-overrides.ini` delta.
- **Setup connect latency** (`perf(setup): cut connect-phase latency from ~78s to ~31s`): drops fixed post-approval and grace sleeps, adds `ISetupPairingRequests` with CLI and operator-WebSocket transports, and reuses the finalize connection for the pending-approval drain.

### Security fixes in the latest revision

- **Override validation is now an allowlist, not a deny-list** (review P1). llama.cpp's preset parser resolves every argument alias, so `no-ag = false` (the negated `-ag` alias of `--agent`) would have enabled the CORS proxy and built-in host tools, and `hft = value` (alias of `--hf-token`) would have supplied a credential the override launch log does not redact. `LocalAiRecipeOverrides` now accepts only canonical long option names from the pinned runtimes' `common/arg.cpp` (b11026 and b11320 have identical alias tables), grouped as safe tuning keys (scheduling, batch, KV cache, speculative decoding, sampling, RoPE/YaRN, GPU placement). A `no-` prefix is honored only for options llama.cpp defines a negated form for. `scripts/bench-local-ai-recipe.ps1` mirrors the same allowlist.
- **Operator finalization takes its own approval baseline again** (review P1, #1523 regression). The latency commit had reused the setup-wide pre-connect baseline, so a pairing request minted after initial pairing but before finalization was absent from it and the ID-less approval fallback could approve that stale request. `FinalizeOperatorForTray` now captures a fresh device baseline immediately before the finalization socket opens (`VerifyEndToEndStep.CaptureFinalizationApprovalBaselineAsync`), using the CLI transport, without reintroducing the removed grace-period wait.

`LocalModelCatalog` (first commit):
- Adds `DevelopmentLowMemoryModelsEnvironmentVariable` / `DevelopmentLowMemoryModelsEnabled`. The variable is read on every call and only `"1"` enables it.
- Renames the hidden 9B list to `s_developmentModels`. 9B becomes an explicit alternative with `RecommendationPriority` 100, which ranks it below every production model, so it is only picked when none of them fit.
- With the guard on, `Models`, `ExplicitAlternatives`, `Find` and `GetProfiles` return the 9B-inclusive view. With it off, 9B is still only resolvable through `FindInstalled`, with its single native F16 profile.
- Rebased onto current main, which additionally retired the 48GB-SKU IQ4_XS quantization: `FindInstalled` now resolves both `s_legacyModels` (retired receipts keep the Spark-48GB profile they were installed under) and `s_developmentModels`.
- The launch check is strict: a 9B receipt with a reduced profile fails receipt validation in any process that doesn't see the variable. Nothing is silently remapped.
- Test isolation: `tests/TestIsolation/LocalAiDevelopmentGuardReset.cs` is a `[ModuleInitializer]` that clears the variable before tests run, so a developer's user-level setting can't flip guard-off assertions. It is linked into every test project through `tests/Directory.Build.props`.
- Documents the variable in `DEVELOPMENT.md`.

Resulting 9B picks: a 16 GiB GPU gets ctx-131072-f16 (16,069,374,304 bytes), a 12 GiB GPU gets ctx-65536-f16 (12,579,713,376 bytes), and an 8 GiB GPU stays unsupported.

## Required proof pools

- `windows-winui-interactive`: the Local AI availability row and model selector in onboarding change when the guard is set.

## Validation

Current head `303b9986` (rebased onto main `037c17dc` plus the two P1 fixes):

- `./build.ps1`: all builds succeeded, docs validation passed.
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests`: 4266 passed, 0 failed, 36 skipped.
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Connection.Tests`: 1601 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped. Includes 28 `LocalAiRecipeOverrides` tests covering the allowlist: `no-ag`, `ag`, `agent`, `hft`, `hf-token` rejected as "not an allowed llama-server tuning option"; `no-temp`/`no-batch-size` rejected as non-negatable; `-no-ag` rejected as not an option name; `no-context-shift`, `no-kv-offload`, `temp` accepted.
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests` with `OPENCLAW_REPO_ROOT` set: 2294 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped. Includes the new `FinalizationBaseline_ExcludesRequestsThatPredateTheFinalizationSocket` regression test: a request minted between initial pairing and finalization is included in the fresh finalization capture (absent from the setup-wide baseline) and the ID-less fallback then refuses to approve it.
- `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests`: 3996 passed, 0 failed.
- Alias-table ground truth: the allowlist was built by parsing `common/arg.cpp` from both pinned runtimes (b11320 commit `b8f96c3e82284028cb077811ed1666caac3c5bac`, b11026 commit `b49650adb31f2e49a0d76113aeb1792134fd8413`): 357 option groups, 502 alias names, identical across both pins; `-ag` -> `--agent`, `-hft` -> `--hf-token` confirmed in the pinned source.
- Benchmark mirror check: `Assert-OverridableKey` exercised with 13 cases in a throwaway PowerShell harness (attack vectors reject; `batch-size`, `ubatch-size`, `spec-draft-n-max`, `no-context-shift` accept). Scaffold deleted.

## Real behavior proof

Host: NVIDIA TITAN V, 12288 MiB, driver 581.57.

### Guarded 9B selection (earlier revision, unchanged by the security fixes)

Eligibility through `LocalInferenceEligibility.Evaluate(new CudaHostHardwareProbe().Probe())`:

```
guard unset: Unsupported InsufficientGpuMemory qwen3.8-27b-mtp-ud-q4-k-m ctx-65536-q8_0 23183715232 12884312064
guard = 1:   EligibleButBusy None qwen3.5-9b-mtp-q4-k-m ctx-65536-f16 12579713376 12884312064
```

`EligibleButBusy` means the desktop was already using some GPU memory.

Isolated tray (`OPENCLAW_TRAY_DATA_DIR` temp dir, `OPENCLAW_FORCE_ONBOARDING=1`). Text below was read through UI Automation, and screenshots were captured locally:

- Guard = 1:
  - The Gateway chooser shows "Your PC supports Local AI. Run a model locally using your NVIDIA TITAN V."
  - The Local AI review page (Debug `OPENCLAW_SETUP_PREVIEW_PAGE=capabilities-review`, real hardware probe) shows "11.7 GiB required. 12 GiB CUDA-visible on NVIDIA TITAN V." and the model selector shows **"Qwen 3.5 9B (5.9 GB, 64K, F16 KV) (Recommended)"**.
- Guard unset:
  - The Gateway chooser has no Local AI row.
  - The Local AI review page shows "Local AI is not available", and "See why" shows "Hardware: Qwen3.8 27B (UD-Q4_K_M) requires 21.6 GiB of GPU memory for model weights, KV cache, and runtime workspace. OpenClaw detected 12 GiB."

### Override rejection before any effect (current head `303b9986`)

Throwaway console harness referencing the built `OpenClaw.Connection.dll`, driving `LocalAiRecipeOverrides.Load` (the function the launch path calls via `LlamaServerRouterConfiguration.BuildForVerifiedRuntime`, whose `InvalidDataException` is caught in `LlamaServerRuntimeService.StartAsync` before preset publication, logging, or child-process launch):

```
qwen3.8-27b-mtp-ud-q4-k-m: rejected: recipe-overrides.ini line 2: 'no-ag' is not an allowed llama-server tuning option.
qwen3.5-9b-mtp-q4-k-m: rejected: recipe-overrides.ini line 2: 'no-ag' is not an allowed llama-server tuning option.
permitted keys: accepted (2 overrides)
no-agent=true: rejected: recipe-overrides.ini line 2: 'no-agent' is not an allowed llama-server tuning option.
SMOKE PASS
```

(The file also contained `hft = secret-token` on line 3; parsing stops at the first invalid line.) Scaffold deleted.

## Not verified / blocked

- Screenshots are local to the dev host and not attached.
- No end-to-end 9B install and llama-server launch was run on the TITAN V. The pinned CUDA 13 runtime may not support Volta (sm_70). That would be a host/runtime limit, outside this catalog change.
- The finalization baseline fix is proven by unit test (`FinalizationBaseline_ExcludesRequestsThatPredateTheFinalizationSocket`, current head) rather than a full gateway E2E, which needs a real WSL gateway socket on this host; the earlier setup-latency proof (before the fix) measured the full wizard connect phase at ~31s.

body:
## What

Three existing issues each guard a different call site that can start `wsl.exe` during a Windows session-end sequence:

- #1572 — the process-start boundary of the managed-local provenance probe
- #1573 — the tray's keep-alive entry points
- #1574 — the reconnect retry loop

All three need the same input: a reliable, injectable answer to "is a Windows session-end sequence in progress?". **No such source exists in the repository today**, and #1572 deliberately left the concrete Windows wiring out of its scope. As the reviews on #1573 and #1574 note, three independently-defined seams would be incompatible with each other, or would never be wired to anything real.

This issue owns that prerequisite: the abstraction, a concrete Windows source, and its production registration. It is the contract the other three implement against.

## Where

- The contract must be consumable from `src/OpenClaw.Shared` — `WebSocketClientBase.cs` (#1574) lives there, and that assembly must **not** gain a Win32 or tray dependency. Put the abstraction in the shared layer; put the Windows implementation where the host can observe session events.
- A concrete source is `Microsoft.Win32.SystemEvents.SessionEnding`, or the `WM_QUERYENDSESSION` / `WM_ENDSESSION` pair handled on the tray's own window. Either is acceptable; where a window already exists, prefer the message pair, because it lets the process act *before* the session ends rather than only observing that it is ending.

## Required behaviour

1. **One** injectable abstraction answering "is the Windows session ending?", consumed by all three call sites — a single source of truth, no per-call-site re-derivation of the state.
2. A production implementation **actually wired up in the tray host**, not left as a null / always-false default in a released build. A seam that is never connected is worse than none: it looks fixed and is not.
3. Substitutable in tests: forcing "ending" must not require shutting Windows down.
4. Registering it must not change behaviour when no session end is in progress.
5. Do **not** use `Environment.HasShutdownStarted` as the whole answer; on its own it is not reliable evidence that a session-end sequence is in progress.
6. If the mechanism can observe the **transition** (a session end has been requested) and not merely a latched state, expose that. #1574 needs to react to a session end that *begins during* an in-flight backoff wait, and #1572 prefers to decline as early as possible.

## Scope

- Add the abstraction, the Windows implementation and its registration. That is the whole of this issue.
- **Do not** change the three consumer call sites — #1572, #1573 and #1574 own those, and each owns exactly one production file (plus, in #1573's case, the keep-alive cancellation boundary under discussion there).
- **Do not** refactor `AppShutdownCoordinator` or the ordered-shutdown design recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- Do not add a new user-facing setting.

This should stay a small change: one new contract, one new implementation, one registration. Keeping it that small is deliberate — a previous single issue covering all three spawn paths produced a fix artifact that spanned three subsystems and was rejected as too broad for autonomous execution.

## Acceptance

```
./build.ps1
dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore
dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore
dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Connection.Tests/OpenClaw.Connection.Tests.csproj --no-restore
```

## Required regression test

- A test asserting the **wiring is real**: with the host configured as in production, the abstraction the consumers receive is the Windows implementation, not a default no-op. This is the failure mode that otherwise ships silently.
- A test asserting the substitutable path: an implementation reporting "ending" is observed as ending by a consumer, and one reporting "not ending" is observed as not ending — without any real session end.
- The test suite must not require an actual shutdown, a real `wsl.exe`, or WSL to be installed.

## Related

Prerequisite for #1572, #1573 and #1574 — they depend on this contract and should not be closed in favour of it. #1571 is the evidence umbrella for the underlying defect.

## What I can and cannot contribute

- I can confirm the reported behaviour on Windows 11 Home China build `10.0.26300` with OpenClaw Companion `2026.9.4.0`, including the Event 1074 → Event 26 ordering and tray-log excerpts during teardown.
- I do not have a working build environment for this repository, so I cannot run `./build.ps1` or the test projects. Someone else needs to verify.

body:
## What

The WebSocket reconnect retry loop keeps running during a Windows session-end sequence. Its next step is `ReconnectAuthorizationAsync`, which routes through endpoint provenance and can reach the managed-local port probe — the code path that starts `wsl.exe`. Creating that process at teardown fails with `STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED (0xc0000142)` and produces the shutdown "Application Error" dialog recorded as `Application Popup`, **Event ID 26**.

This issue covers **one production file**. It is the third of three spawn paths described in #1571; read #1571 for the evidence trail (the 16-day Event 26 burst census, the tray log excerpts, and why the unrelated `XLGuard.sys` boot popup must be counted separately).

## Where

`src/OpenClaw.Shared/WebSocketClientBase.cs`

- The reconnect retry loop sits around `:594`. It checks disposal, its cancellation token, the reconnect policy and the socket generation, then continues into authorization.
- `ReconnectAuthorizationAsync` is declared at `:156`–`:157` and invoked at `:618`–`:621`:
  `await ReconnectAuthorizationAsync(_cts.Token).ConfigureAwait(false);`
- `_cts` is the client's own token source (`:102`, created at `:228`); it is cancelled by the client's teardown, but that teardown is order-dependent and does not observe a Windows session-end sequence.
- Neither this loop nor the authorization path consults a session-ending signal.

## Scope — deliberately one file

- Change **only** `src/OpenClaw.Shared/WebSocketClientBase.cs`.
- **Do not** change `src/OpenClaw.Connection/ManagedLocalGatewayPortProvenanceService.cs` (separate issue), `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs` (separate issue), or any document/config/schema.
- **Do not** change reconnect backoff, the reconnect policy, or the disposal ordering.
- Do not add a new user-facing setting.

A previous single issue covering all three spawn paths produced an autonomous fix artifact that spanned three subsystems and was rejected upstream as too broad for autonomous execution. Keeping this to one file is the point of the split.

## Required behaviour

1. Once the process has observed that the Windows session is ending, the reconnect loop must **exit before invoking `ReconnectAuthorizationAsync`** — the call at `:621` must not be reached.
2. Normal reconnects are unchanged: with no session end in progress, the loop must behave exactly as today, including its existing token/policy/generation checks.
3. The check must not depend on the client's own `_cts` being cancelled at the right moment; that race is the current gap.
4. The session-ending signal must come from the same injected abstraction used by the other two call sites, so there is one source of truth. If that abstraction is not yet available, code the call site against it rather than re-deriving the state locally.
5. Declining must be logged at the point of refusal.
6. `WebSocketClientBase` lives in a shared library with no window; do not add a Win32/tray dependency to it. Take the signal as an abstraction.

## Acceptance

```
./build.ps1
dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore
```

## Required regression test

In `tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests`, a test that:

- substitutes a session-ending signal that reports "ending",
- drives the reconnect path,
- asserts that `ReconnectAuthorizationAsync` is **not invoked**,
- and that with the signal reporting "not ending" it **is** invoked.

Assert on a substituted `ReconnectAuthorizationAsync` delegate (it is already settable at `:156`), not on a real socket or a real `wsl.exe`.

## What I can and cannot contribute

- I can confirm the reported behaviour on Windows 11 Home China build `10.0.26300` with OpenClaw Companion `2026.9.4.0`, including tray-log lines showing `Connection closed prematurely` followed by `reconnecting in …` during teardown, and the matching Event 1074 → Event 26 ordering.
- I do not have a working build environment for this repository, so I cannot run `./build.ps1` or the test projects. Someone else needs to verify.

body:
## What

The tray's WSL gateway keep-alive can still run its ensure/start path during a Windows session-end sequence. The resulting `wsl.exe` creation fails with `STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED (0xc0000142)`, which is what produces the shutdown "Application Error" dialog recorded as `Application Popup`, **Event ID 26**.

This issue covers **one production file**. It is the second of three spawn paths described in #1571. The first (the provenance probe's process start) is tracked separately; read #1571 for the evidence trail.

## Where

`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs`

- `:956`–`:957` — the keep-alive is started in a **detached** task:
  `var wslKeepAlive = new WslGatewayKeepAliveService(() => _settings, () => _gatewayRegistry);`
  `_ = Task.Run(wslKeepAlive.TryEnsureAsync);`
- `:973` — the managed-local auto-repair adapter invokes `_ => wslKeepAlive.TryEnsureAsync()` and **discards the cancellation token** it is handed.
- `WslGatewayKeepAliveService.TryEnsureAsync` accepts no cancellation token, and can launch WSL after asynchronous preparation — i.e. after the point where a caller could have decided not to.
- The repair monitor that drives `:973` is `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Services/ManagedLocalGatewayAutoRepairMonitor.cs` (5 s poll, 90 s cooldown); it keeps evaluating during teardown. Its `IsTransportUnreachable` path treats a `Connecting` state with no classified error as unreachable, which is exactly the state observed after the WSL VM disappears at session end.

## Scope — deliberately one file

- Change **only** `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs`.
- **Do not** change `ManagedLocalGatewayAutoRepairMonitor.cs`, `ManagedLocalGatewayRepairCoordinator.cs`, `WslGatewayKeepAliveService.cs` beyond what this file's call sites require, or any document/config/schema.
- **Do not** alter the 5 s poll interval, the 90 s cooldown, or the 3-restart budget.
- Do not add a new user-facing setting.

A previous single issue covering all three spawn paths produced an autonomous fix artifact that spanned three subsystems and was rejected upstream as too broad for autonomous execution. Keeping this to one file is the point of the split.

## Required behaviour

1. Once the process has observed that the Windows session is ending, the keep-alive path must **not** start a gateway — the detached task at `:957` and the repair adapter at `:973` must both decline.
2. The repair adapter at `:973` must **honour the cancellation token it is given** rather than discarding it with `_ =>`.
3. Normal operation is unchanged: at startup, and on every managed-local auto-repair while no session end is in progress, the keep-alive must still run.
4. The session-ending signal must come from the same injected abstraction introduced for the provenance probe (separate issue), so there is one source of truth rather than a second ad-hoc check. If that abstraction is not available yet, define the call site against it rather than re-deriving the state locally.
5. Refusal must be logged at the point of refusal so the tray log alone shows why nothing was started.

## Acceptance

```
./build.ps1
dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore
```

## Required regression test

In `tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests`, a test that:

- substitutes a session-ending signal that reports "ending",
- drives the keep-alive entry point (and the repair adapter),
- asserts that **no gateway start was attempted** — and, separately, that the adapter's cancellation token is observed (a cancelled token must also prevent the start).

The test must not launch a real `wsl.exe` or need WSL installed.

## What I can and cannot contribute

- I can confirm the reported behaviour on Windows 11 Home China build `10.0.26300` with OpenClaw Companion `2026.9.4.0`, including tray-log lines showing the keep-alive/reconnect activity during teardown.

## Where

`src/OpenClaw.Connection/ManagedLocalGatewayPortProvenanceService.cs`

- `IsExpectedWslGatewayListening` is declared on the interface at `:32` and implemented at `:97`.
- The probe is started at `:102`: `using var process = Process.Start(probe.StartInfo);`
- The `ProcessStartInfo` is built by `CreateExpectedWslGatewayProbe` at `:120`–`:124`.
- There is a second start in the same file at `:213` (`process = Process.Start(psi);`, psi built at `:202`).
- Callers inside the same file: `:334`, `:361`, `:389`, `:419`.
- Neither start consults any Windows session-ending signal. Searches across `src/`, `tests/` and `docs/` find no `SessionEnding`, `WM_ENDSESSION`, `WM_QUERYENDSESSION`, `SM_SHUTTINGDOWN` or `HasShutdownStarted` implementation.

## Scope — deliberately one file

- Change **only** the process-start boundary in `ManagedLocalGatewayPortProvenanceService.cs`.
- **Do not** touch `docs/`, settings or configuration, schema, or any other project.
- **Do not** change the reconnect loop (`src/OpenClaw.Shared/WebSocketClientBase.cs`) or the keep-alive path (`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs`); those are tracked as separate follow-up issues.
- **Do not** refactor `AppShutdownCoordinator` or the existing ordered-shutdown design recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- Do not add a new user-facing setting.

A previous single issue covering all three spawn paths produced an autonomous fix artifact that spanned three subsystems and was rejected upstream as too broad for autonomous execution. Keeping this to one file is the point of the split.

## Required behaviour

1. Once the process has observed that the Windows session is ending, `IsExpectedWslGatewayListening` must return **without creating a process** — no `Process.Start`, so no `wsl.exe`, so no `0xc0000142` and no Event 26.
2. The same applies to the second start at `:213`.
3. Behaviour when no session end is in progress must be **unchanged**, including the existing "no Windows listener remains, check WSL" path.
4. The session-ending signal must be an **injected abstraction** (an interface or delegate the probe consults), not a direct static call, so a unit test can force "session ending" without shutting Windows down.
   - Wiring a concrete Windows session-end source (`WM_QUERYENDSESSION` / `WM_ENDSESSION` on the tray window, or `SystemEvents.SessionEnding`) is **out of scope here** and belongs to a follow-up. This issue only needs the seam plus a safe default.
   - Do **not** use `Environment.HasShutdownStarted` as the whole answer; on its own it is not reliable evidence that a Windows session-end sequence is in progress.
5. The refusal must be observable in the log at the point of refusal (one line is enough), so a future report can be diagnosed from the tray log alone.

## Acceptance

```
./build.ps1
dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Connection.Tests/OpenClaw.Connection.Tests.csproj --no-restore
```

## Required regression test

In `tests/OpenClaw.Connection.Tests`, a test that:

- substitutes a session-ending signal that reports "ending",
- calls `IsExpectedWslGatewayListening`,
- asserts that **no process was started**.

Assert on the injected seam (the process-runner / start-info factory), not on a real `wsl.exe` — the test must pass on a machine with no WSL and must not launch anything.

## What I can and cannot contribute

- I can confirm the reported behaviour on Windows 11 Home China build `10.0.26300` with OpenClaw Companion `2026.9.4.0`, and I can supply Event 26 / Event 1074 timelines and tray-log excerpts on request.
- I do not have a working build environment for this repository, so I cannot run `./build.ps1` or the test projects. Someone else needs to verify.

title: Tray spawns `wsl.exe` during session teardown, producing an "Application Error 0xc0000142" popup on every shutdown/restart

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal priority bug or improvement with limited blast radius.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦞 diamond lobster
labels.description: Very strong issue quality with high-confidence source-level or clear reproduction.

labels.name: clawsweeper:source-repro
labels.description: ClawSweeper found a high-confidence source-level issue reproduction.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction
labels.description: User-facing flow adds avoidable confusion or support burden without fully blocking progress.

body:
### Summary

When the tray is running (the normal case — it autostarts), shutting down or
restarting Windows frequently pops up a Windows hard-error dialog:

```
wsl.exe - Application Error
应用程序无法正常启动(0xc0000142)。请单击"确定"关闭应用程序。
```

This is `STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED` raised via `NtRaiseHardError`. It happens because
the tray's reconnect timers fire *after* the session has started tearing down, and
each fire spawns a `wsl.exe` that can no longer get a conhost. Nothing is actually
broken — the gateway comes back fine on next boot — but the dialog is alarming and
users reasonably read it as "my system is failing".

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 Home (China), build 10.0.26300 |
| App | OpenClaw Companion 2026.9.4.0 — `D:\OpenClawTray\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe` |
| Distro | app-owned `OpenClawGateway` (base `Ubuntu-24.04`, systemd enabled) |
| Gateway | `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`, loopback + token auth |
| Data | `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\settings.json`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\openclaw-tray.log` |
| Tray autostart | yes; starts 2–4 min after boot |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the tray normally and let it reach the steady state (keepalive running,
   i.e. a long-lived `wsl.exe -d OpenClawGateway -- sleep infinity` is present).
2. Shut down or restart Windows from the Start menu.

Observed on essentially every shutdown where teardown takes long enough for the
timers to fire (~45% of shutdowns on this machine, measured over 47 shutdowns
since install; when it happens it is **exactly 2 dialogs**, always).

### Observed behaviour

The dialogs are recorded verbatim by Windows as `Application Popup`, System log,
**Event ID 26** (`Properties[0]` = caption, `Properties[1]` = message):

```
10-01 12:46:xx  [wsl.exe - Application Error]  应用程序无法正常启动(0xc0000142)。请单击"确定"关闭应用程序。
10-01 12:46:xx  [wsl.exe - Application Error]  应用程序无法正常启动(0xc0000142)。请单击"确定"关闭应用程序。
10-01 14:31:xx  [wsl.exe - Application Error]  … (x2, same text)
10-01 16:44:46  [wsl.exe - Application Error]  … (x2 — 16:44:46 and 16:44:49)
```

Correlated with the tray log (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\openclaw-tray.log`,
local time — note the app logs local, not UTC):

```
16:44:44  User32 1074: shutdown initiated (StartMenuExperienceHost.exe, "restart")
16:44:45  <both WS sockets to the gateway close>  "Connection closed prematurely" (x2, 15-35 ms apart)
16:44:45  "node reconnecting in ~1.1s"
16:44:45  "gateway reconnecting in ~1.2s"
16:44:46  timer fires -> wsl.exe spawn          <- dialog #1
16:44:47  timer fires -> wsl.exe spawn          <- dialog #2
16:44:46+ Winlogon 6000 / 7002, FilterManager 6006, Hyper-V-VmSwitch NIC teardown
```

Inter-dialog spacing is not fixed (0.09 s / 0.15 s / ~3 s observed across events),
so it is not one code path firing twice on a fixed schedule — it is the two
independent reconnect paths (node + gateway) racing the teardown.

### Which spawn is it

The spawn command is `wsl.exe -d OpenClawGateway -- bash -s` (the repair/probe
form), not the steady-state `-- sleep infinity`. Note that **the tray logs nothing
for this spawn** — the log has no `Repair`/`Probe` line at all, which is what made
this hard to pin down from the outside. Might be worth logging it.

### Ruled out (by testing, not by reading)

- **`EnableManagedLocalGatewayAutoRepair: false` does not prevent it.** With that
  switch set, the 2026-10-01 16:44:44 restart still produced exactly 2 dialogs
  (16:44:46 and 16:44:49) — same as with it left `true` (12:46 → 2, 14:31 → 2).
  So the spawn is not (only) the auto-repair coordinator; it is the
  reconnect/keepalive path. Setting reverted afterwards.
- `EnableNodeMode: false` would at best remove 1 of the 2, at a large functional
  cost, so it is not a fix.
- This is not a WSL/hypervisor defect: the distro itself is fine, and the same
  `wsl.exe` runs happily all day while a session is alive. The problem is purely
  "spawn a console app after teardown has begun".
- Not a WER dialog: `HKCU\...\Windows Error Reporting\DontShowUI` does not
  suppress it (this is a hard error, not a report).

### Root cause, as best I can tell from outside

The 4 tray assemblies contain **zero** occurrences of `SystemEvents`,
`SessionEnding`, `QUERYENDSESSION`, `HasShutdownStarted`, or `WM_ENDSESSION`.
The app has no notion of "the session is ending", so when the gateway connection
drops during shutdown it treats it as an ordinary transient disconnect and re-arms
keepalive / reconnect timers (`_reArmKeepAliveAsync`, `reconnectIfCurrentAsync`,
`probeReachableAsync`, `WslGatewayKeepAliveService.TryEnsureAsync`) into a session
that is already gone.

### Suggested fix

1. Before any keepalive/reconnect spawn, bail out if the session is ending. Either:
   - check `Environment.HasShutdownStarted`, and/or
   - subscribe once to `Microsoft.Win32.SystemEvents.SessionEnding` and set a flag
     that gates `_reArmKeepAliveAsync` / the reconnect callbacks, and/or
   - poll `GetSystemMetrics(SM_SHUTTINGDOWN)` (works without a message pump).
   Any of these would also stop the pointless spawn during logoff, not just
   shutdown/restart.
2. Log these spawns (command + reason) — their absence from the log is the main
   reason this took a full day of external tracing to attribute.

### Impact

Cosmetic but loud, and in this case it is the *only* thing the user sees at
shutdown, so it reads as a system fault. There is no in-app workaround.

The only machine-side suppression I found is
`HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Windows\ErrorMode = 2`. I have since
verified it on a restart where the trigger chain definitely fired (same two
`Connection closed prematurely` lines, same two reconnect timers): the dialogs
are no longer displayed, but Windows **still logs the three `Application Popup`
records**, so the underlying spawn still happens and the failure is only hidden —
not fixed, and now hidden machine-wide for every app. That is why this still
needs a fix in the tray.

### Diagnostic commands used

```powershell
# the authoritative record of a desktop popup (caption + message)
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System';Id=26;StartTime=(Get-Date).AddDays(-7)} |
  Sort-Object TimeCreated |
  ForEach-Object { "{0:MM-dd HH:mm:ss} [{1}] {2}" -f $_.TimeCreated, $_.Properties[0].Value, (($_.Properties[1].Value -replace '\s+',' ')) }

# what initiated the shutdown
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System';Id=1074;StartTime=(Get-Date).AddDays(-7)} |
  Sort-Object TimeCreated |
  ForEach-Object { "{0:MM-dd HH:mm:ss}  {1}" -f $_.TimeCreated, (($_.Properties | ForEach-Object {$_.Value}) -join ' | ') }

# the trigger chain in the tray's own log
Select-String -Path "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\OpenClawTray\openclaw-tray.log" `
  -Pattern 'Connection closed prematurely|reconnecting in' -Encoding UTF8
```

title: Chat tail-scroll controller spins the UI thread at 100% CPU on layout changes

labels.name: clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr

labels.name: impact:crash-loop
labels.description: This issue is about crashes, hangs, restart loops, or process-level availability.

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Emergency: data loss, security bypass, crash loop, or unusable core runtime.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

labels.name: clawsweeper:linked-pr-open
labels.description: ClawSweeper found an open linked pull request for this issue.

labels.name: impact:ux-release-blocker
labels.description: A non-technical user is blocked without terminal, logs, config, or support.

body:
## Summary

The chat timeline's tail-scroll controller enters an **unbounded self-referential layout loop**. `LayoutUpdated` calls `StartBringItemIntoView`, which itself causes a layout pass, which re-raises `LayoutUpdated`. The only brake is a version check that is not invalidated while the chat view stays loaded, so the UI thread spins forever and the app becomes fully unresponsive.

This is **not** a slow-render or heavy-load issue. A single qualifying event is enough.

- Windows reports `AppHangB1` (stopped interacting with Windows)
- UI thread at **71.2s CPU** while every other thread stayed under 6s
- Working set grew **230 MB -> 999.9 MB** during the hang
- Reproduced on a freshly restarted process within ~27 minutes of uptime

## Affected build / environment

| | |
|---|---|
| App | OpenClaw Companion (`OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`) `2026.9.4.0` |
| OS | Windows 11 25H2, build `26200.9550` |
| Runtime | .NET 10.0.12, win-x64, self-contained |

## Root cause

`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs`

### The loop closes

```csharp
// line 181
private void OnLayoutUpdated(object? sender, object args)
{
    DetachLayout();
    ...
    itemsView.DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue(() =>
    {
        if (_disposed || !_valid || !itemsView.IsLoaded || version != _version
            || itemsView.ScrollView is not { IsLoaded: true })
        {
            if (!_disposed && _valid)
                AwaitLayout();          // re-arms LayoutUpdated
            return;
        }

        AttachScrollView();
        if (!StartTailRequest(request) && !_disposed && _valid)   // line 205
            AwaitLayout();                                        // never reached, see below
    });
}

// line 254
private bool StartTailRequest(TailNavigationRequest request)
{
    ...
    _following = true;
    itemsView.StartBringItemIntoView(request.Index, new BringIntoViewOptions   // line 269
    {
        AnimationDesired = false,
        VerticalAlignmentRatio = 1.0,
    });
    return true;      // line 274 -- always true on the success path
}
```

1. `LayoutUpdated` fires.
2. `StartTailRequest` calls `StartBringItemIntoView` (line 269).
3. `BringIntoView` **itself triggers a layout pass**, re-raising `LayoutUpdated`.
4. Goto 1. Repeat.

`StartTailRequest` returns `true` whenever it gets past the guards, so the `AwaitLayout()` fallback at line 205 is unreachable on that path. The only exit is the `version != _version` check at line 196, and `_version` is only incremented in `OnUnloaded` (line 282). **While the chat view remains loaded, that exit never triggers.**

Every iteration allocates a fresh `BringIntoViewOptions`, which is what drives the 4x memory growth.

## Stack trace (symbolized from a live dump)

Captured with `procdump -ma` on the hung process and resolved with `dotnet-dump` against the PDBs shipped alongside the binary. This is the actual stack at hang time, not inference.

```
OS Thread Id: 0x58d4
  ABI.Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.IItemsViewMethods.StartBringItemIntoView(
      WinRT.IObjectReference, Int32, Microsoft.UI.Xaml.BringIntoViewOptions)
      index = 0x0000000000000060        (96)
  Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView(Int32, BringIntoViewOptions)
  OpenClawTray.Chat.<...InitialTailPositioner>.StartTailRequest(TailNavigationRequest)
      [...\src\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI\Chat\ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs @ 269]
  OpenClawTray.Chat.<...InitialTailPositioner>+<>c__DisplayClass20_0.<OnLayoutUpdated>b__0()
      [...\src\OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI\Chat\ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs @ 205]
  ABI.Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueueHandler.Do_Abi_Invoke(IntPtr)   <-- UI thread
  Microsoft.WinUI!ABI.Microsoft.UI.Xaml.IApplicationStaticsMethods.Start(...)
  OpenClawTray.Program.Main(System.String[])
```

Full dump available on request (1011 MB, PID 16712).

## Trigger in practice

Any burst of layout changes in the chat timeline. The most common source is the gateway broadcasting `sessions.changed`, which rebuilds the session and chat lists. Three events inside a single millisecond immediately preceded this hang:

```
15:36:07.162  [INFO] [EVENT] Received event: sessions.changed
15:36:07.163  [INFO] [EVENT] sessions.changed received - refreshing sessions list
15:36:07.164  [INFO] [EVENT] Received event: sessions.changed
15:36:07.165  [INFO] [EVENT] sessions.changed received - refreshing sessions list
15:36:07.165  [INFO] [EVENT] Received event: sessions.changed
15:36:07.165  [INFO] [EVENT] sessions.changed received - refreshing sessions list
```

Process state at capture: `Responding=False`, 54 threads, 999.9 MB, UI thread 71.2s CPU.

## Suggested direction

Not a prescribed patch, just the constraints a fix needs to satisfy:

1. **Stop re-entering on the layout caused by our own scroll.** Track whether a `BringIntoView` is in flight and ignore `LayoutUpdated` until it completes, instead of relying on a version counter that only changes on unload.
2. **Make the guard at line 196 actually reachable**, or remove it if it is not load-bearing. Today `StartTailRequest`'s unconditional `true` makes the `AwaitLayout()` branch at line 205 dead code.
3. **Bound the retry.** `AwaitLayout()` re-arming on every failed attempt is the other half of the loop. A cap or a coalescing queue would bound it even if the scroll path is wrong.
4. The project already references `System.Threading.Channels`, and the existing `_tailNavigationQueue` / `QueueTailRequest` path (line 230) looks like the intended coalescing point. Worth checking whether the `LayoutUpdated` path (line 194) bypasses it.

## Impact

Any user running an agent that emits tool calls while the chat window is open. The process must be killed; the session data survives but the UI is unusable until restart. Recovering UI resources also requires a restart (see #1567 for the leaked popup windows).

## Required proof pools

- `UI` (chat)

## Real behavior proof

Hung-process dump plus the symbolized UI-thread stack above, captured from the shipped `2026.9.4.0` binary using its own PDBs.

## Validation

Report, not a code change. Stack trace produced from a live dump of the hung process.

labels.name: impact:ux-friction

body:
## Summary

After roughly 90 minutes of continuous uptime, right-clicking the tray icon opens the menu window but **it renders empty**: no icons, no menu rows. The UI thread is still pumping (`Responding=True`), so this is not a hang.

Restarting the process restores it immediately.

## Evidence: before/after restart

| Metric | Fresh process | After ~90 min |
|---|---|---|
| Orphaned `Microsoft.UI.Content.PopupWindowSiteBridge` windows | **0** | **3** (parked at -32000,-32000) |
| GDI objects | 64 | 211 (+1.6/min) |
| USER objects | 67 | 93 |
| Working set | 228 MB | 416 MB |

`PopupWindowSiteBridge` is the host window WinUI 3 creates for `Popup`/`Flyout`. These three survive after the tray menu closes and are never destroyed. Extrapolating the rate, GDI objects reach ~700 after about 7 hours.

## Root cause

Icon construction failures are **silently swallowed**. `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Windows/TrayMenuWindow.xaml.cs:571`:

```csharp
var iconElement = ResolveIcon(icon);
if (iconElement != null)          // line 572
{
    ...
    Grid.SetColumn(iconElement, 0);
    grid.Children.Add(iconElement);
}
```

When `null`, nothing is added, nothing is thrown, nothing is logged. The row renders with an empty icon column.

Icons all funnel through `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Helpers/FluentIconCatalog.cs:118`:

```csharp
public static FontFamily SymbolThemeFontFamily =>
    (FontFamily)Application.Current.Resources["SymbolThemeFontFamily"];
```

**59 call sites** across the tray menu, chat, settings and nav all depend on this one property. It indexes the resource dictionary directly with **no null check, no try/catch, and no fallback**.

Supporting observation: `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.pri` contains the **key name** `SymbolThemeFontFamily` (next to `BrandMark` / `TitleText` / `NavBackButton`) but not the literal `Segoe Fluent Icons`. The font mapping is expected to be injected by the WinUI runtime during `Application.Start`, which is exactly where the native popup/GDI accumulation happens.

The same resource failure is visible in the log, repeating on every run:

```
[WARN] LocalizationHelper: Resource lookup failed for 'Chat_Composer_Slash_Loading' (language='<default>'): NamedResource not found
```

## Suggested direction

1. Add a fallback to `SymbolThemeFontFamily`: on lookup failure, fall back to `new FontFamily("Segoe Fluent Icons")`, or resolve to `null` and let `Build` return an icon without an explicit `FontFamily` so the default font fallback applies.
2. Icon construction failure should not be silent. At minimum log one WARN on first failure so this is diagnosable.
3. Track down the popup resource leak. `PopupWindowSiteBridge` windows are not destroyed when a Flyout closes, and `WindowManager` holds `_chatWindow` / `_hubWindow` / `_trayMenuWindow` as cached singletons with no invalidation strategy. Give them a resource-health check.

## Impact

Long-running users see an empty menu with **no error surfaced**, which is very hard to self-diagnose. A restart clears it.

## Required proof pools

- `UI` (tray UX)

## Validation

Report, not a code change. Window enumeration via `EnumWindows` plus `GetGuiResources` on the shipped `2026.9.4.0` binary, before and after restart.

body:
## Summary
Typing into the Gateway Web Chat composer inside Windows Companion is slower when maximized on a 3840 x 2160 display than in a small window. Continuously focused manual input now reproduces the symptom: median keypress duration is 14.809 ms in the small window versus 240.009 ms maximized, while the handlers remain about 2.2 ms.

This followed the initial routing of openclaw/openclaw#162324 to the Windows host. Later detailed traces and the live DOM identify the large Control UI outer chat clip as the software-rendering trigger. The minimal CSS repair is proposed in openclaw/openclaw#162418; no Companion graphics flag or host change is proposed.

## Reproduction and measurement
Use the same existing chat and draft in the Companion's Gateway Web Chat surface, first with a 737 x 539 WebView and then maximized at 3579 x 2010. Keep Companion continuously focused while typing; do not send the draft. The reported host uses software compositing in an RDP session.

| Continuously focused manual capture | Small | Maximized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Keypress samples | 67 | 107 |
| Keypress EventTiming duration, median | 14.809 ms | 240.009 ms |
| Keypress handler processing, median | 2.247 ms | 2.227 ms |
| Layout, median | 0.453 ms | 0.469 ms |
| Viz StartDrawToSwapStart, median | 6.785 ms | 167.282 ms |

Neither measured typing interval contains recorded focus/blur dispatches. These captures supersede the initial two-key, focus-switching automation samples; those original samples are not used to establish continuously focused input latency.

A further manual capture with detailed Viz events contains 53 keypresses: median EventTiming duration 245.728 ms, handler processing 3.174 ms, and `DirectRenderer::DrawFrame` 166.436 ms. `SoftwareRenderer::DoDrawQuad` is observed directly. Between the first and last keypress starts, 44 of 46 compositor damage rectangles cover the entire 3321 x 1962 chat pane.

The live pane has `overflow: hidden` and `corner-shape: superellipse(1.5)`, owned by `ui/src/styles/chat/startup-layout.css` in the OpenClaw repository. An isolated software-rendered Edge fixture loading the actual baseline and candidate stylesheet verifies that changing only the outer pane to `round` reduces large-pane median drawing from 181.550 to 19.446 ms while preserving dimensions, radius, and overflow clipping. Each condition verifies 12 input/image changes.

**Evidence boundary:** the fixture uses synthetic content and screenshot-forced presentation. Its drawing measurements are not after-fix real-user input latency in Companion. The latest available `test3` is still the pre-fix detailed capture, not a new candidate result.

## Candidate validation and disposition

A new reversible A/B/A uses the full, actual Control UI 2026.9.7 served by the running Gateway, with the existing chat route and content, not a mocked Gateway or synthetic pane. In isolated Edge 154.0.4258.37 with software compositing, the viewport is 3579 x 2010 and the outer pane is exactly 258,48 3321x1962. The only candidate change is `.chat.chat { corner-shape: round; }`, then its removal.

| Condition | Keypress samples | EventTiming median | Handler median | Software DrawFrame median |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original superellipse | 40 | 200.617 ms | 1.693 ms | 187.308 ms |
| Candidate round | 40 | 7.935 ms | 1.745 ms | 0.143 ms |
| Reverted superellipse | 40 | 205.148 ms | 1.755 ms | 194.116 ms |

Each condition has 40 trusted keypress events and 40 input events, the correct final draft, continuous focus/visibility, and no focus/blur dispatches. No screenshots are taken during timed input. `SoftwareRenderer::DoDrawQuad` is observed in all three conditions; after the change, 39 of 40 damage rectangles are text-sized instead of repeatedly covering the large chat surface. The roughly 96% median input reduction disappears when the single declaration is removed.

**Scope:** this is automated keyboard/EventTiming evidence on the real application page in headless Edge, not a new manual Companion WebView2/IME recording or physical-display latency measurement. The candidate declaration was temporarily injected, not installed as a rebuilt bundle. The original `test3` remains pre-fix evidence. The draft was restored and the temporary test-browser device was removed and its removal verified.

Sanitized real-page before/after screenshots are embedded in the repair PR body. Both images were verified to render in the public PR, decode to their original 3579 x 2010 pixel dimensions, and match the inspected local images byte-for-byte after download. The earlier upload blocker is resolved.

The repair PR is now Ready for review. Keep this issue open: the fix has not been merged or released, and a new manual Companion/IME after-capture remains outside the proof above. No Companion graphics flag or host change is proposed.

The detailed, evolving investigation is in [the follow-up comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1564#issuecomment-5924292995). Raw traces remain private because they may contain session metadata.

## Environment
Windows 11, 3840 x 2160 display, RDP with Microsoft Remote Display Adapter; Windows Companion 2026.9.4; Gateway/Control UI 2026.9.7 in WSL; WebView2 Runtime 154.0.4258.48. Broader prevalence is unknown.

body:
The five existing audio tools advertise empty, permissive input schemas. Their descriptions explain arguments, but clients cannot discover required fields and useful defaults from `inputSchema`.

I implemented a small discovery-only pilot for `stt.transcribe`, `stt.listen`, `stt.status`, `tts.speak` and `tts.status` on [my fork's `proposal/mcp-audio-tool-schemas` branch](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/tree/proposal/mcp-audio-tool-schemas). It adds no dependency or runtime validation. The focused checks and required local test suites pass; the full repository build is still blocked at WinUI's existing npm dependency download. This is a proposal for review, not a merge-ready claim.

## Existing work

This is not a newly discovered gap. [#355 was closed as consolidated, not necessarily fixed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/355#issuecomment-4473186623), into the MCP hardening work associated with #372. That tracker was later [closed in favor of the project board's Scenarios view/Mission field](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/372#issuecomment-5222150923). Both are historical references, not a claim about current tracking or shipped behavior.

[#401, Add typed MCP tool input schemas](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/401#issuecomment-4472964017), was closed unmerged, with fresh post-refactor review and implementation requested. This pilot does not revive its broader all-command catalog or opt-in runtime validation.

## Concrete example

At inspected base `273b0182745a3093c0e09f306ca8a1fff6ef3c5a`, [the bridge advertises an empty permissive object for every command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/273b0182745a3093c0e09f306ca8a1fff6ef3c5a/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Mcp/McpToolBridge.cs#L245-L272). The current upstream bridge and audio parser file blobs still match this tested baseline.

For example, `stt.transcribe` changes from:

```json
{"type":"object","additionalProperties":true,"properties":{}}
```

to the following structure (descriptions omitted here):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "properties": {
    "maxDurationMs": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 30000},
    "language": {"examples": ["en-US", "auto"]}
  },
  "required": ["maxDurationMs"]
}
```

The complete captured [before](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/audio-tools-before.json) and [after](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/audio-tools-after.json) responses show all five actual registry names. Only their schemas change; descriptions and other catalog fields stay identical.

## Keep the current parser contract

The [argument helpers](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/273b0182745a3093c0e09f306ca8a1fff6ef3c5a/src/OpenClaw.Shared/NodeCapabilities.cs#L146-L179), [STT handlers](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/273b0182745a3093c0e09f306ca8a1fff6ef3c5a/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/SttCapability.cs#L131-L247) and [TTS parser/provider policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/273b0182745a3093c0e09f306ca8a1fff6ef3c5a/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/TtsCapability.cs#L58-L174) are more permissive than a conventional strict schema:

| Input | Preserve this behavior |
|---|---|
| `stt.transcribe.maxDurationMs` | Required positive Int32, at most 30000. JSON Schema accepts `5000.0`/`5e3` as mathematical integers; the parser rejects those token forms. Describe that limitation. |
| `stt.listen.timeoutMs` | Default 30000; Int32 values clamp to 1000..120000, not reject. Wrong types and unreadable numbers select the default. |
| STT `language` | Trimmed limited language/script/region pattern or case-insensitive `auto`. Blank/null/non-string acts omitted. Transcribe uses configured language; listen uses `auto`. |
| `tts.speak.text` | Required string, trimmed before nonblank and 5000 UTF-16-code-unit checks. A raw `maxLength` would reject padded valid text and count Unicode differently. |
| TTS options | Strings trim; blank/null/non-string selects settings. Provider case is normalized by the service. Nonblank explicit provider requests stay strict. Only literal JSON `true` enables `interrupt`. |

Every schema retains `additionalProperties: true`. Optional fallback fields omit strict types. Provider names are examples, not a case-sensitive enum. Defaults are annotations, not bridge coercion. The schema does not guarantee permission, provider readiness or call success. Unknown provider names still reach the existing service error path.

## Small implementation steps

1. Add the focused [metadata helper](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/a993bc9e08fe1815f6080e571570f82d19f00bc3/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Mcp/McpAudioToolSchemas.cs) using existing command constants and System.Text.Json anonymous-object conventions.
2. Select that metadata inside `HandleToolsList`; preserve the original generic fallback for every other command. Do not change capability registration, dispatch, errors or results.
3. Add [real-bridge characterization and schema tests with fake audio handlers](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/a993bc9e08fe1815f6080e571570f82d19f00bc3/tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/McpAudioToolSchemaTests.cs). Update MCP and winnode guidance with coercion and schema limitations.
4. Review this five-tool slice before expanding the catalog. No SDK, audio-provider, transport or result-format refactor is required.

Alternatives are to retain description-only discovery, make a separate behavioral breaking change toward strict inputs, or build a broader all-command schema system. The pilot avoids coupling those larger choices to exposing information the existing parsers already define.

## Acceptance criteria and evidence

- All five existing names expose the expected properties, required fields and default annotations. Disabled capabilities remain absent; unrelated tools retain their generic schema.
- Real bridge/capability calls preserve accepted inputs, error strings, clamping, optional coercion, provider policy and existing output casing.
- All five public schemas are exercised with an existing validator, with mismatches between schema acceptance and parser success explicitly documented.
- Required local suites report real nonzero test inventories; build and product-proof gaps remain visible.

The same harness blob, `8ec3c9379dc2f132b258f3908d81249427ffd634`, ran on [B](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/commit/01956ec2f31fcc1d5145ee387be35ac4476d7fd6) (base production code plus harness) and [C](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/commit/a993bc9e08fe1815f6080e571570f82d19f00bc3) (candidate). B ran 75 characterization cases; C also ran the six assertions that require the new schema.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline characterization | 75 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Candidate focused suite | 202 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped: 81 new-schema/characterization, 47 bridge, 42 STT, 32 TTS |
| Five schemas, existing `Test-Json` validator | 21/21 expected acceptance outcomes matched, including disclosed caveats |
| Full Shared suite, final | 4188 passed, 0 failed, 32 existing opt-in integration skips |
| Full Tray suite, final | 3072 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Full WinNode CLI suite | 127 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Required full build | Exit 1: existing node-pty npm TLS download failure in WinUI |

[Seven before-call pairs](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/audio-calls-before.txt) and [after-call pairs](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/audio-calls-after.txt) are identical: five successes and two parser errors. These are representative in-process JSON-RPC calls through the actual bridge and capabilities, not HTTP or real audio proof. Handler results are deliberately synthetic, including TTS result propagation; strict provider selection is checked separately against the existing policy.

[Validator outcomes](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/schema-validation.json) identify PowerShell 7.6.6 and JsonSchema.Net 7.0.0.0. Draft 2020-12 is selected only for validation, not added to wire output. Whitespace-only/overlong TTS text and decimal/exponent transcribe tokens illustrate why schema acceptance is not equivalent to a successful call.

## Reproduction and remaining gaps

[The evidence guide](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/README.md) includes commands, environment isolation, requirement-to-test mapping and failure history. [Exact command arrays, exit codes and counters](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/command-results.json), [method inventories](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/test-inventory.csv) and [SHA-256 manifest](https://github.com/luisquintanilla/openclaw-windows-node/blob/17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b/docs/evidence/mcp-audio-schemas/manifest.json) are available in documentation-only evidence commit `17db0e3bf194fbf54dabe281bf2950e361c0ae0b`. It preserves C's production and test trees.

The initial Tray run had 3071 passes and one failure from an app-local VC runtime missing in the incomplete WinUI output. A first copy-target attempt used the wrong platform output path; its focused rerun still had three passes and one failure. Matching the existing target to the actual build directory repaired the environment, after which all 3072 Tray tests passed. Both failed attempts remain recorded. No test weakening or source fix was needed; this does not turn the blocked full build into success.

Structured autoreview was attempted once but could not start its missing `codex` executable. Direct source review found no actionable in-scope issue; there is no clean structured-review claim. Running WinUI/HTTP MCP, gateway invocation, real audio providers and ecosystem-wide client compatibility remain unverified. No agent-success percentage or performance improvement is claimed.

I can put up a PR if there is interest.

body: ## Summary In single-agent mode, the Windows Companion desktop UI can only show **one conversation at a time**. There is no way to open a second conversation without losing sight of the first, and no way to jump between ongoing conversations quickly. Two small additions would fix this: 1. A visible **"New conversation" / "New session" button** in the Chat view. 2. A **tabbed conversation bar** so several conversations can stay open side by side (browser-style tabs). ## Current behavior - The Chat view binds to a single active session; opening another session from the sidebar replaces the current one. - No `+ New conversation` control is present in the Chat header — only the existing session list (also reported in #1271). - Switching back to a previous conversation means re-finding it in the session list and reloading it; in-flight replies in the previous conversation are easy to miss. - In single-agent mode this is especially limiting: the agent is fixed, but the *conversations* are not — users still run several parallel threads (e.g. one for work, one for a personal project). ## Expected behavior - A `+ New conversation` button (and `Ctrl+N`) in the Chat view header that starts a fresh session against the currently selected agent. - A horizontal tab strip above the chat area: one tab per open conversation, showing the session title (truncated) + an unread/activity indicator, with a close `×` per tab. - Clicking a tab switches conversations instantly, keeping each conversation's scroll position and draft input. - Middle-click or `×` closes a tab (session remains in the sidebar history). - Optional but useful: `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` to cycle tabs, and pinned tabs for conversations the user keeps open all day. ## Actual behavior Only one conversation is rendered at a time; the UI has no notion of "open conversations", so there is no button to create one and no tabs to switch between them. ## Why it matters This is the standard interaction model for every chat client (browser tabs, Slack, ChatGPT desktop, etc.). Without it, the desktop app feels strictly weaker than the web Dashboard, which already supports multiple sessions, and it blocks any real multi-thread workflow on Windows. ## Environment - OS: Windows 11 (also expected to affect Windows 10) - App: OpenClaw Windows Companion (desktop UI), single-agent mode - Related: #1271 (New Chat / New Session action)
