body:
## What Problem This Solves

Open Dashboard could send a gateway token through an SSH forward that belonged to a different gateway, and it could drop that forward before the browser connected.

## User Impact

The browser opens only when the gateway identity and SSH destination still match the ones checked before the wait. If a stop is already waiting before the browser is opened, the dashboard does not open and the stop finishes.

A saved gateway URL that names a remote host is left in settings. GatewayDashboardLauncher builds the browser URL. That URL keeps the saved mount path, query, and fragment, and uses the verified local forward for the host and port.

Before that URL is handed to the browser, this app binds both 127.0.0.1 and ::1 on the public port. SSH listens on a backend port. Guarded gateway clients use 127.0.0.1. If the tunnel already belongs to the connection manager, the replacement stays on that owner. Stop and Reset after the navigation is submitted end the SSH process and leave the public port occupied. Recovery drops the launch lease and can start SSH again on a backend port for the same user, host, remote port, and SSH port. A guard created for a start that fails before the browser opens is released.

Browser traffic is copied only when the accepted loopback socket belongs to that SSH process and the process start time still matches. Browser-proxy forwarding uses the saved local port. Local proxy ports 65534 and 65535 remain valid. The remote gateway port still has to leave room for the proxy's `+ 2`.

A failed browser open shows the existing Connection notification and retry dialog. Retry keeps the requested path. A successful open dismisses that notification. The launch error is not written to the log, because the message can contain the token URL.

Switching to another saved SSH gateway that stores the same local port keeps the older dashboard port pinned to the first destination. The second gateway listens on a new runtime port. Its stored local port is not rewritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ownership wait returns the generation, local port, and SSH process id that passed listener verification.

The public port has to be owned on every loopback address the client can select, before SSH exits and before the browser receives the URL. Manager-owned tunnels keep that owner. A failed start does not leave the new bind behind.

Dashboard URL construction and launch failure handling stay in GatewayDashboardLauncher.

## Evidence

The `ssh.exe` session below is from parent `2a20af4a0d672d61fec4ba95d88d49a7c5bc119e`. Head `6c7b974084eebd5f629fdf0baf2612b1cd008418` adds the second-gateway runtime port and was not part of that session. `SshTunnelService.EnsureSettingsOwnedForwardReadyAsync` started real `ssh.exe` to `root@127.0.0.1` port 22, with BatchMode and no password. The guest HTTP server listened on `127.0.0.1:19048`. The owned forward was local port 19049, ssh pid 7580. `GET /ocwn-1514?token=not-a-gateway-token` returned HTTP 200. A browser opened that same URL. The guest log recorded `token=true` for those requests and did not store the query value. One later guest line was `token=false`, from a browser fetch that did not include the query.

A second call for remote port 19047 on the same local port returned `owned=false`. It did not replace the forward. Binding another listener on 19049 failed while the guard held it. The next request then failed with `HttpRequestException`. Calling ensure again for the original destination returned `owned=true` with a new ssh pid 43132, and the same GET returned HTTP 200.

A later run on the same head kept ssh pid 45824 as the recorded owner and pointed the backend port at a different process listening on `127.0.0.1:19046`. The public GET failed. That other process accepted the TCP connection and read 0 bytes. The guest log did not record that request. Recovery then used ssh pid 36624 and the GET returned HTTP 200. The guest log for the whole run was two `token=true` lines, the allowed call and the recovered call.

The same head then covered a delayed navigation across explicit Stop and Reset. `EnsureSettingsOwnedForwardReadyAsync` used real `ssh.exe` to `root@127.0.0.1` port 22, local port 19149, remote port 19148. The first owned forward was ssh pid 48196, backend port 61404. `GET /ocwn-1514?token=not-a-gateway-token` returned HTTP 200. The guest log was one `token=true` line. Navigation was submitted on that handoff, then `Stop` ran. Status was Stopped, the public port stayed held, and a second bind of 19149 threw `SocketException`. The delayed GET failed with `HttpRequestException`. A foreign listener on backend port 61404 accepted 0 connections and read 0 bytes. The guest log did not gain a line. Ensure for the same destination then used ssh pid 39768, backend port 61409, and the GET returned HTTP 200. The guest log gained a second `token=true` line.

`ResetNotConfigured` used the same sequence. Navigation was submitted on ssh pid 39768. After reset, status was NotConfigured, port 19149 stayed held, and a second bind threw `SocketException`. The delayed GET failed. A foreign listener on backend port 61409 accepted 0 connections and read 0 bytes. The guest log stayed at two lines. Ensure for the same destination then used ssh pid 35880, backend port 61414, and the GET returned HTTP 200. The guest log gained a third `token=true` line.

A local port Dashboard has reserved stays tied to the original user, host, remote port, and SSH port. A different destination is not accepted on that same port. A second saved gateway that stores the same port gets a different runtime listener, and stopping that gateway does not release the first port.

Unit coverage on this head, from the earlier closeout:

Unit coverage on this head:

- A manager-owned tunnel that is already running on the requested port stays manager-owned. A settings-owned tunnel stays settings-owned.
- Holding the dashboard port rejects a second listener on 127.0.0.1 and on ::1. The guarded WebSocket host is 127.0.0.1.
- Startup with SSH port 0 does not leave the public port bound.
- Stop after a submitted navigation ends the planted SSH process and keeps the port bound.
- A submitted navigation whose planted SSH process has exited drops the launch lease and keeps the port after Stop.
- A different SSH port cannot reuse that hold.
- Local port 65533 with browser-proxy forwarding emits proxy port 65535.
- Two saved gateways that store one local port: the first destination stays pinned, and the second connect port is the allocated runtime port. Its browser-proxy port is neither the saved port nor the saved port plus 2.
- Stopping the second gateway leaves the first dashboard port held and still pinned to the first destination. That test failed before the release filter.

## Change Type

- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs or instructions

## Scope

- [ ] Local MCP or `winnode`
- [x] Gateway, connection, or pairing
- [ ] Setup or onboarding
- [x] Permissions, privacy, or security
- [x] Tests, CI, or docs

## Required proof pools

- `windows-winui-interactive`: isolated Debug tray built from this head. Settings had `EnableMcpServer` true, `EnableNodeMode` false, and `UseSshTunnel` true with an empty user and host, so setup did not block and the tunnel settings were incomplete. `openclaw://dashboard` was forwarded on the isolated pipe. The log recorded `SSH tunnel is enabled but settings are incomplete`. The Connection page showed a dialog titled Dashboard, with the text "Dashboard could not open. Check the verified gateway connection, then try again." Retry and Close are both fully inside the window. Invoking Retry removed that button, and the same dialog returned about 200 ms later. The incomplete-tunnel warning was logged again.

![Dashboard retry on the isolated tray](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9b5b441-9038-4528-80a9-dff6b6bb9fcf)

## Validation

Head `6c7b974084eebd5f629fdf0baf2612b1cd008418`.

- `./build.ps1`: exit 0
- Shared: 4226 passed, 33 skipped, 0 failed
- Tray: 3808 passed, 0 failed
- `SshTunnelServiceTests`, `DashboardBrowserHandoffTests`, and `GatewayClientEndpointResolverTests`: 56 passed, 0 failed

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Claiming the dashboard port stopped a manager-owned tunnel and restarted it as a settings tunnel. The guard bound only 127.0.0.1, so ::1 on the same port stayed available. A failed start could also leave the new guard bound.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows 11, worktree `C:\Users\sebta\wt-wn-1514`, head `2a20af4a0d672d61fec4ba95d88d49a7c5bc119e`. Guest SSH is Ubuntu-24.04 on `127.0.0.1:22`. The HTTP proof server was `127.0.0.1:19048` inside that guest.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `SshTunnelService.EnsureSettingsOwnedForwardReadyAsync` for `root@127.0.0.1`, local port 19049, remote port 19048. Then an HTTP GET and a browser open of `http://127.0.0.1:19049/ocwn-1514?token=not-a-gateway-token`. Then the same call with remote port 19047. Then ensure again for remote port 19048. On this same head, the delayed case used local port 19149 and remote port 19148: submit the navigation, call `Stop`, send the GET, then ensure the original destination. Repeat that with `ResetNotConfigured`. The isolated tray then received `openclaw://dashboard`.
- **Evidence after fix:** owned forward ssh pid 7580 returned HTTP 200. The changed destination returned `owned=false`. A second bind of 19049 was denied. Recovery used ssh pid 43132 and returned HTTP 200. On the next run, ssh pid 45824 stayed the recorded owner while a different process listened on the backend port. That process read 0 bytes and the guest did not see the request. Recovery used ssh pid 36624 and returned HTTP 200. After Stop, ssh pid 48196 was gone, the delayed GET failed, and the foreign listener on backend port 61404 read 0 bytes. Recovery ssh pid 39768 returned HTTP 200. After Reset, the foreign listener on backend port 61409 read 0 bytes. Recovery ssh pid 35880 returned HTTP 200. The isolated tray dialog is the screenshot above. Retry left and then returned.
- **Observed result after fix:** Credential-bearing bytes were forwarded only through the owned ssh process. A different SSH destination did not take over that local port. A backend socket owned by another process received no request bytes. A GET that arrived after explicit Stop or Reset was not delivered, and the same destination worked again after recovery. The tray shows the failure dialog and opens it again when Retry is invoked.
- **What was not tested:** Two saved SSH gateways were not switched in the tray, and the new runtime port was not opened with `ssh.exe` or a browser. The port choice and the stop are covered by the unit tests above. The `ssh.exe` and tray dialog evidence is from parent `2a20af4a`.

## Security Impact

- New or changed network calls? `No`
- Command or tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`

This app binds 127.0.0.1 and ::1 before the URL is issued and keeps that binding after SSH stops. Guarded clients use 127.0.0.1. Forwarding happens only when the accepted loopback socket belongs to the SSH process for the original user, host, remote port, and SSH port. Launch failures are not logged, because the exception text can contain the token URL.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the config editor shows a Nostr private key and a Google Chat webhook URL in a normal text box.

## User Impact

User impact: those fields use the same password box as other secrets, and a stored value is not preloaded. A stored secret object that declares properties shows how many entries are configured. Replace all starts blank. Clear all asks before it removes the entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The schema editor and the no-schema fallback share `ConfigPathSensitivity`. An exact path segment named `nsec`, `privateKey`, `webhookUrl`, or `webhookUrls` takes the existing sensitive field. `webhookUrlExtra` stays a normal field. A sensitive string array uses a password box. The stored item is kept by the editor, not on the control. A blank box keeps that item.

A sensitive array of objects stays off the page. The page shows how many entries are configured. Replace all opens a blank JSON box and the patch contains only that new array. Clear all asks, then sends an empty array. Cancel, or a save that does not use those actions, leaves the stored array out of the patch. The no-schema fallback uses the same editor.

A sensitive object uses that same hidden editor, including when its schema declares properties. Child titles and stored children stay off the page. An object that is not itself sensitive still expands. A sensitive string stays a password field. Replace all checks the expected JSON kind before it stages a value. A wrong kind leaves the stored value in place and keeps Save disabled. Cancelling that replacement, or cancelling Clear all, clears the blocking validation state.

## Evidence

Terminal output from commit `4184c01c`.

The page reloaded from `config.get` and showed "1 entry is configured. Stored values stay hidden." `ConfigPage_ReplacementSurvivesInvalidRetryAndCanceledClear` passed in 32 seconds on the merged app. Gateway fixture protocol tests after the merge: 40 passed. `./build.ps1` and Shared tests (4107 passed, 32 skipped) were run on `406fe032` before the merge.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the next launch connects with a shared or bootstrap token when the per-gateway identity file is missing and the legacy device key for that same gateway URL is still on disk.

A later change of that gateway URL must not send the copied device token.

## User Impact

User impact: a paired gateway keeps its device token across that startup instead of dropping back to the weaker token. If the saved gateway URL changes, startup does not send the device token that was copied for the previous URL.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup now copies the legacy identity into the per-gateway directory, stamps that directory with the gateway URL, and resolves it again before it accepts a shared or bootstrap token. If that copy fails, startup refuses the connection and does not send the shared or bootstrap token. If the record URL no longer matches the stamp, startup and the connection owner use a directory named for that URL. A later URL gets a different directory, so it cannot send the previous URL's device token. Bootstrap retirement and an explicit shared-token replacement use that same directory. A credential that is already a device token, and was not copied from the legacy file, is left alone. Whether a failed copy should instead offer a visible Fix or Doctor recovery path is still a maintainer decision.

## Evidence

Earlier connect traces are on `5aca1da3bb186b07f5fdefe0f703b5ad22689071`. The setup reassignment below is on `955f8e938e458fc40dca89524bccca360e665be9`.

Isolated tray and a loopback gateway. The loopback answers `connect.challenge` with `hello-ok` protocol 4. Token text is not recorded. The server log records the role and whether the frame carried the legacy device token, the token stored for the previous URL, or the shared token.

  startup source identity.DeviceToken
  operator CONNECT auth=deviceToken
  node CONNECT auth=deviceToken
  Node status: Connected

  startup source record.SharedGatewayToken
  operator CONNECT auth=token
  node CONNECT auth=token
  Node status: Connected

  Copied legacy identity into active gateway
  Connecting node-only gateway, source identity.NodeDeviceToken
  node CONNECT auth=deviceToken
  no operator CONNECT
  Node status: Connected

fresh profile, no legacy identity file:
  startup source record.SharedGatewayToken
  operator CONNECT auth=token
  node CONNECT auth=token
  Node status: Connected

  Refusing startup connect because the saved device identity could not be copied
  no CONNECT accepted

  Copied legacy identity
  operator CONNECT auth=token
  node CONNECT auth=deviceToken
  Node status: Connected

path case, first URL ends in /GatewayA, then the record URL ends in /gatewaya:
  first startup operator and node CONNECT auth=deviceToken
  second startup operator and node CONNECT auth=token
  the second URL has its own realm directory and does not reuse the first device token

alternate directory pairing, then another URL:
  the first connect sends the shared token, not the stamped legacy device token
  hello-ok stores operator and node device tokens in that URL's directory
  the next URL's operator and node connects send the shared token

  node reaches Connected

  the same clear the direct-connect path uses removes the stored device tokens from that URL's directory
  the next operator and node connects send the shared token

  the chat URL is built from the device token stored for that URL
  the legacy token is not placed in the chat request

  the CONNECT frame did not carry the legacy device token

- Local Tray suite on the earlier head: 3067 passed. Five failures are the [#1518](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1518) source-contract checks. They look for CRLF text in an LF checkout, in files this change does not edit.

- The chat URL builder test passed.

Tray tests passed 5294, then `LegacyCredentialMigration_StaysRegistryBacked` failed on the old method name and passed after the contract used `ChooseStartupOperatorCredential`.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Startup could send a weaker token when a legacy device identity for the same gateway URL was still on disk. After that identity is copied, a later URL change could still send the old device token.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows 11, isolated tray data, loopback gateway. The earlier loopback connect traces were captured on `ed61d0bc`. On this head the x64 Debug tray used legacy web chat. The WebView GET of /chat carried the active URL token and not the legacy token. With no token for the new URL, the page showed the Connection-settings sentence and the listener saw no chat request.

A fifth launch blocks the copy by making the destination path a directory.

The upgrade connect sends `deviceToken` for operator and node, and the node reaches Connected. The reassigned connect sends `token` for both roles, not `deviceToken`, and the node reaches Connected. The node-only connect sends `deviceToken` and reaches Connected with no operator connect. The fresh connect sends `token` for both roles. The blocked copy refuses startup and the loopback accepts no connect. After a token is stored for one URL, the next URL's operator and node connects send the shared token and do not carry that stored token. After the direct-connect clear, the following operator and node connects on the paired URL also send the shared token and do not carry the cleared device token.

## Latest head

Head e3068ef7 keeps the SSH generation observed after a listener rejection stops the candidate tunnel. A start receipt that no longer matches the manager is not used as the rollback scope. ConnectWithSharedTokenAsync_ListenerFailureAfterTunnelStartRestoresPriorLiveConnection failed before the fix because the restored client never started, and passed after it. The shared-token suite passed 37. build.ps1 succeeded. Shared tests passed 4636, skipped 24. Tray tests passed 4450. Main is merged. The only conflict was MxcExecutorTests.cs, deleted on main by the MXC 1.0 move. That deletion stands.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: connecting with a rejected shared token removes the saved bootstrap token and SSH tunnel before the new token is checked, when no device token is stored yet. A gateway that rejects the token after the connect call has already returned also left that rejected token saved. A newer connection that starts during that wait could be overwritten, and a settings callback could target the edited gateway instead of the gateway that was active before the attempt.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed shared-token connect leaves the setup-code bootstrap credential and the saved SSH tunnel in place. Saved tray settings are restored from the gateway that was active before the attempt. If the operator was already connected, that previous connection is opened again. A newer connection that takes over during the wait keeps its own record.

## Why This Change Was Made

A stored device token still uses the existing pre-replacement check. When the record only has a bootstrap token or an SSH tunnel, the shared token is saved and connected on the normal path. If that operator connect fails, including an auth failure that arrives while the operator is still connecting, the previous record and active id are restored only when this attempt still owns the connection generation. If the wait ends and the operator is still connecting, that attempt is disconnected and the record is rolled back. The previous connection is opened only after the operator is Idle, and the restore waits for a terminal result. When rollback leaves no active gateway, the settings callback restores the snapshot taken before the rejected record was applied. That capture runs after ConnectWithSharedTokenAsync takes the transition lock, so a second request cannot snapshot settings before the first transaction has started. Each connectSharedToken call captures its own settings attempt and passes that object into the callback. A second call cannot replace the first call's snapshot. The app captures the snapshot before the candidate callback. That callback keeps it after a successful sync. The rollback callback reuses it. If runtime tunnel reconciliation fails on both attempts during that rollback, the pre-attempt settings are written back before the callback throws. The commit callback then runs with the record for the prior active gateway. If saving those settings or the runtime tunnel fails, the callback retries the restored gateway and reports an out-of-sync error instead of writing the rejected snapshot back. A connection that was already live is started again. A successful connect still clears a stale bootstrap token.

## Evidence

Current head `d91c9bb3c1dafe2a1bf67fac87444f652a9ef982`. The counts below are from `8c191b3938aac911dc22fa513d4e38c94d3f4602` before the main merge.

Connection tests on that earlier head: Passed 808, Failed 0, Skipped 1, Total 809.

The live gateway trace below was recorded on parent `41834892e8f186b0951600e2a0066532115486e7`. This head adds the unfinished-handshake rollback and the settings recovery.

The live check used an isolated registry and the gateway already listening at `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`. The previous shared token was the installed gateway token. Its value is omitted. The replacement token was `rejected-shared-token-not-real` (30 characters). The device token stored by the first connect was cleared before the replacement so the pre-replacement check did not skip the rollback.

```text
first_connected=True state=Connected
durable_tokens_cleared=True
outcome=ConnectionFailed committed_flag=False
callbacks=cleared-bootstrap,has-bootstrap
bootstrap_restored=True
shared_len=48
operator=Connecting
later_operator=Connected later_bootstrap_restored=True later_shared_len=48
```

The stored shared-token length after the failure was 48 again, which is the previous token. The operator was Connecting when the call returned, and Connected again three seconds later.

- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Connection.Tests/OpenClaw.Connection.Tests.csproj`: Passed 808, Failed 0, Skipped 1, Total 809.

## Real Behavior Proof

Earlier head `41834892e8f186b0951600e2a0066532115486e7` used the installed gateway at `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`. That trace had no SSH tunnel. Outcome was ConnectionFailed, GatewayCommitted was false, the commit callback returned to the previous bootstrap token, and the operator reached Connected again. The current-head trace below is the one with the tunnel.

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A rejected shared token must not keep the new record when the previous record has an SSH tunnel and no device token. Saved settings and the operator connection that was already up have to come back with that tunnel.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows worktree, head `8c191b3938aac911dc22fa513d4e38c94d3f4602`. Production `SshTunnelService` and `GatewayConnectionManager`. Windows OpenSSH local forward, listener `127.0.0.1:19221`, remote `127.0.0.1:19219` through `root@127.0.0.1` port 22. The registry directory was a new temp directory, not the installed tray config. The peer on port 19219 speaks the connect handshake only. It is not the installed OpenClaw gateway.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** The peer accepts one shared token and returns `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH` for the other. It does not issue a device token. `ConnectAsync` opened the tunneled record and reached operator Connected. `ConnectWithSharedTokenAsync` then sent the rejected token with the same tunnel and a commit callback.
- **Evidence after fix:** The tunnel log was `SSH tunnel started` for local port 19221. The first connect logged `hasDeviceToken=False` and `Received hello-ok`, and the operator was Connected with the local port listening. The callback then recorded `credential=rejected` with the SSH tunnel still set. The gateway answered `token mismatch` with detail code `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH`. The callback then recorded `credential=prior` with the same tunnel (`remotePort=19219`, `localPort=19221`). Outcome was ConnectionFailed. GatewayCommitted was false. The restore connect logged `hello-ok` again. The operator was Connected, the local port was still listening, and `gateways.json` still held the prior credential and the SSH tunnel.
- **Observed result after fix:** The rejected token did not stay saved. The SSH tunnel and the previous operator connection were both up after the rejection.
- **Screenshot or artifact links verified?** No
- **Not verified / blocked:** The 15-second unfinished-handshake cutoff is unchanged. Whether that wait should stay is a maintainer decision. A fresh setup wizard was not run. The product `windows-wsl-gateway-e2e` suite was not run. The gateway below is a disposable OpenClaw 2026.9.6 process in its own home directory. It is not the installed service on port 18789, which was left running.

Current head `1adab8a78fae5e4cad06b890c748a50de89b1751`. The production callback sequence is the one in `App.CapabilityHandlers`: capture a settings attempt when the transaction starts, then call `GatewayDirectConnectService.SynchronizeSettingsWithCommittedGateway` for the candidate and for the rollback. `ConnectWithSharedTokenAsync` was called with no replacement tunnel, matching `app.connection.connectSharedToken`. Settings were a real `SettingsManager` directory and were read back from disk after the process finished.

The peer was OpenClaw 2026.9.6, `gateway run --dev --auth token`, loopback port 19229. The prior operator connected through Windows OpenSSH, local port 19237 to that port, and the gateway returned hello-ok with operator scopes. That hello-ok stored a device token. The token was cleared before the replacement so this stayed on the no-durable-token path. The first callback recorded `credential=rejected ssh=False`. The real gateway then returned `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH` with message `unauthorized: gateway token mismatch`. The next callback recorded `credential=prior ssh=True remotePort=19229 localPort=19237`. Outcome was ConnectionFailed and GatewayCommitted was false. After that, the operator was Connected again with hello-ok, the local forward was still listening, the reloaded settings had the prior URL and SSH enabled on local port 19237, and `gateways.json` still held the prior credential and that tunnel. Tokens are not included here.
- **What was not tested:** `ConnectWithSharedTokenAsync_RejectedTokenRestoresPriorLiveConnection` still covers a fake tunnel. `ConnectWithSharedTokenAsync_UnfinishedHandshakeRollsBack` covers a handshake that stays connecting. `ConnectWithSharedTokenAsync_NewerGenerationSkipsRollback` covers the generation check.

When no device token is stored, a failed connect, including an auth failure that arrives after connect returns, rolls the registry record back and runs the commit callback with the prior active gateway. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: canvas content can open a private or loopback address after the first URL check, including from data HTML. The same broad request filter must not attach the gateway bearer to a service worker, a cross-site request, or a same-site frame. Same-site is a different origin.

## User Impact

Data HTML is no longer presented. A later navigation is cancelled unless it passes the same URL check as the first navigation. A redirect to a disallowed address is answered locally, so that host is not contacted. A service worker, a cross-site request, and a same-site frame do not receive the gateway bearer. A same-origin request and a top-level document navigation still do.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first Navigate check allowed data:text/html and did not run again when the page navigated or redirected. Cancelling in NavigationStarting still left the redirected request on the network. The all-source filter also delivers frame and worker requests to the handler that attaches the gateway bearer. That handler now keeps the bearer for a same-origin request and for a top-level document navigation. It withholds the bearer from shared workers, service workers, cross-site requests, and same-site frames.

## Evidence

Head `00727bbf6a433d1e6e2501608be421d804a600d7`. A missing `Sec-Fetch-Site` no longer grants the bearer because `Upgrade-Insecure-Requests` is present. That header is also sent for an iframe that suppresses Referer. The bearer stays for a same-origin referer, and for fetch metadata that says a document navigation. The isolated tray lines below are from ancestor `e6c9bf2a6a6d924d931eaed44a6a5e49c8cece60`, which still treated `Upgrade-Insecure-Requests` as top-level. They are not this head. The isolated tray used two host names on one parent domain. Both names resolve to loopback. The gateway name is the trusted origin. The other name is a different host, so a request from it is same-site and not same-origin. Addresses below use those roles. `auth=match` means the request carried the gateway bearer.

```
GET /doc auth=match
GET /from-doc auth=match referer=<gateway-host>/doc
GET /page on <frame-host>
```

`/doc` is the top-level gateway document. `/from-doc` is that document's own fetch. `/page` is the frame host. The frame page's image and fetch of the gateway host did not reach the fixture. A same-site frame whose referer host differs from the gateway host is refused by the bearer rule.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a direct Config edit can put a legacy placeholder where the gateway shows its native secret mask. The gateway already restores `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` before it writes. This client guard refuses that placeholder before the patch is sent, and an untouched mask is left out of the patch.

## User Impact

User impact: a direct edit that replaces the native mask with a legacy placeholder such as `***` is refused, and the draft stays. An unrelated Config save leaves `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` out of the outgoing patch.

## Why This Change Was Made

`config.get` replaces a stored secret with the exact mask `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__`. The gateway restores that mask before it writes. It is not a legacy placeholder, so a Channels save still sends it when another channel shows the mask.

The Config editor omits the mask only on an untouched credential such as `apiKey`. A direct edit of that credential to a legacy placeholder is refused locally, the same as a parent edit. A SecretRef `id` is not a credential, so replacing that id still stays in the patch.

`5fa003d1` had put the mask in the shared sentinel set. That blocked a Channels save and dropped a SecretRef `id`. `fffc8472` separated those cases. `6ad6ed0f` teaches the Config loaded-placeholder check to recognize the native mask without putting it back in the Channels set.

## Evidence

Head `6ad6ed0f3b253d7577701ac95db040bc4b0acd68`. A console called `ConfigEditorModel.FindUneditedRedactionSentinel` and `ConfigEditorModel.OmitUntouchedRedactionSentinels` on the document returned by `config.get`. Those are the two calls `ConfigPage.OnSaveAsync` makes after `ApplyChanges`.

The peer was a disposable OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (`eb377ac`) `gateway run` on loopback port 19242, with its own config file. It was not the installed gateway on port 18789. The product `windows-wsl-gateway-e2e` suite was not run. That process was stopped after the trace. Ports 18789 and 19241 were still listening.

Allowed save, edited path `models.providers.custom.baseUrl`. The outgoing document omitted `apiKey`. `config.patch` was sent with `{ raw, baseHash }`.

```
MODE allow
loadedApiKeyIsMask True
blocked none
wouldSend True
sentHasApiKey False
base https://page.example
modelsLen 1
hashSet True
ok True
disk_matches_secret True
disk_is_legacy False
disk_base https://page.example
disk_models_len 1
disk_model_id_m1 True
```

Direct edit, edited path `models.providers.custom.apiKey`, replacement `***`. No `config.patch` was sent. A later `config.get` still returned the gateway mask for that key, and the on-disk secret still matched the value seeded before the save. The secret is not printed here.

```
MODE direct
loadedApiKeyIsMask True
blocked models.providers.custom.apiKey
wouldSend False
sentHasApiKey True
sentApiKeyIsLegacy True
base https://page.example
modelsLen 1
disk_matches_secret True
disk_is_legacy False
```

`disk_matches_secret` compares the on-disk provider secret with the value seeded before the saves.

The same head was then opened in the isolated tray Config page against a new disposable OpenClaw 2026.9.6 gateway on loopback port 19244, auth mode none, paired in this session. The page subtitle named the disposable config file. The loaded provider showed Api Key as the gateway mask and Base Url `https://old.example`.

Allowed save: Base Url was set to `https://page.example` and Save Changes was clicked. The page said "Configuration saved and the gateway connection is back. Refreshing the latest config." The Base Url field read back `https://page.example`. The on-disk secret still matched, models length stayed 1, and the model id stayed `m1`.

Refused save: Api Key was set to `***` and Save Changes was clicked. The page stayed on 1 unsaved change and showed:

```
Save failed
Save blocked. A redacted placeholder is still present at models.providers.custom.apiKey. The value was not sent.
```

The JSON diff kept the draft:

```
- "apiKey": "__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__",
+ "apiKey": "***",
  "baseUrl": "https://page.example",
```

The on-disk secret still matched and the base URL stayed `https://page.example`. The window was captured with PrintWindow. body:
**Version:** OpenClaw Companion 2026.9.4 (3c43751), also unchanged on `main` @ a2c4647 and in v2026.9.5-alpha.13. Gateway 2026.9.5. Windows x64.

### Symptom
Sending a chat message with an image attachment shows **two** user bubbles: the local one with the attachment chip, plus a text-only copy of the gateway echo. Text-only messages are not duplicated. The web Control UI is fine.

### Evidence it is render-side only
For three image sends, the gateway log shows exactly one `chat.send` (one runId, one agent turn) and the tray log shows one "Sent chat message" (1 attachment) and one `session.message` user echo. No retry.

### Cause (from reading the source at 3c43751)
- `OpenClawChatDataProvider.SendMessageAsync` creates a local queued user row with a non-empty attachment signature (e.g. `1|image/png|image`).
- On echo, `ChatQueueState.TryConsumeLocalEcho` → `ChatAttachmentEchoCorrelation.SelectMatchingMessageId` only recognizes attachments when the echo content starts with `[media attached: media://inbound/…]` lines (parsed in `GatewayMediaMessageProjection.Project`).
- Gateway 2026.9.5 stores user-turn media in structured `__openclaw.media` (with `mediaImageLayout`) and leaves `content` as plain text. `ExtractOpenClawMetadata` reads only `id`/`seq`/`kind`/token fields, not `media`.
- So the echo looks attachment-less and this rule rejects the match:
  ```csharp
  if (!hasMediaEnvelope &&
      matching.Any(candidate => candidate.AttachmentCorrelationSignature.Length > 0))
      return null;
  ```
- The fallback `ReconcileExistingLocalQueuedUser` → `ApplyProjectedRemoteUserMessageLocked` also fails on the signature mismatch (empty vs `1|image/png|image`), so a new text-only row is appended.

### Suggested fix
- Read `__openclaw.media` (contentType/kind) into the message metadata and derive the attachment signature/presentations from it when no text envelope is present.
- Better: send an `idempotencyKey` with `chat.send` and match echoes on it, so correlation doesn't depend on attachment shape.
- Add a test for "structured media echo, no envelope" with an image attachment.

Related but distinct: #914 (closed, user messages rendering double), #453, #1119, #1259.

When the final `done` step restarts the gateway, the hosted wizard can return the exact terminal error `Error: TUI exited from signal SIGTERM`. ## Why

The gateway had finished the wizard and then terminated its hosted TUI during restart. The WinUI owner did not use the setup engine's existing terminal-error decision seam or track which step the request had just answered.

## User Impact

The WinUI wizard now uses `SetupWizardRunner.DecideTerminalWizardError` and `WizardFinalStepTracker`. The exact SIGTERM response completes setup only immediately after answering the authoritative final plain acknowledgement step named `done`. The same SIGTERM before the final step, after a progress poll or replay, on a skipped transition, with an answerable step, or with inexact text remains an error.

This run continued through that note, then answered `done` with true. The setup log said `Gateway wizard completed`. It did not log `Error: TUI exited from signal SIGTERM`. body:
## Summary

Windows Companion native Chat remains on **“Assistant is thinking...”** after the assistant's final response is already visible and the Gateway reports the session as **done**. Typing `/stop` then produces **“Queued (1)”** with `/stop` in the local queue rather than clearing the apparent busy state.

This makes a completed conversation look stuck and prevents the user from recovering through the obvious stop command.

## Environment

- Observed: 22 September 2026.
- Client: OpenClaw Windows Companion, native Chat, connected to a remote macOS Gateway.
- Paired Windows node advertised version `2026.9.4` in the preceding diagnostic check; exact Companion executable build and Windows OS build have not been independently collected.
- Gateway-host installed CLI: OpenClaw `2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)`; running Gateway build not independently verified for this report.
- Session/model: main session, `gpt-6-astra`.

## Observed sequence

1. Send a normal task message from Windows Companion Chat.
2. The assistant completes its turn with a final text response requesting a file from the user. That response is visible in the Windows chat.
3. The client nevertheless continues displaying **“Assistant is thinking...”**.
4. Send `/stop` to recover.
5. The client displays `/stop` as a user bubble and also shows **“Queued (1)”**, with `/stop` and a **“Cancel queued message”** control.
6. Independently inspect the same session through the Gateway: `status: done`, `abortedLastRun: false`, and the last assistant message matches the completed response visible in Windows. This completed status was checked again while preparing this report.

This is one observed incident, not yet a deterministic minimal reproduction. The exact trigger for the stale busy state is unknown.

## Expected behavior

- Reconcile the native chat's busy/streaming state with the completed session and clear the thinking indicator.
- `/stop` should be handled as a control action rather than ordinary queued chat behind a stale busy state. When no run is active, it should resolve promptly with an idle/no-active-run outcome.
- Client queue state should not remain stranded after the underlying turn has completed.

## Actual evidence

The user-provided screenshot shows these elements simultaneously:

- Green **Connected** indicator.
- A complete assistant response.
- User `/stop` bubble.
- **Assistant is thinking...**.
- **Queued (1)** containing `/stop`.

The screenshot's private conversation text is intentionally not published; the UI labels above are transcribed exactly. The paired Windows node was also reported connected during the preceding check. Gateway session completion and the client-visible local queue are separate observations; this report does not claim that `/stop` reached the Gateway queue.

## Scope / investigation leads

Suspected client run-lifecycle reconciliation or terminal-event handling; root cause is not established. Please also check whether the slash-command path bypasses the ordinary message queue while busy. No Gateway restart, client restart, or workaround has been tested for this incident.

Related, but not established duplicates:

- #672 (closed): stale failed tool output versus a completed response. Here the final response is already visible, but the busy/queue state remains stale.
- #1366: native chat slash-command handling gaps.
- #1363 concerns a genuinely pending `ask_user`; this incident instead has a completed session.

Report prepared with AI assistance from the user's screenshot and Gateway session inspection.

body:
When going through OpenClaw Setup on Windows and choosing "Anthropic Claude CLI" as the auth method, the onboarding wizard repeatedly fails with:

Provider setup failed
Claude CLI is not authenticated on this host.
Run claude auth login first, then re-run this setup.

Steps I took:

Ran claude auth login inside the Ubuntu WSL distro (manually installed via wsl --install) — logged in successfully, claude auth status --text confirmed a valid Claude Pro session.
Discovered OpenClaw actually provisions its own separate WSL distro OpenClawGateway (found via %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\wsl\OpenClawGateway\ext4.vhdx).
Entered OpenClawGateway via wsl -d OpenClawGateway -u root, installed Node.js + @anthropic-ai/claude-code, ran claude auth login — succeeded, claude auth status --text confirmed login.
Also copied /root/.claude to /home/openclaw/.claude and chown'd it to the openclaw user, in case the gateway process runs as that non-root user.
Fully restarted the OpenClaw Windows Companion app (quit from tray, relaunched).
Still get the same "Claude CLI is not authenticated on this host" error when retrying setup / clicking Install again.

Relevant log lines from %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\openclaw-tray.log:

[WARN] [WslKeepAlive] Distro 'OpenClawGateway' not found; skipping keepalive.
[ERROR] Previous session did not exit cleanly (started ...)

Environment:

Windows (OpenClaw Windows Companion / OpenClawTray)
WSL2, distro OpenClawGateway (auto-provisioned by OpenClaw)
Claude Pro subscription account
Expected: Setup should detect the successful claude auth login inside the gateway's own WSL distro.
Actual: Always reports "not authenticated" regardless of login location or restart.

body:
Reported on behalf of another user from a supplied public-support-thread summary dated 2026-09-16. This is not a local reproduction by the filing account. Root cause and fix remain unverified.

## Summary

A user can run PowerShell successfully in their Windows terminal, but requesting shell execution through the OpenClaw dashboard leads to application-startup failures. Screenshots were identified during support as showing `powershell.exe` and `where.exe` application errors with code `0xc0000142` (DLL initialization failure).

The agent's repeated claim that an empty executable allowlist caused the failure is not established by the collected evidence. Gateway effective policy and the node's saved defaults/main-agent policy were all `security=full`, `ask=off`. The node does not expose a complete resolved host policy, so those saved settings do not establish every runtime restriction.

## Environment

- Gateway/CLI: OpenClaw **2026.9.3**, commit **1391f7c**.
- Windows node reports version **2026.7.1-4**.
- Companion state directory: `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray`.
- Windows version reported earlier in the thread: **10.0.26200.9445**.
- Earlier MCP crash output reported Node.js **v26.8.1**; the interpreter used by each current component has not been independently established.
- CLI launcher found at `%APPDATA%\npm\openclaw.cmd`.
- Agent model referenced in the conversation: `minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3`.
- Two paired node records with the same display name; one connected, one disconnected. Diagnostics targeted the connected node by ID.
- This is not a confirmed clean-install reproduction: troubleshooting included attempted configuration rewrites before the evidence below was collected.

The Gateway/node version difference is a diagnostic lead, **not proof of incompatibility or causation**.

## Reported reproduction sequence

These steps describe the affected installation, not a maintainer-verified minimal reproduction.

1. Connect the Windows companion node to the Gateway and open the dashboard chat.
2. Ask the agent to execute:
   ```text
   powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command Get-Date
   ```
3. Observe the Windows application-startup error during dashboard-triggered execution.
4. Run the same command manually in the user's existing PowerShell terminal.
5. Observe successful date output.

A subsequent dashboard-related screenshot was identified as a `where.exe` application error with the same code. Its complete command line and invocation context have not been captured.

## Expected behavior

An authorized command should start successfully, or return an actionable error identifying the actual launch/policy failure. The same simple PowerShell command should not fail only through the companion without sufficient diagnostics to explain the difference.

## Actual behavior and evidence

### Manual PowerShell succeeds — direct user terminal output

```text
PS C:\WINDOWS\system32> powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command Get-Date

Wednesday, September 16, 2026 4:16:08 PM
```

### Dashboard execution fails — screenshots and agent summaries

The support conversation recorded screenshots of application-error dialogs for:

- `powershell.exe`: `0xc0000142`.
- `where.exe`: `0xc0000142`.

Original screenshot message links are below. The filing agent could not access the source Discord messages in this session; screenshots are not attached or independently inspected here.

The user's agent separately reported this output:

```text
Warning: tools.exec.pathPrepend is ignored for host=node.
Access is denied.
(Command exited with code 1)
```

It also reported a different test ending with `-1073741502`, which corresponds to `0xC0000142`, not `0xC000013A`.

**Evidence boundary:** these textual tool results were copied from the agent's prose, not obtained as a complete raw tool invocation/result. The exit-1 report and the application-error reports should not be assumed to be the same attempt. Exact argv, working directory, environment, launch identity, and timestamps remain missing.

### Gateway approvals — direct CLI output

Command used:

```powershell
openclaw.cmd approvals get --gateway
```

Reported:

```text
Defaults: security=full, ask=off, askFallback=full, autoAllowSkills=on
Agents: 0
Allowlist: 0
Effective tools.exec: security=full, ask=off
```

`openclaw.cmd approvals pending` reported no pending approvals at the time checked. This is not proof that no approval was ever requested.

### Node approvals — direct CLI output and selected local file contents

The connected node's approvals report showed:

```text
Path: %APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\exec-approvals.json
Defaults: security=full, ask=off, askFallback=deny, autoAllowSkills=off
Agents: 1
Allowlist: 0

Effective Policy
This node does not expose a complete resolved host policy, so Effective Policy is unavailable.
```

Reading only the file's `agents` field returned:

```json
{
  "main": {
    "security": "full",
    "ask": "off",
    "askFallback": "deny"
  }
}
```

### Node capabilities — direct CLI output

Selected fields from `openclaw.cmd nodes describe --node <connected-node-id> --json`:

```json
{
  "platform": "windows",
  "version": "2026.7.1-4",
  "clientId": "node-host",
  "clientMode": "node",
  "deviceFamily": "Windows",
  "sessionHost": false,
  "approvalState": "approved",
  "paired": true,
  "connected": true
}
```

The returned command list includes `system.run`, `system.run.prepare`, `system.which`, and `system.execApprovals.get/set`. A missing advertised shell-execution capability is therefore not supported by this output. Pairing approval alone does not authorize every shell command.

## Diagnostics already attempted

- Confirmed `openclaw.cmd` works. Bare `openclaw` previously produced unexpected launcher behavior; the Windows launcher association/resolution issue was not fully diagnosed.
- Confirmed manual PowerShell launch succeeds.
- Checked Gateway policy, connected-node saved policy, and main-agent saved policy.
- Checked node connection/capabilities.
- Queried the Windows Application event log for messages containing `powershell.exe` in the prior 30 minutes; no output. The query used `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`, so this does not establish that no relevant event or query error existed.
- Recursively listed `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\Logs`, including hidden files. Only September 9 setup logs were found, not current execution logs.
- Located a Diagnostics item in the tray menu, but no resulting diagnostic report has yet been collected.
- No verified fix, clean reinstall reproduction, or successful companion execution retest has been obtained.

## Configuration history / confounders

The user's agent suggested unsupported nested configuration paths involving `agents.entries.main.models.…agentRuntime.tools.exec` and whole-file PowerShell rewrites. A direct terminal capture shows a property-not-found error. A later save line could still have rewritten configuration after that error.

The agent also claimed backups/restoration and additional script changes; these claims have not all been independently verified. Do not treat the current state as pristine or the claimed backup as verified.

An earlier, separate MCP subprocess-cleanup crash reported:

```text
Error: stdio process cleanup cannot confirm descendant extinction
```

That earlier crash should be triaged separately unless evidence links it to this launch failure.

## Requested engineering investigation

1. Capture a complete failing exec invocation and node-side process-launch diagnostics: executable path, argv, cwd, sanitized environment differences, process/user/session identity, launch flags, and native error/exit status.
2. Identify the supported way to obtain current runtime logs from this companion build; the discovered directory only contained setup logs.
3. Reproduce on the reported Gateway/companion version pair and compare with a supported matched/current pair in a controlled test.
4. Compare terminal and companion launch contexts for both PowerShell and `where.exe`; do not assume permissions, PATH, a specific DLL, security software, or the version mismatch is the cause without evidence.
5. Preserve existing configuration and approval policy while collecting evidence. No further blanket permission widening is justified by these findings.

## Source references

- Public support thread: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1546779292078313543
- Manual PowerShell success: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1546779292078313543/1549740683559174215
- PowerShell screenshot message: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1546779292078313543/1549740882218061864
- where.exe screenshot message: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1546779292078313543/1549743949110054996
- Node capability output: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1546779292078313543/1549742567950917713
- Node main-agent policy: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1546779292078313543/1549740596917313537
- Tagged CLI documentation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.3/docs/cli/nodes.md
- Tagged approval documentation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.3/docs/cli/approvals.md

Discord references may require server access. Sanitized original screenshots and complete raw invocation/results remain evidence gaps.


## Related reports and diagnostic leads

- #1143 (closed) reports the same error family for PowerShell and other User32-linked programs under MXC UI-deny on an older companion. This could be the same policy behavior, but this installation’s active sandbox mode and Windows UI API setting were not captured; recurrence/regression is **not established**.
- #1189 (open) concerns `SetInformationJobObject(JobObjectUILimitInformation)` / `0x80070057`. That signature is not present in this supplied evidence, so it should not be assumed to be the same defect.
- openclaw/openclaw#149401 discusses local sandbox controls and the companion ownership boundary; this report requests diagnosis and actionable launch errors, not an unsandboxed-execution feature or broader approval policy.
- The current companion [README](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#local-files) documents `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\openclaw-tray.log`, whereas support inspected `%APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\Logs`. The former has not yet been collected from the affected host. Current README also documents `openclaw://logs` and redacted support-context diagnostics; availability in this exact installed build has not been verified.

Please first determine whether this is expected UI-deny behavior needing clearer diagnostics, recurrence of #1143, or a separate launch-context failure. Preserve the user’s current configuration and sandbox settings while collecting that evidence. Model troubleshooting errors and the earlier MCP cleanup crash are outside this issue’s scope.

body:
# This report is redacted to exclude tokens, credentials, private messages, project contents, and protected project paths.

This report is redacted to exclude tokens, credentials, private messages,
project contents, and protected project paths.

## Summary

OpenClaw Windows Companion `2026.9.3.0` crashes in the native WinUI Chat
surface after receiving `chat.history`. The Gateway and Ollama remain healthy,
and no provider/model request or `chat.send` occurs before the crash.

The failure reproduces after both selected-thread correction and a clean
Companion Chat/UI-state rebuild, so it is not tied solely to one historical
session.

## Environment

- Application: `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`.
- Companion version: `2026.9.3.0`.
- Product version: `2026.9.3+84928c4370bc52d7f19127c65a637c7a28aab46e`.
- Windows build: `10.0.26200.9445`.
- Architecture: x64.
- Faulting runtime module: `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll` `3.2.3.0`.
- Installed package dependency metadata includes Windows App SDK / WinUI and
  Microsoft UI Reactor components.

## Reproduction

1. Launch Windows Companion.
2. Connect to the existing Gateway.
3. Open the Chat surface with the validated Crestodian session selected.
4. Allow the session history to load.
5. The UI exits during history rendering. A user-visible attempt to type/send a
   normal message exposes the same failure, but the recorded crash occurs before
   `chat.send` is submitted.

The same crash was reproduced after:

- redirecting the selected dashboard thread to the validated Crestodian
  session; and
- rebuilding Companion-owned Chat/UI state.

The protected Gateway sessions were not modified.

## Crash evidence

Latest WER-enabled reproduction:

- Timestamp: approximately `2026-09-14 17:19:34.440` local time.
- Application Error event: `1000`.
- Exception: `System.ArgumentException: The parameter is incorrect.`
- Exception code: `0xc000027b`.
- Faulting module: `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll` `3.2.3.0`.
- Fault offset: `0x00000000003a9c5d`.
- Stack boundary: `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.FrameworkElement.ArrangeOverride`.

Associated WER APPCRASH record:

- WER fault module: `combase.dll`.
- WER parameter: `80070057`.
- WER fault offset: `0x00000000000579e4`.

Earlier repeated timestamps were approximately:

- `2026-09-13 22:28:25.120`;
- `2026-09-13 23:45:29.503`;
- `2026-09-14 00:17:17.385`;
- `2026-09-14 00:17:49.307`;
- `2026-09-14 00:19:00.884`.

## Lifecycle correlation

Observed order:

1. Companion connects/reconnects.
2. Companion requests or receives `chat.history`.
3. History response is received.
4. Chat rendering enters WinUI layout.
5. `FrameworkElement.ArrangeOverride` raises the unhandled argument exception.
6. Companion exits.

Not observed before the crash:

- `chat.send`;
- agent invocation;
- provider request;
- Ollama request;
- model generation;
- Gateway process failure.

Gateway health remained `ok=true` with a healthy event loop. Ollama remained
running and received no request in the crash window.

## Session/state checks

The validated user-facing session was selected:

`agent:crestodian-coder:companion-crestodian`

Its intended runtime is:

- agent: `crestodian-coder`;
- provider: `ollama`;
- model: `qwen3:14b-12k`;
- context: `12288`;
- thinking: `off`.

The protected validation session
`agent:crestodian-coder:ollama-clean` was not modified.

The selected dashboard thread had previously contained stale thinking metadata,
but redirecting away from it did not fix the layout crash. A clean Companion
Chat/UI state rebuild also reproduced the crash. This points to a general Chat
history/rendering path rather than one malformed selected session alone.

## State-reset results

- Selected-thread redirection: crash remained.
- Companion-owned Chat/UI state rebuild: crash remained.
- Gateway session deletion or modification: not performed.
- Package update/reinstall: not performed.

## Dump capture

One temporary per-application WER LocalDumps registration was used with a
dedicated dump folder and full-dump mode. The single reproduction generated no
`.dmp` file. No usable archived WER dump was available, and no debugger or
ProcDump installation was available in the diagnostic environment.

The current report therefore gives the framework boundary but not the exact
Chat control or invalid layout value below `ArrangeOverride`.

## Expected behavior

Chat history should render without terminating the Companion process. The
operator should be able to type and send a normal message, and the Companion
should remain connected while the Gateway handles the request.

## Actual behavior

The Companion process terminates with an unhandled WinUI argument exception
during Chat/history rendering. The Gateway and Ollama continue running.

## Related upstream evidence

- #1150 discusses Windows Companion UI failure under event-stream pressure.
- #1167 discusses Chat history projection/re-render instability after session switching.
- PR #1301 describes a similar Reactor visual-tree/layout crash pattern (closed).
- PR #1386 addresses snapshot-delivery races (merged), but the installed build still reproduces this crash and no exact fix attribution is claimed.

## Requested maintainer investigation

Please inspect the native Chat history hydration and Reactor visual-tree update
path for a layout update that reaches WinUI with an invalid argument or with

body:
## Summary

In Windows Companion v2026.9.3, typing `/new` successfully creates a new Gateway session, but Companion does not switch to that session and does not expose the empty session in the chat-area session selector.

The newly created session is visible immediately in Companion's Gateway session list as **New session**, so session creation itself succeeds. The failure is in Companion's local selection/materialization behavior.

## Environment

- Windows Companion: **v2026.9.3**
- Gateway: **OpenClaw 2026.9.4**
- Windows 11 x64
- Existing selected chat/session: **Main**

## Reproduction

1. Start with **Main** selected in Companion.
2. Type `/new` in the Companion composer.
3. Click **Send** once.
4. Do not select anything else.

## Actual behavior

- Companion remains on **Main**; the chat view does not change.
- A new session named **New session** appears immediately in Companion's Gateway session list.
- The new session is absent from the chat-area session selector below the conversation.

Additional controlled verification:

5. In ControlUI, select the newly created **New session** and send one message (`test`).
6. The session becomes a normal/materialized chat and appears in Companion's chat-area selector as **Direct message**.
7. Companion still remains on **Main**.
8. Manually selecting **Direct message** in Companion works normally and shows the message.

So the created session is healthy; Companion simply does not perform the expected local handoff to it.

## Expected behavior

After successful `/new` session creation, Companion should immediately select the newly created session and make it usable in the chat UI, even before the session has received its first message.

## Source behavior in v2026.9.3

The current lifecycle path appears intended to do exactly that:

- `ChatLifecycleCommandDispatcher` parses `/new`, calls `CreateSessionAsync(...)`, and returns `Succeeded: true` with `NewSessionKey` when creation succeeds.
- `ChatComposerController.SendCoreAsync(...)` then invokes `_selectedSessionHandoff(sessionKey)` when `NewSessionKey` is returned.
- `OpenClawReactorChatRoot` binds that handoff to local selection and maintains `_pendingSelectedThreadId` / a compose-only thread so a newly created session can be selected before it is materialized by history/content.

Observed behavior indicates that this selection/materialization handoff is not taking effect.

## Notes

- This is not the same as #1271, which requests a visible New Chat/New Session UI action. Here `/new` exists and **session creation succeeds**, but Companion fails to transition to the newly created session.
- No crash behavior is part of this report; the reproduction above is a functional failure only.

body:
Related: #1495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed Local AI recovery rejecting a different compatible catalog model, so users can proceed without reinstalling their WSL Gateway or being forced to keep an interrupted model selection.

## User Impact

Recovery reuses validated runtime assets and lets users change models after interruption. Optional bookkeeping must not strand an otherwise valid installation. Uncertain compensation retains potentially active files instead of deleting them.

The **Change model** navigation remains a separate stacked PR: #1538 (fix(local-ai): Change model opens the scoped Local AI setup instead of full onboarding). This PR does not alone close #1495.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical installation receipt remains authoritative for the selected runtime/model. Setup borrows the tray-owned runtime instead of starting a competing owner.

The forward-recovery revision changes the original strict transaction approach:

- Keep canonical `LocalAI/state.json` readable by the pre-PR reader. Store optional recovery provenance in `LocalAI/recovery-hints.json`, bound to the canonical receipt.
- Treat missing, stale, corrupt, or unusable hints as disposable, not a new mandatory state dependency.
- Allow C, or a return to A, after interrupted A-to-B replacement.
- Treat endpoint/history/fallback bookkeeping drift as best effort for the same validated installation. Preserve artifact/path/hash identity and unrelated Gateway/file ownership checks.
- Make old Gateway conditional-write support advisory rather than a setup version error. Unsupported moved-route compensation preserves uncertainty and files; it does not perform an unguarded provider overwrite or claim restoration succeeded.

Losing optional provenance can still prevent safe recognition of a historical provider. This revision does not promise recovery by overwriting unrelated configuration.

## Evidence

Published repair head: [`2eeab2ca07f7bcb0e8a6082cff8bec737ac6e33e`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/2eeab2ca07f7bcb0e8a6082cff8bec737ac6e33e), tree `8c57424ecfd45e083ffcfbac62837c46efd195e3`, parent `f687956323913f36a033d7a0cad29b8e7fcaab4e`. The four-file CI repair was published by ordinary fast-forward push, preserving the rebase onto main `ef05d53a77392ac798676dc32774d087b8f74029`, authored merge resolutions, and human credit. The published tree equals the independently reviewed and locally tested candidate. No PR merge.

The initial cleanup integrated pinned main `4dea6231304036c4eb4b7d1f341c226af620c559` and repaired the [October 17 findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1232#issuecomment-6242553712): fallback handback, active legacy-model cleanup, missing-provider refusal, and expected startup history.

The permissive revision now preserves hints-only route provenance through another selection, discards semantically unusable optional historical models, and uses a qualified third model in all eight route regression cases. These address three independently source-verified P2s. Historical cleanup candidate tree: `b774214be03892757fd9d524323ba8dea8240b57`. The last test-only correction separates accepted endpoint drift from real installation-change rejection and fixes the invalid model-path fixture. Canonical independent review at the cleanup tree completed with no P0-P3 findings. It is retained for the unchanged PR patch, not claimed as fresh-main runtime validation. Hosted tests subsequently found failures described below.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs or instructions
- [x] Tests or validation
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore or infrastructure

## Scope

- [ ] Windows node capability
- [ ] Local MCP or `winnode`
- [x] Gateway, connection, or pairing
- [x] Setup or onboarding
- [ ] Permissions, privacy, or security

- `windows-wsl-dgx-blackwell`: replacement inference, cancellation, and failed-switch recovery on qualified hardware. Not verified for the published cleanup head.
- `windows-wsl-gateway-e2e`: real replacement/reselection through restart, route compensation, and finalization, including legacy Gateway behavior. Generic setup/connect CI is not proof of this changed transaction.
- `windows-winui-interactive`: runtime handoff, cancellation, and choosing another model after interruption. The selectable Change model entrypoint is in stacked #1538.
- `windows-clean-installer-upgrade`: signed previous-version upgrade, interrupted repair, downgrade, relaunch, and uninstall. Not verified for the published cleanup head.

## Validation

### Current-head Windows CI

[Build and Test run 39909587105, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/39909587105), published head `2eeab2ca`. Fresh current-head reads also show UI/functional/accessibility, CodeQL and security passed, and the [CI Gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/39909587105/job/120275277536). body:
## Summary

Today the Windows app shows you which OpenClaw skills you have installed, but there is no way in the UI to discover and install new skills/plugins from ClawHub. Ideally users should be able to explore and install things from ClawHub easily.

It would also be great if the app could check locally installed applications and highlight official ClawHub plugins/skills for those apps. That way if a user installs a new application, or an application publisher creates/updates official skills/plugins it's easy for users to connect their claw to that application.

As more desktop software adds MCP/CLI tools and skills to drive them users will want to easily connect their claw to them.

## AI Research Summary

### Current experience

The existing Skills page lists gateway-reported skills and lets users enable or disable them. It does not browse ClawHub or present relevant plugins.

Plugin installation guidance appears only in some feature-specific recovery flows. The Local MCP Server setting under Permissions is a separate feature that exposes Windows-node capabilities to local MCP clients; it does not discover MCP integrations offered by installed applications.

For example, a user may have a known desktop application installed that offers an MCP server, while an official ClawHub plugin knows how to connect to it. The Windows app does not connect those facts or help the user review and enable the integration.

### Desired behavior

The Windows app should provide a ClawHub experience covering skills and plugins, including a view for plugins that provide MCP capabilities.

When that page is opened, OpenClaw should be able to scan installed applications locally and prominently show relevant official integrations. Matching should use stable application and publisher identities rather than display-name similarity.

Selecting a recommendation should let the user review what was matched, who published the ClawHub package, what capabilities it provides, and any setup or restart requirements before installation. Skill and plugin installation should use the Gateway's trusted lifecycle and policy checks. An MCP integration should not be reported as ready until its connection and exposed tools can be verified.

The current installed-skill enable/disable controls should remain available as part of the ClawHub experience.

### Trust and privacy expectations

- An installed app is a relevance signal, not permission to install or enable anything automatically.
- Installed-app matching should require exact package/publisher or signed application identities. A matching display name, process, executable name, or open port is not sufficient by itself.
- Installed application inventory should remain on the Windows machine. ClawHub catalog metadata can be downloaded and matched locally without uploading the user's app list, executable paths, or signer details.
- App-based recommendations should be limited to available packages from official publishers.
- Community packages may remain browsable when explicitly requested, with clear trust warnings.
- Trust, integrity, compatibility, moderation, and install-policy decisions should remain enforced by the Gateway.
- Warnings, required credentials, and restart requirements should require explicit user confirmation.
- OpenClaw should not scan arbitrary ports, launch detected apps, or import MCP configuration from other tools as part of discovery.

### MCP scope

MCP should be presented as a capability supplied by a ClawHub plugin or bundle, not as a separate package type. The plugin owns the supported connection and configuration path for the application and exposes the resulting MCP tools to OpenClaw.

The initial scope can support only integrations whose official plugin already provides a working connection path for the active Gateway topology. A generic bridge for MCP servers that are reachable only from the Windows node can be considered separately.

> **Moved from [openclaw/openclaw#125576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/125576)** — that repo's maintainers closed it as outside their boundary and directed Windows Hub / tray issues here (docs/platforms/windows.md: "openclaw-windows-node release page"). Reposting the full report below.

---

## Summary

The Windows Hub system tray app (`OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`, v2026.7.1.0) crashes with an **access violation (0xc0000005)** inside `Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core` while mounting UI elements. Since installation it has crashed **8 times** in two distinct stack paths. The gateway itself is unaffected.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.7.1-2` (latest stable at time of report)
- Companion / Windows Hub: `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe` v2026.7.1.0
- OS: Windows 11, build 10.0.26200 (x64)
- .NET runtime: 10.0.10 (coreclr.dll 10.0.1026.32716)
- Windows Error Reporting: `APPCRASH`, P1 `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`, exception `0xc0000005`

## Crash timeline (Windows Application event log, .NET Runtime 1026 + Application Error 1000)

| Time (local, +08:00) | First stack frame |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-14 19:18 | `V1Protocol.Descriptor.OneWayPropEntry\`3.Mount` |
| 2026-08-14 19:19 | `V1Protocol.Descriptor.OneWayPropEntry\`3.Mount` |
| 2026-08-14 19:49 | `V1Protocol.Descriptor.OneWayPropEntry\`3.Mount` |
| 2026-08-14 19:55 | `V1Protocol.Descriptor.OneWayPropEntry\`3.Mount` |
| 2026-08-14 19:56 | `V1Protocol.Descriptor.OneWayPropEntry\`3.Mount` |
| 2026-08-14 19:58 | `V1Protocol.Descriptor.OneWayPropEntry\`3.Mount` |
| 2026-08-18 02:16 | `RichTextBlockElement+<>c.<.cctor>b__109_22` |
| 2026-08-18 11:11 | `RichTextBlockElement+<>c.<.cctor>b__109_22` |

Notes:

- Companion installed 2026-08-14 ~16:44. Six crashes within **40 minutes** that evening (19:18 → 19:58) = crash / auto-restart loop (RestartAgent.exe restarts the tray after each crash).
- The 2026-08-18 02:16 crash happened while unattended, suggesting the bug can be triggered by background rendering, not only explicit UI actions.
- All 8 crashes share the same exception code and the same subsystem (`Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core`); the two stack paths differ only in which Reactor element is being mounted.

## Stack traces

### Path A (6 crashes): OneWayPropEntry.Mount

```
at Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor.OneWayPropEntry`3[[System.__Canon,...],[System.__Canon,...],[System.Boolean,...]].Mount(System.__Canon, System.__Canon)
at Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor.DescriptorHandler`2[...,...].Mount(Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.MountContext, System.__Canon)
at Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.Reconciler.Mount(Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.Element, System.Action)
at Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.V1HandlerAdapter`2[...,...].DispatchChildrenMount(...)
... (repeated DispatchChildrenMount/Mount frames) ...
```

### Path B (2 crashes): RichTextBlockElement

```
at Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.RichTextBlockElement+<>c.<.cctor>b__109_22(Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichTextBlock, Boolean)
at Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor.DescriptorHandler`2[...,...].Mount(...)
at Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.Reconciler.Mount(...)
... (repeated DispatchChildrenMount/Mount frames) ...
at Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Handlers.ExpanderHandler.Mount(...)
...
at Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.Start(Microsoft.UI.Xaml.ApplicationInitializationCallback)
at OpenClawTray.Program.Main(System.String[])
```

Path B shows the mount tree includes an **ExpanderHandler** whose children contain a **RichTextBlock** — the crash occurs while the Reactor mounts that element (unhandled exception in the static cctor lambda, then the process is terminated by the runtime).

## Expected behavior

The tray app should not crash when rendering expandable/rich-text items, and should not enter a crash-restart loop.

## Actual behavior

Unhandled exception → process terminated; RestartAgent restarts it; crash repeats (observed up to 6 times in 40 minutes). The gateway is not affected.

## Workaround (user-side)

Disable the tray app's startup entry (`HKCU\...\Run` `OpenClawTray`) and use the browser Control UI instead. This avoids the crash loop but does not fix the underlying rendering bug.

## Repro hints

- Triggering seems to involve rendering an `Expander` containing rich text (e.g., a message/notification list item). Exact user action unknown; the unattended 02:16 crash suggests it can fire from background updates too.
- Happy to run any debug build / capture more traces (e.g., WER dump) if useful.

body:
## Summary

OpenClaw Companion v2026.7.1 can become unresponsive when switching to a session whose history load returns approximately 200 messages. The gateway remains healthy while the native WinUI stops updating, and Windows records `AppHangB1`.

This appears related to synchronous history projection/snapshot rendering, but is distinct from the per-event streaming flood tracked in #1150 and its candidate fix #1158.

## Environment

- OpenClaw Companion: v2026.7.1
- Release commit: `4206611f2b2e47cd575e1c8aa94e3e7708f6dd96`
- Windows desktop client: `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`

## Reproduction

1. Have a session with enough history for the Companion to load the approximately 200-message history window.
2. Switch from another session to that session.
3. Wait while the history response is projected and the resulting snapshot is rendered.

Reproduced on 2026-08-16 around 12:04 local time.

## Actual behavior

- The native WinUI becomes unresponsive or stops visually updating.
- Windows records `AppHangB1`.
- Gateway health remains OK during the UI hang.

## Expected behavior

Switching sessions and loading the bounded history window should remain responsive, including for histories containing many agent/tool events.

## Exact-release source path

In the v2026.7.1 source, `OpenClawChatDataProvider` folds the loaded history (up to 200 messages) into timeline state and publishes the resulting snapshot. The `Changed` handler in `OpenClawReactorChatRoot` then calls `setSnapshot(args.Snapshot)`, triggering the native WinUI/React render.

Even though this is one publication rather than the per-event publication storm in #1150, projecting and synchronously rendering a large snapshot immediately after a session switch can saturate the UI thread.

Relevant source:

- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/OpenClawChatDataProvider.cs`
- the `OpenClawReactorChatRoot` snapshot `Changed` handler

## Why this is not a duplicate of existing reports

- #1150 is the canonical report for UI saturation under a high-rate live agent-event stream. Draft PR #1158 bounds/coalesces those per-event paths, but does not appear to batch the initial history projection/render during a session switch.
- #860 was closed by merged PR #898, which virtualized chat timeline rows. That merge is already an ancestor of v2026.7.1, so this hang reproduced with row virtualization present.

## Suggested fix/validation area

- Batch or incrementally project history where practical.
- Avoid a large synchronous full-timeline render on the UI thread after session selection.
- Add a current-head WinUI responsiveness test that switches into a session with 200 varied history messages, including dense agent/tool entries.
- Preserve scroll restoration, selection, and terminal event state while batching.

## Crash scope

There was also one separate 2026-08-13 crash involving `CoreMessagingXP.dll`. There is not enough evidence to attribute that crash to this history-load hang, so this report is limited to the recurring AppHang/UI-saturation behavior.
